text: It's always a good time, but I don't see why anyone schedules events for the summer with this being open air. At least you can bring in food now, but drinks are really what you need.

name: Gigi Katz
text: I always have a great time when I go to a concert here, great atmosphere, beautiful lawn, and wonderful concerts! Totally recommend for anyone wanting to have a good time at a concert!

name: Mary Hopkins
text: The concert was very good really enjoyed it the only thing that I didn't like was the lawn seating

name: Melissa Alexander
text: The facilities- nice. Fact that their rules about 8.5×11 are not enforced, not cool. Why can people bring in pizza boxes but they would not allow my small carrier with food in it which fit within the measurements posted?

name: Suzanne Driskill
text: We went to see Trevor Noah in concert and there were only 2 entrances available. There were about 20 available, but they had 2 open. It was completely ridiculous. I won't go again.

name: Roselia Labbe
text: Every seat is a good seat, to include the lawn seats. The fixed bathroom facilities are well kept. There was an attendant throughout the show making sure every stall was stocked and clean. Plenty of concession stands. Lots of nearby parking. I always enjoy coming here.

name: Brooke Hubbell
text: We had a great time at the concert!! Very fun and great customer service at the concession stand. The food came out hot and fresh. I was impressed with the Papa John's Pizza. It was very good. We will be back!

name: Thaddeus Fine
text: Always fun. Lots of people there by 7 pm tough to get good lawn seat.

name: Maestro Maestro
text: The venue itself is fine - although it makes you wonder why somebody thought it was a good idea to put it in the middle of a very busy "town", with limited infrastructure.   So, when you couple that with an oversold event, it makes for a very frustrating evening, logistically speaking.   They also don't seem to care about smoking - whether legal or illegal substances. I guess what I'm saying, come for the classical music events - the crowds will be smaller and better behaved.

name: natalie macias
text: So much fun. First concert in a long time.

name: V LP
text: As expected, the area was out in the open.   Even though it rained the concert was not cancelled.   Suggestion is to wear comfortable shoes for the walk and lawn.   Bring plenty of money and spring for the chairs or just pay extra to be in front   Other than a handful of people being rude we had fun.

name: Alejandra Marina
text: This is where my brothers 2019 graduation was held. It was so nice. packed with a lot of ppl. It was a little hot but it was definitely worth it 👍

name: Stacy Ingram
text: The pavilion is a great place to spend an evening out - date night or family night! It is clean and fun. Great shows at reasonable prices. Eat before you go as concessions are pricey!

name: DaRealKingCoopa Vlogs
text: I love coming out here from the music and magic 102.1 under the stars come out here with friends and family really really nice place

name: Sturg S
text: Great time, great place for watching a concert. Damn concessions are outrageous in cost though!! $14-$19 for A beer (1 damn beer).

name: Jellybeans Cougfan
text: I loved the park and beautiful setting.  The seats were good for an outdoor arena.

name: Mariessa Dennis
text: Had a blast! Staff is always friendly and helpful

name: Chelsea Jenkins
text: Great security! I felt very safe. Plus there are plenty of bathrooms for women.

name: Billy Stringfield
text: This Venue is a great place to come and listen to music!  Just remember it is outdoors so keep a look out for the weather.  It was in the 80s for OneRepublic (7 pm concert) and it felt great!

name: Brittney Summerville
text:
Eat before you go!! 5 stars other than the cost of EVERYTHING... $7 for a small bottle of water... If you do eat there, get the "For two Sampler" - it cost $15 but it was the only thing actually worth $15... So much food - it was like a giant chili cheese fries with chicken tenders added in; also the beers START at $15 a piece.

The acoustics of the Pavilion can't be beat. I wish everyone would come here instead of the other arenas in Houston, I can dream right!

name: Katherine Hoskins
text: We saw the Smashing Pumpkins Sunday and it was great!! I will say....the fries in the concession are awful cardboard. But I dont have to eat fries when I'm there and the sound is always great at the pavilion. Well done!

name: brenda flowers
text:
I love this place
The people makes everything convenient and well organized...but those $5.00 water and soda

name: Eric
text: Wife purchased lawn seats for my son and I, lady walked up and put us up close and personal for my sons first concert.  Great time.

name: Cheryl James
text: I love this venue. Never a bad seat, big screen TVs and the sound system is Awesome!!

name: Richard Perales
text: This is a great outdoor venue but if you're coming for a festival so, be sure to bring your sunscreen.

name: Amber Justice
text: I've always loved this pavilion and the events that happen here. Normally pricing is affordable to the events. The concession prices are absolutely outrageous. 35$ for 4 bottles of water and a corn dog. $67.50 for 4 sodas and 4 chicken tender with waffle fries. I have beautiful memories that will last a lifetime at The Pavilion now for myself and my family. Excellent bathrooms, could use more than one baby changing area in them. Had a hard time with the stroller and all the steps. They most likely have ramps to each elevated section but there was so much to see at the Children's Festival, we were too impatient to find them. 🤣

name: Greg Davis
text: Great nice setup just can't stop the Houston rain to stay dry but my son and his mom had a great time...

name: Cindy Frost
text: Concerts here are always amazing, VIP parking so convenient. Very pricey drinks. Get there earlier for a better view on the hill.

name: Jerry Greengold
text: Simple awesome. Great facility. Great show. Easy parking. Highly recommed!

name: chris tennes
text: Loved this venue! Good sound. Easy to get to seats and stuff.  Lots of vendors. Really cool structure.

name: Kathy Meyer
text: The Pavilion is a very clean and well-managed outdoor venue.  There are several free parking lots staffed with Pavilion staff and paved paths to get to the venue.  If there is an artist you would like to attend a concert, the The Pavilion is a great place.  Several concession stands are available.

name: Eddy Arnold
text: Great staff. If you have a seat reserved, you are under the canopy... if you are on the lawn, all bets are off for seats and location. Most reserved seats have a decent view of the stage. Biggest thing that gets people is what you can bring in... just read the posted signs but it can change per concert (based on what the performer wants).

name: Veronica S. Dixon
text: Always a great place to see a show

name: C S L
text: Great venue w/ excellent service, Ms. Jo really  has her ushers on top of everything...

name: Andrea D. Knupple
text: Enjoyed the Casting Crowns and Kari Jobe concert with my son, blessed experience praising the Lord Jesus 🥰

name: Kenny Mansfield
text: Wonderful small, open-air venue to see major names in concert. Excellent seats no matter what you sit.

name: Carlos Tijerina
text: Kari Jobe was awesome. The pavilion was a very nice outdoors with a good covering. Great food a bit pricey like minute maid park. But they have this nice river walk there very ideal for a first date. Would definitely go again for other events or to see kari jobe again

name: Jennifer Triplett
text: Park at the woodlands mall to save the $20 event parking fee. Dont bring a big purse or they wont let you in. Drinks and food are mediocre and expensive.(and when you do buy a bottle of water, prepare for them to take your cap so you cant even carry the thing without spilling it) But, other than that, concerts here are good- HOT, but good.

name: Viva Golden
text: CWP is the only venue where i will attend a concert. Never overwhelming and it is just a beautiful place to spend and evening! Love it!

name: Paris Jackson
text: Good experiences at the Pavilion, though I would definitely recommend eating at a nearby restaurant instead because of pricing. But, the occasional free lawn concerts & exceptional concert lineups are cool.

name: Cajun Smoker
text: One if the best venues in the nation. Sound is great. It's well run. Plenty of concessions....don't have to miss 3 or 4 songs just to grab a cold beer. Love the Pavillion!

name: crystal larson
text: My favorite venue for big shows, never had a bad time here!

name: Debbie Barron
text: Always love this place location in the woods makes it feel very secluded great shows great artists i visit regularly

name: Tony King
text: ZZ Top concert was fantastic and so much fun with great sounds and environment is perfect for us! Young, old, disabled and the food was fresh! Not too happy with bottled water, they take your water bottle tops and that is pure sillyness on their part. Great time was had by all!

name: damion kirkpatrick
text: Always a great place for concerts. Nice open lawn seating and a great area for most pits due to the amount of room.

name: Rob Schnell
text: Restrooms were very clean and we'll maintained throughout the entire event. The food service staff worked efficiently and lined moved quickly. The security was reasonable. Only issue was shutting down concessions because lightning was in the area. Went from feeling like a guest to a prisoner rather quickly in the heat with no beverage service available. Overall good venue for shoes.

name: Justin Grimm
text: Crank up those fans, it's hot. Purse restrictions are annoying, luckily I convinced my wife she didn't want to hang on to hers before we made the four block walk to where others were being turned away. Little mad I had to pay to take off my belt and be treated like a criminal... Good selection of snacks and booze though... Security theater ensures I won't be back.

name: Justin Jones
text:
It felt great to get ripped off 30$ for 2 modelo 24 oz in the can. So 65
$ ripped off after paying for tickets made us feel great. This place is just as what you would expect kiddies!

name: Tracy Childers
text: I like going to concerts here very convenient. Friendly staff. Need more drinks options.

name: Pernia Rutherford
text: It's a pretty neat experience from the lawn

name: Alex Lima
text: Acustics is amazing, great venue

name: Lori Lemire
text: The concert we attended was awesome. The facilities, on the other hand, didn't leave me feeling the same. We had great seats in section 107, row c. We had a great view of the stage.  But there's a but.  We were 3 rows back from a sewer manhole cover. And there were times where our noses were VERY aware that we were close to a sewer access point.  Now, my question is...why?  Why would you put a sewer manhole cover in the middle of a pavilion?  Poor planning, at best. It is sad to me that I have to give less than 5 stars because of something that is so ridiculous.  That just shouldn't have even been a problem.  Otherwise, everything was great. Except for staff who seemed to like to accumulate in the walkway directly in front of us to discuss things periodically. Then we were bobbing around trying to see around them.

name: Jennifer R Gunner
text: Beautiful outdoor venue that is well maintained!  If you can swing it, get tix on the first 4 rows center stage.  There is air conditioning that blows down from the stage.

name: tanya langner
text: To get free parking, arrive early to your event. There is street and mall parking available. A large can of Karbach was $17, which I felt the need to share so you come prepared.

name: Richard Waits
text: Always a good time here. Clean facilities and friendly atmosphere!

name: Mary Trujillo
text: Parking was confusing. The line to rent the lawn chairs was a mess. The concert itself was fine. But the experience could be improved.

name: Lauri D. Bridgen
text:
Bob Seger concert, Thursday May 2... where do I start...? Hard to review this place when there were so many issues they could not control, so this review is to possibly help future issue from happening.
Yes, the rain was terrible and the concert was delayed over 2-1/2 hours. That’s not even part of this review.
1) Upon arriving, before the rain even started, there were two lines funneling into the pavilion. No one knew which line was for which seats (covered or lawn); not even the 2 gentlemen wearing blue “Cynthia Woods Pavilion” collared shirts. When my friend and I directly asked one of the men which line was for what, the man actually replied, “this is the line to get in for the concert”. Pretty obvious. Then when we asked for a more clear direction, the man said he did not know. As an employee, they should have known.
2) The beer lines inside ‘The Lounge’ were exceptionally long (literally took 42 minutes to get one round of beers on just one of our visits to the bar). This is understandable as there was nothing to do but drink while we waited for the rain to subside. My complaint is the way it was handled. The line would not have been so long had the bartenders not continued to let people cut in line. It was ridiculous!
People pay good money and drive a long way for this entertainment. Get some procedures set. You will lose customers.

name: Disabled Dave
text: It's easy to see from the street. Parking is good but you have to walk a block or two be careful not to park in a place that says do not park. It is clean but it is open when you go through the main gate so you could get wet or be in the Sun. Most of the seats are under a big cover. The Sounds sounds good and it's easy to see the performers. Just one block away are plenty sidewalk cafes on Waterway Avenue a great place to eat before or after a concert. Market Street is closed and there is lots of shopping there before the concert. Hotels nearby are the Hyatt on Market Street or the Marriott or the West they're all very nice and have nice views. It is on the Waterway and it's nice to walk along the water before or after the concert it's very safe. They are a bit picky as to what you can bring into the concert of course no food and drinks. They do have food and drinks available at the concert for a higher price. It was my second time here and I will be back again I highly recommend this to anyone.

name: Kenneth Reddick
text: Great place for music. But hot with the crowd. The over head fans were kept on slow speed??   But ok.

name: David Ramos
text: There is not a single bad seat in the house which is awesome!  The sound is great and their screens are just as good!  One star was deducted because their concession lines take anl really long time, and their purse policy needs to be posted. Luckily we read the email, but as of this review, they have a VERY strict 8.5" x 11" purse/bag policy. Even a quarter inch more and you have to take it back. Otherwise, great venue. Would recommend!

name: Ike Maxwell
text: Maze KEM. WAS AWESOME CONCERT MAJIC 102 MANE

name: steve jackson
text: Easy in and out, but must be under cover if the weather is wet.

name: Ethan Faulkner
text: My very first time here and enjoying a amazing concert seeing Frankie Beverly and Maze

name: Tequila Goodwill
text: Great experience Parking was so easy I love this venue

name: Sam Tyer
text: Great venue! Great set up! One of the best!

name: Douglas Roberson
text: Nice place i ride bikes in the area so it was a great time as usual

name: Edlin Chavez
text: I love hanging out at the lawn. You can bring a blanket to sit

name: journei antonidas
text: As long as the weather is good it's  a great venue.  I try to get the covered seating just in case.  On warm Texas days it could use more air flow.  Shows have to end by a certain time so to the surrounding neighborhoods.

name: Alvaro Rey
text: Is a nice place, parking is very convenient and close to the place and mostly free. Summer in Texas can be brutal so outdoors venues can get hot as hell

name: Gerry Barillas
text: The Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavilion is an awesome open venue for concerts, music or art in general. Any seat is a great seat so don't worry too much about how close you are to the stage. The sound is crisp and clear. Also the are its in is so amazing and brearhtaking. I have been here multiple times and it is always extremely enjoyable and memorable!!!

name: Linda Wilson
text: Buzzfest! Had a blast! Godsmack and Bush!

name: Top Shelf
text: Isnt a bad seat in the house and free parking like every place should be! How they keep that grass so clean and green is truly a mystery

name: james wood
text: Free parking is a little bit of a walk but you can save $20 the drinks are over priced.. very easy to get in and out of bathrooms, they do have food that's as reasonable as can be expected for a concert. All in all I have enjoyed all my experiences here and will gladly go back, the lawn is a great option for large groups of friends. Hope this helps someone, if so give me a like 😉

name: C Ellis
text: Beautiful venue! Boston Pops was amazing! I love the free seats at some of the concerts on the lawn and sometimes mezzanine seats.

name: Drew Nabi
text: Nice big tents with outdoor events! :)

name: Naomi Faz
text:
All the staff from the gate people, merchandise sellers to the concession stands were nice. They didn't rush you and were very patient.
The venue is great for intimate shows. Saw the Imagine Dragons and we had lawn seats. Don't think I'll do lawn seats again. My fault for waiting too late for tickets. You can rent seats for $7, which was cool. But maneuvering thru those seats and blankets spread out on the ground can be tricky.

name: Jason Lynn
text: Always liked this place. It's pricey as hell but you will have a good time for sure.

name: Alfonso
text: Great place for an outdoor concert. People are friendly. Just be careful when the concert is in July or August

name: Chibuzo Elonu
text:
I think this venue is astonishing.
Essentially it's all outdoor but there is covered seating. I went to a concert to see Chris Brown. The weather started off hot! I had seats under the cover but that doesn't stop the heat from surrounding you. I would STRONGLY RECOMMEND covered seating. They have lawn seating but it's first come first serve.
Parking is interesting. The Venue is surrounded by the Woodland Mall so it shares it's parking with that.
There facilities are clean and plentiful and easily accessible.
It a great place to watch a concert or event, but stay hydrated and look for covered seating!

name: Luis Elgueta
text: Great place, if you want to go for the cheap tickets you are in the lawn area quality of sound tends to drop there but hey it is cheaper, now if you want assigned sits then it is great sound all around.

name: Madalina Surdea
text: I went for “game of thrones” concert , the sound system was amazing !

name: FilthSquad Games
text: This is the BEST concert venue in Houston and surrounding areas! Tons of space, awesome concert listings, and they donate alot of the profits to musical programs in surrounsing schools, which i feel is a very important aspect of education. If you've never been i definately recommend going to a concert sometime!

name: Alexa B
text: Always a good time. Good layout for nearly complete visibility. Fair selection of drinks from multiple locations including frozen daiquiri. If you don't care for the hike around the lake and through the woods there is paid event parking on the edge of the mall. You'll see signs if you drive around. Still a minor hike. And possibly crossing one or two roads.

name: Nacole Hicks
text: Nice venue! Needed more air circulation, but otherwise a comfortable atmosphere. No bad seats!

name: Jade Barao
text: I used to work here, and been here for a couple of events including my brothers graduation. Best job I’ve had, wish I can go back. And the events held here are so much fun! Always bringing down great artists.

name: Ray Evans
text: Great venue... Parking is decent... Pricing runs par for the area.

name: Tif Simmons-O'Shields
text: Venue is what it is: outside, pricey drinks (water also not just alcohol), cannot see the band too well from the lawn, the sound normally is good, PIT tickets are rare and expensive , and the weather in the area is typically not the best for any type of outside show. The staff is good I must say never had anything but good views on the people working the venue. Parking can be a little of a maze the first few times but eventually just like everyone else you find your spot

name: Jennifer Hernandez
text: My first time visiting the Cynthia Woods Mitchell pavilion on Good Friday. So beautiful and a pleasant experience. Clean and friendly atmosphere.

name: Nikki Hough
text: Saw Alice and Chains and Korn here! Amazing venue! Drinks are over priced but overall had a blast at this place.

name: E W
text:
Wonderfully easy venue. All of the security and concession staff we encountered were super friendly too.

There was one woman who stopped my friend from coming in because her small, clear bag was "too big" even though it was a replica of what was on the "Allowed" sign behind us, but security at the gate checked it and said it was fine.  So, don't let the people wandering around outside the gates stop you. That was the only hassle.

name: slick ks
text: Great place for concerts. Expensive for concessions. 1 beer 1 water $21 bucks ridiculous oh and you cant keep ur water bottle cap they claim its because of the artist not wanting ppl to throw them? Seems like you can throw a bottle just as easy.

name: kory woodside
text: The Jimmy Buffet concert was great. But there rent a cops need to learn to how to talk to people. Just standing there waiting for a friend,  was hold 3 beers, 1 for my wife, me and brother. When she came up and harassed me about it. No signs, or anything saying cant carry more than 2 drinks.  They sold me 3, but yet shes telling me i need to throw 1 away.

name: Vajih Khan
text: Great venue, especially in the summer, wish they would bring more bands to the location. Wonderful to place to walk around.

name: Ivy Eakins
text: Went for a concert. We had lawn tickets. It was clean and spacious.

name: gillian metz
text: Amazing open air arena but should stop people from using phones 10 min after concert starts

name: Ginnetta Joseph
text: It was great just bring an blanket if you get tickets for the lawn. Else u can rent an chair from them.

name: Alfonso Cruz
text: Great venue fir concerts. Just get there early to get good parking and dinner.

name: Charlie Skiman
text: You can always see the stage, good sound system, always a slave to the elements, too darn hot & humid!

name: Cee
text: Great venue,  show up early to avoid long entry waits. Other then that,the sound is  great in the seats or on  the lawn.

name: Robert Hernandez
text: Great venue.... Bathroom lines long... Beer $13.00 a pop. Overall I had a great time!

name: Vee V
text: I’m always on the lawn bc it is a way more fun crowd! If you want a coveted seat, you’ll pay for it, but worth it if you want to chill and be closer to the artist. In the lawn our whole family was able to sit on blankets and low chairs and stand and dance also! Great combo!

name: toni chidester
text: I loved the venue and concert but there was no visible signage the way I walked to the venue about the purse size check. I had walked from the blue lot and had to walk all the way back to my car. I only saw the sign about the purse size when I decided to take a different path to the venue.

name: Craig Peltier
text: I love this place.  I don't love the concession prices though.  $11 beers and $9 hot dogs Is why I gave a 4 star.  Otherwise, I have no problem driving 50 miles from Clear Lake.  I can always take the Hardy Toll Road for concerts that start at 7 on a rush hour work night.  And I don't mind the long walk.  I always park on the backside lot and I enjoy the scenery.  The sound Is usually pretty good and the environment makes me feel like I'm at a Fairgrounds.  And It doesn't take forever to get on the freeway when I leave.  Always a good time.  😃

name: Nedra Bell
text: I'm loving this venue, concert are awesome. You can view the stage from wherever you sit..

name: Christopher Lawrence
text: Awesome place! Great concert experience, awesome food and plenty to drink. If you havent been then you have to get out and try it out.

name: joanna hollimam
text: We went to see the ZZ Top 50th Anniversary Bash. The Pavilion was amazing! Great seating, plenty of leg room. Security was faster that expected. See happy we could take in our snacks!

name: Genesis
text: Super great but would gladly appreciate it if the the check in people wouldn't be so harsh..

name: Steve Peters
text: Always have great shows and I always run into friends and old familiar faces.

name: Jennifer Jones
text: Fantastic venue! We have a great time every-time we go here. Tip: A lot of times if you buy grass seats and then go rent a chair you’ll find they’ll upgrade your tickets for free. Obviously this usually only happens on shows that did not fill up the seats.

name: TYLER HEBERT
text: I've seen two concerts here and enjoyed each one. This is such a nice place.

name: Kendra Friscia
text: Great concert venue..good lawn seating...been twice,great times!...food selection is lacking for vegetarians.

name: Jeri Sullivan
text: Peter Frampton Farewell Concert was amazing! What a great memory for years to come!

name: Cyndi Brown
text:
Great venue... most of the time.

It would be helpful if there was more clarity on all the changing rules on what can be taken in to which events,  which tickets can be used on mobile apps versus having to have printed forms, and if they would turn up the fan speed in the summer (it gets hot in there!!)

We normally get lawn seats for most events which means it's taking a chance on bad weather. It would be nice, when the ground is super muddy, if they would provide the rental chairs for free (or let us bring our own), as it can be hard to find a spot to stand or use blankets.

Overall though, very happy to have it so close by.

name: Paula Martinez
text: Saw Bonham and Frampton. Awesome concert. Cynthia Woods is always a great time!!

name: William H. Carver
text:
Parking is mediocre at best and one had better arrive no less than 2 hours prior or you’ll be hiking from your spot to the venue and back afterwards. Vendor prices are astronomical and alcohol vendors selling a single person more than one cocktail is strictly enforced. This is fine, unless one wants to purchase a bottle of wine, in which case one must be escorted by another in your party or you’ll not be purchasing a bottle for your party. Chairs for lawn seating are available for rent at $7 each and are child size.

The sound is better than typical amphitheater’s. And lawn tickets are typically just $25, which makes up for the overpriced vendors.

name: Jada Brielle
text: Beautiful outside arena. Went to see my first rock concert and saw 30 Seconds to Mars live in concert with Walk the Moon as an opening act, who was equally amazing. An amazing, wonderful once in a lifetime experience.

name: Hannah Jauregui
text:
I was told by teenage staff members that my small clear backpack was not allowed inside, so I walked back to my car to drop it off, only to find out that it would’ve been permitted. Please get all of your staff members on the same page. Also a real turn off by the $17.00 prices for a single beer and $5.00 for a bottle of water
Will never come back to this venue

name: Shannon Barnes Laws
text: What an amazing theatre. It's breezy a day on the water. Well worth what you paid in tickets,

name: Pamela GREEN
text: I went there for the first time for a concert. Had a great time, beautiful place!

name: Edward Davalos
text: The Cynthia Woods Pavilion always has the Best Concert Shows and at a Ticket Price on anyone's Budget. So, you get an Awesome Concert Show at a Great Price with an Fantastic View with an Amazing Staff to take care of your every need with a Smile, always. And Tons of Free Parking.

name: Alex Villasenor
text: Great venue, the lawn area is amazing foe watching concerns and very economic. They have lots of events all year.  Parking could be problematic during large events.

name: Ryan Wachtstetter
text: Nice venue for a concert. Parking during peak concert going time was an issue, but once on site it was easy to get around

name: Jessi Kopp
text: One of my favorite Houston music venues for larger shows

name: Bill Everts
text: The Third Day Farewell tour concert was awesome.

name: Raul Rios
text: As usual the star spangled salute was spectacular with the Houston Symphony performing American classics, band music, Aretha and Gladys Knight songs, and obviously Tchaikovsky's 1812 overture with cannons at the end.

name: Brad Iund
text: Saw Casting Crowns #castingcrowns, Kari Jobe, Cody Carnes and Jamie Kimmett last night! Great concert! It was the first time my wife and I have been there and it is awesome! No parking fees, some say food prices are expensive but when have you ever been to an event and prices were normal? The place is great and the surrounding area is awesome! We will definitely be back, not only for a concert/event but just to walk around the river and waterfalls!  Also the ticket prices are very reasonable!

name: Nelson DeHass
text: An absolute beautiful venue for a concert, its a huge architectural wonder of a pavilion.  However,  its not so big that you feel lost in the crowd, which also provides a more welcoming feel. If your into just going to a place then leaving, your missing out here. The engineering feat that was accomplished to build this structure is an eye pleasing brain boggler. There is free parking, and the stroll from the parking areas to the pavilion is a nice one. Paved paths take you thru wooded areas, next to the paddle boat house, across the spillway, and into the park. A enjoyable walk during the day, and a romantic lite treat for the eyes at night.  Definitely the Best location and Venue I've  been to in my 40 years of concert goings.  Good Fun, Good People, Good concessions. The only, oh no, I came across here, is the Beer Prices $$$. It takes a roll of $20s to get drunk here. (Which might explaine the lack of totally inebriated people. If that's the reason for the high beer prices.. it's a totally smart move, because it works.)

name: Kimberly stafford
text: Whether I go alone or with friends, I always have a great time here!!

name: Timothy Van Cloud
text: Awesomeriffic Environment,  Very Organized, On Our 1st Visit We Had A Wonderful Time!

name: Alejandro Villalobos jr
text: 5 Stars just because it's the second time I get to see Slipknot here

name: carpecasei
text: Great Place to see a concert.  Friendly venue, nice seats and a great lawn.  Varied food options and adult beverages available.  Many restaurants and bars nearby as well as several nice hotels in walking distance.

name: Logan Starker
text: Absolutely loved watching ZZ Top perform. Even though it rained it was still a lot of fun. The area under the tent was a bit loud but the grass area was the perfect volume.

name: shan elliot
text: Great bands and close to home. Sucks in the summer though. So hot.

name: Jamie A
text:
I love attending concerts at the Pavilion! They've added TV screens in the plaza and at the concession stands so you don't miss anything if you have to grab a snack. Drink prices are high and margaritas are wine based. Of course I am there to enjoy the music, not get wasted so it doesn't matter to me. Food is also overpriced, but they are trying to add some healthy alternatives like sweet potato fries and portabella mushroom burgers.  I typically enjoy dinner and drinks at one of the many restaurants within walking distance to avoid drinking and eating here anyway.

Many people enjoy the lawn, however I do not. Too many people sandwiched together and then you end up standing the entire time. Also, no protection from the unpredictable Texas weather. The covered seating is great! Nice big fans overhead. Large screens on both sides of the stage. I have pretty much sat in every section including obstructed view and there's not really a bad seat.

name: Kathryn Hagerty
text: Great venue! Excellent view from the seats. Good selection of beers outside.

name: Images Inc
text: Nice venue but it was hot! They need to turn those fans on up top for those of us who bought lower level seats instead  of letting them circulate slowly!

name: Rika Linxwiler
text: Horrible experience! The ground was saturated and the attendees wouldn't allow blankets for the lawn seating, also they were not providing lawn chairs for rental. The seating availability was great, but we had to purchase seating and blankets as well! Never visiting again after paying over $800 for tickets for my family and I!

name: Cynthia Zelaya
text: Every seat offers excellent visibility, and the lawn is great for the price and value. Bring your own meal! Can't bring drinks but concessions sells them at $5. Pricey, but not the end of the world, especially compared to some stadiums.

name: Andrew Lopez
text: Wow had a blast!  Like all shows expect to have a reasonable amount of cash, but they have card readers and for the amount of people the lines seemed to flow quickly!

name: The Shepherd Mix Food Bar
text: Harder to get into than a flight, but, unlike an airport, a safe, comfortable and entertaining experience.

name: Bobby & Michelle Stephens
text: This place is great for concerts. Everyone can afford a seat somewhere here.  Either the lawn or seats.  Great drinks,  clean restrooms and food. Never a disappointment when we come here.

name: Lynsey Sawyer
text: Tons of places to get food, very clean bathrooms, great layout and seating was easy to find. I'd suggest going to events in cooler months or at night if possible.

name: Dee walls
text: Loved it , not a bad view on the lawn,  great sound, no mosquito, no ants and no one was in no ones way.

name: Mars Crew & Others
text: I was expecting to see  Hocus Pocus, but I don't think there was anything even Hocus Pocus related, except the sign to take a pic behind. Also, my son (2yr, near 3) didn't get to really do anything because by the time we got through the ridiculous line it was almost time for the show to start! They made me pour out mine and my sons water! They told my purse was too big! They also told me I would have to check my wagon. I was not happy!! Does not mean I'll never go back, but it's not an airport I think all of that was very ridiculous!!

name: Heidi Arroyo
text: Had an amazing experience with my kiddos. Definitely plan to return for future events.

name: Mark Renza
text: It was great , easy access to parking and we were upgraded on our ticket!

name: Christopher Townsend
text: Best open air live venue in Houston metroplex

name: Kimberly W
text: Great sound on the lawn.  My only complaint is the lack of lighting on the way to the parking lots and the lack of lighting on the streets.  It gets so dark out there.

name: Linda Ball
text: Beautiful outdoor performing arts center with a large section of reserved seating,  handicap seating, free mezzanine seating and sloped grass seating (not covered) for community events.  They also have weekly national headline acts. Seating Area is under  large circus tent tops with large comfortable fans.

name: Jackson Valencia
text: The best open air concert venue I have visited. Remember to dress like you will be outside, potentially including sunglasses. If you’re sitting on the lawn, chairs are unnecessary for many concerts because almost everyone will stand.

name: Daniel Hentschel
text: This place is a great concept for a concert venue. It features a covered amphitheater with seats and a pit area. However, I don't recommend buying lawn tickets during the summer. Not too many people can stand to sit under a 100+ degree sun with no shade for hours. Bring something to block the sun, or you will fry like an egg, or just buy seats under the covered area.

name: Cristina Herrera
text: Amazing venue! Been to many concerts here for the last 24 years or so of my life. Great acoustics, lots of seating, even sitting on the lawn is a great option here. They have done great with the upkeep, staying ontop of concessions, keeping good staff, and hosting great events.

name: Mara Belmont
text: Good place for an open air  concert...a good amount of staff to assist people...lines move fairly quick...

name: Betsy M
text: Too damn EXPENSIVE!!!! They want $5.00 for a 16.9 oz. bottle of water.  $13.50 for a beer,. Prices are getting outrageous there. The last time we were there for the Alice in Chains concert, there were no chairs on the lawn. People who have back problems should be able to sit down in a chair, not on the ground.  🤬🤬🤬 It's difficult to get up.

name: Bob Wilson
text: Great venue. Acoustics are wonderful. No vision obstructions to either the stage or the 2 screens. Beware of going to events in the Houston summer-it's hot under the tent. Fans help a little.

name: Irvin Johnson
text: Man my lady and I had a great time at the recently heal concert

name: mario saenz
text: I didn't expect this venue to be so cozy. Other than the Texas heat and humidity. This place is great! It's just big enough for the amount of people there, they've put plenty of restrooms and bars all over..... also I imagine any seat is a good seat here... although I like to sit towards the center no matter what.

name: William Graves
text: What a great little ice rink. The keep the surface smooth and had two safety personnel there while I was there with kids. $12/2hours. Good stuff.

name: Starlet Reed
text: Excellent Place for Concert...U can sit on the lawn or under the pavilion...Also a club with A/C ...Great music to enjoy...Great Drinks

name: Tracy Mishler
text: Been many times, never had a bad experience. Friendly staff, clean bathrooms and better food and drink options than in past years.

name: Akshat Gupta
text: It's a great venue. There are free parking options. You're allowed to bring your own food. I haven't sat in the lawn yet.

name: Naomi Gentry
text: One of my favorite places for concerts!! I love the music and you are in sync chanting and dancing at unison with so many people! You can LITERALLY feel the ENERGY in the air when you are at this place!

name: Ashley Alexander
text: There were security measures for the lightning advisory and the venue kept everyone informed and safe and the tour still happened.

name: Carolyn Parker
text: Great Venue and the music always sounds great here.  We were is section 108 row G and could not have asked for a better location!

name: Chelsea Huett
text: Got lawn tickets to see Halestorm and Alice cooper. Well the lawn was closed due to crowd control so got really good upgraded tickets.

name: Lyrae Morgan
text: Torchy's is a great addition to the food selection. Now they need to add Frozen Pina Coladas!

name: Ron Benjamin
text: Nice childrens programs available at a reasonable gate price.

name: Nik Murphy
text: Despite the outrageous booking fee this was one hell of a venue. Would highly recommend lawn seating for that change of atmosphere at a big gig. Very easy to find but not so easy to park at.

name: Nancy Fletcher
text: AWESOME!! Went to see Bob Seger with my daughter..

name: Kim W
text: Love it went to a concert there and I had lots of fun. So organized.

name: Nick Bogucki
text: Definitely a great place for great music. The Waterway nearby is a good place for a jog, a walk with friends and family or just a nightly stroll. The trolley drive on the waterway a few times a week (for free) and has multiple stops. Also, if you play Pokemon Go there are a ton of pokestops here.

name: Jason
text: Having attended multiple concerts from different genres this venue is only okay, the hill or lawn is cool for cheap tickets and chilling in the sun, if you get a lawn ticket try and bring a beach towel or portable chair because the grass tends to get muddy being in Houston Texas it rains every other day, luckily theres no bug or mosquito population because the venue uses mosquitonix to fog the lawn before concerts but mud is usually a slight concern, the hill also has no bathrooms on it so you have to walk pretty far to use one (good leg workout!) The seats in the pavilion are the usual plastic stadium seats you would find at a baseball game, good leg room but I wish the acoustic were better. Overall not too bad as long as the tickets are reasonably priced or you're seeing someone important to you. There is usually food trucks or carts from local and popular restaurants, food and drinks can get really pricey here $15 for 2 bottles of water (1 litre each) and beer is usually $10 to $15 per can (tall boys). Also you can park for free at the mall and walk over to the pavillion so don't pay for parking if you don't mind the 5 minute walk.

name: Debbie Saxon
text: Good venue for music, affordable prices. Make sure you look at the seating chart carefully, there are seats with view of stage blocked.

name: Amber Hinds
text: If you’ve been here, then you know. The Woodlands pavilion is pretty much always the same. Packed hill (get there early), super expensive beer and food- but always a good time!

name: obum88
text: Great venue with food.  Limited stage viewing dependent on sit.

name: Johnny Bravo
text: This place rock go for concerts awesome

name: Michael Adair
text: Love seeing shows here! The covered seating is o.k but the lawn is where the fun is at.

name: Kevin Kocurek
text: The venue is nice and the concert was fun, and well priced. However the lines to get in were long and inefficient. And the rules about what can or cannot be brought in could be communicated more clearly.

name: Vicki Knauss
text: It was a nice outdoor space. Nice restrooms. Smooth entrance procedure. Offered chair rentals. Traffic direction was non existant and parking was unclear. No signs anywhere. Police sat on horses and would not help unless to say you can't stop to let people out there. So everyone going here, there is a reasonable pay parking lot kitty corner to the stadium if you can find it,  it was such a mess, I would recommend a car service.

name: Adam Smith
text: The Shinedown show was awesome! A special thank you to TD Industries! The CWMP took great care of us! The facilities were amazing, and they took great care of us all!

name: J M
text:
Horrible acoustics for concerts.

I was just recently at a concert and they had reverb so bad you could not understand the lyrics to the songs... And this was on the fifth row of the center section. It took them nearly half the show to get it cleared up, but this is something they should have figured out in the first place.
Like my audio production teacher used to say, "Loud does not mean a good mix."  They need to learn.

Plus the fact that this is a TicketMaster venue so the EXTRA fees are enormously out of proportion with other venues.

Just save your money for streaming subscriptions or high quality audio sources or concerts at concert hall venues.

name: Frank Marmolejos
text: Wonderful amphitheatre like venue and a great free concert by the Houston Symphony Orchestra.

name: Bigbad Bennie
text: Good place, great sound and lighting but a wee bit pricy on the concessions.

name: Joshua Jones
text: Great outdoor pavilion for concerts. Almost anywhere you sit is a great seat. Sitting on the lawn is Avery fun atmosphere.

name: Errol Hughes
text: Very warm atmosphere.  Needs more air circulation

name: cody chumley
text: Easy to find, access to parking, friendly staff. Really only complaint was the seats are very hard. Granted its outdoors mostly. I found myself having to shift in my seat every 10 minutes

name: Robert Biddison
text: Joan Jett rocked it. Heart was cool too. The lounge is nice for coolin off.

name: Tony Jones
text: Went to a free orchestra concert and movie. Nice venue but very strict when it comes to bringing bags. They say you can bring bags and food. We had an official NFL clear bag and they said it was too big. They were using a piece of notebook paper to measure the size of the bags. So if your bag is bigger than a piece of notebook paper then forget about it. If bringing food then make sure it's in it's original packaging. Also, No liquids allowed. You can bring an empty water bottle and fill it at the water fountain inside the venue. Also, they were asking kids not to play on the lawn area... I mean they are kids on a grass Hill and you expect them not to play... A little ridiculous in my opinion.

name: Allison Hernandez-Scarborough
text: Love this pavillion. Parking is close and there isn't a bad seat in the venue.

name: James West
text: Very nice place. The Bob Seger concert was great had a bit of a rain delay but it all worked out in the end.

name: Elizabeth Hill
text: Excellent acoustics.  Extra large TV screens.  Strong presence of police.  Concessions prices are high.

name: CannibalCarWash
text: Me and my friend went to go see Bush and Godsmack. The show was good

name: lisa campbell
text: Beware there are restrictions on bag sizes and types you can bring in, you will have to leave the line to put in your vehicle. There are no bags to carry any souvenir purchases. They take the lid off of your water bottle and won't let you have it back so be prepared to spill it all over yourself.

name: Terrence Terrell
text: It's too dang hot, go doing the colder months.

name: Renell Allen
text: This venue is very very hot for July in Texas.  Dress very comfortably, bring an umbrella and towel for your sweat.

name: Sarah Potvin
text: Always a good time. Except for the ANTS!!! Heart was the only time we've had to fight ants...

name: Andrew lANGELier
text: For an Outdoor Concers the sound is great wherever you sit.

name: ART OCHOA
text: Very friendly staff....awesome time....needs more bathrooms.

name: Joey Hardwick
text: Best sounding large venue for live music.

name: Amanda Ridge
text: Came here for Weenie Roast. Stupid hot and not near enough moving air. (I’m awake it’s July) maybe the water (since you can’t bring anything in) could be sold next to nothing or half price. The food was not good and everything has gluten in it except the popcorn... which sucked... (how do you mess up popcorn?! You don’t let it fully pop, no salt or butter...) at least the acoustics are ok and the restrooms are ample. Oh yeah, parking sucks.

name: Paulette Atkins
text: Mc Hammer, Doug E Fresh, Sit mix a lot and Kid n Play turned it out!!

name: Eric Hogan
text: Had the Incredible Experience watching Professionals Perform tonight.  Slipknot.

name: Mark Jeffrey
text: My wife and I went to see KORN last night 7/20/19 and it was awesome and the pavilion was easy to get to plenty of parking and had a really good time and felt at ease if that's possible at at KORN concert🤘

name: Margaret Peery
text: Shinedown put on an absolutely spectacular show.  They are simply masters at their craft.

name: Kyle S
text:
We've been visiting the pavilion on evenings where there is free entertainment from the Houston Symphony/Ballet/Operah. It's a wonderful opportunity to introduce our children to the arts in a less "formal" setting.

For these events it's not as crowded so it is much easier to navigate parking and the pavilion itself. The food vendors and they still charge the same amount but on a plus, you get to bring in your own food during the special events.

Overall the atmosphere is much nicer in these nights than when a regular concert is in town.

name: M B
text: Very bad experience with last concert.  Please if you have medical issues do not assume they will allow a medical bag as stated on their site.  I did the research and failed.  Missed the concert I wanted to see.  No accommodation for missing the concert. I’ve been going to concerts often since I was a teen.  Never ever felt so discriminated against and a horrible nightmare time. I have more concert tickets this summer I really have no desire to go to after that treatment. Message to pavilion:   Please remove the medical bag option off your site. Provide your own “medical/diaper” bags at the medical booth so you don’t discriminate who needs what.  Thanks

name: Scott Penn
text: Excellent venue for concerts...Hootie and Bare Naked Ladies were excellent as well.

name: Raechel French
text: I love sitting on the lawn and just relaxing during the show. Get there early to get a good spot and avoid the hangups that do occur with ticket check. A nice pavilion venue! I do wish they have easier routes of accessing the amenities from the lawn. There is plenty parking but some are in lots that are a small trek from the pavilion - the walk is shaded and pretty though so enjoy!

name: Darren Black
text: This place made me very upset however they did come through for me. When I bought the tickets I asked can I bring my own seats and I was told yes. This is the reason why I have purchased lawn seats and not any other seats it's because I could bring my own seats. However after we parked and we walk all the way there with our heavy chairs we were told we could not bring them inside. I ask to speak to a manager and they reaffirmed the same thing and told us that they had their own that we could rent. That was not a good enough answer for me so I asked to speak to a higher up person inform them of what happened and they were able to find me seats I was very happy with the service however I wish it would just been told in the first place that we cannot bring seeds and I would have gladly paid for an upgrade.

name: Sheri S
text: Awesome venue. Big names at reasonable prices. Lawn seating for Luke Bryan $35.00

name: Kristina Hahn
text: This is a terrible venue if you actually like the band you want to see. Sound quality is horrendous - the mic has screeched over 5 times for multiple bands in the same day. Seats have good viewing - but the large televisions they use for the bands are in black and white which really reduces the experience of the bands light shows and use of colors for those who can't see. Let's not forgot about a lack of free parking nearby, be prepared for a 15 minute walk if you don't want to pay or get towed. Now of course the high prices food and beverages are typical for a large venue - but the "pro" is that they allow you to bring your own food. Good luck actually carrying it because they only allow bags as big as a peice of paper although they allow large blanket bags which is super confusing. They should clearly state bag dimensions on signs because having to walk back to a car 15 minutes away to put away a purse is a huge annoyance. Also it's a no brainer that this is a hot outdoor venue. You are really better off seeing a popular band at an indoor professional venue.

name: Abel Melchor
text: When the weather is good. Its hard to beat.

name: Jackie Moon
text: Been to a number of shows here. Always a great time

name: Thiago Cordolino
text: Lawn or seats, you always seem to have a view of the stage. And their new screens make it so easy to watch. The food is a bit expensive, but that's the woodlands for ya.

name: Luis Aguero
text: FIRST TIME THERE GREAT FOR HEAVY METAL CONCERTS, FOOD. ETC..ETC.. IRON MAIDEN ROCKED!!!!!!!

name: Michael Garcia
text: Great  venue  get to the area early ,all great place to eat and shop

name: Chelsea Carreon
text: Saw Florence and the machine twice, sat in the back middle, as well as back of the first section on the far right. Both were great seats, parking is not cheap, about 20$ in the garage. But it’s nice and feels safe.

name: Jean Ferrand
text: Open arena in hot and muggy Houston? Who's bright idea was that?

name: Melissa Thompson
text: Great 4th of July concert with Houston Symphony! Nice staff.

name: James martin
text: This the best venue for any event. Just the best organized parking, seating, and Security staff.

name: Braggij
text: Great venue for concerts and more. Parking can be a bit of a hassle and it is open air, so the heat can get to you

name: SleevedTank
text: Nice location. Staff for most part is friendly, some staff could use an attitude adjustment with a staff.

name: EC design
text: What can I say?  It’s clean, outdoors, fantastic landscaping, modern architecture.  Just add your favorite performance and you get a night to remember.

name: Angela Bell
text: The concert line up was great. The only downside was the unorganization

name: Krista Hoffman
text: It's good for a concert, if it's nice out. The prices for alcohol are ridiculous!

name: celina smith
text: Always a great view and time. The staff have always been great.

name: Brenda Santamaria
text: I went on a field trip here with my son for the Children's Festival and it was an amazing experience. All the staff was super nice and helpful. The place was clean from the seats all the way to the restrooms.

name: Robby Hayes
text: Beer prices are way to high! $17 for a hopadillio? It seems like this venue has lost touch of a good concert experience. 11pm cut off for the noise ordnance is ridiculous also. Really do not want to go back to see a show here again.

name: Sarah Gordon
text: Love the concerts just need a valet service

name: Sam Watson
text: Wonderful venue. Love that they have free concerts with the Houston Orchestra!!

name: Logan Fenton
text: Fun and comfy even on the lawn. Just bring some picnic blankets/towels!

name: Audrey Bernal
text: It's hot under the pavillion...no breeze even though the night was breezy.  Drinks super expensive.  2 tall beers for $27.

name: Chase Dizzie
text: The Pavilion is a pretty awesome place. It's decently large and the way the entire setup was made was pretty smart. All seats and rows form a semi-circle sort of like an opera house. This makes the performance seem way more interesting and makes it a heck of a lot easier to hear and see. The overall venue in general is aesthetically pleasing. Parking is insane on popular nights, but you can usually get out in about 30-45mins after the police clear everything off. The largest issue with Cynthia Woods are the prices. If you though places like NRG and Minute Maid were pricey, wait until you order something here. $50 can be wiped out in the matter if an instant, by yourself. Still though, the Pavilion is where it's at and always has the hottest stars performing.

name: Travis Hyde
text: This place is maintained very well as far as concert venues go.   My biggest complaints are with the security and the parking.   I understand wanting to keep people safe,  but this venue is far more invasive when you enter than airport security even.   Since Houston is a nasty place to be outside in most of the year,  I dread having to wait in line for an eternity prior to having every crevice of my body inspected.  I would suggest getting there early and using a phone app to mark your parking spot,  if it's already dark when you get there and it's a reasonably well sold event,  you're going to have a heck of a time finding your car again because the nearby lots all lack distinguishable features and you'll end up very lost.  Not so much an issue now with the smart phone apps that will track you to your car,  but if that phone dies and you aren't an ace with tracing your steps,  good luck my friend.

name: Greg B
text: Audio could be a bit better... I don't like the way it bounces off the tents and screws up the clarity of most performances.anf their beer is extremely high priced!

name: Anthony Kunen
text: Very helpful staff. Wish it were louder.

name: Samantha Hardin
text:
Such an awesome venue to enjoy concerts (even on the lawn with a comfy blanket)! 🎉

Absolutely love the re-modeling they’ve done in the last few years! ✅

...And, the Pavilion Partners do so much contribute back to the community! 😍

name: Barbie Hackney
text: Concert. Great seats. Beautiful area. Staff nice and helpful.

name: Jarynette Montejano
text: Saw Ozzy last night! Best show I have personally ever been to. Freaking absolutely incredible!! I was on the lawn and the sound quality was absolutely INSANE!

name: Sheanna Nielson
text: This amphitheatre is very nice. It's set up perfectly to chill out and listen to some awesome music. The acoustics are 10000 times better than Texas' yearly rodeo concerts ever could be. However, dont be surprised when you pay 15$ for a beer!

name: Roberto Olivas
text: Great outdoor venue, but be prepared to pay dearly for beer and wine!

name: johnathan miranda
text: Drinks severely overpriced! Also what is with major venues having troths as urinals. You charge $20 for parking, $4.75 for water. $7 to rent a chair for "lawn" seating, yet you cannot install a urinal!?! I mean come on. I will probably never go back

name: Jason Doornik
text: Really one of the best outdoor venues in Houston. Great small atmosphere but not too small. Great food and beverage choices and the surrounding area has lots to offer in the way of food, beverages and entertainment.

name: Michael Kaiser
text: Nothing really wrong...its a nice place just not a five star

name: Sandy Porter
text: We had a blast.  Bare Naked Ladies opened for Hootie & The Blowfish, they were awesome !! The restrooms were VERY clean !!  Everyone there helpful and friendly, can't go wrong at the Pavilion on a nice summer night !

name: Monica Torres
text: I loved it.. it's big enough, people are re very respectful and no matter where you sit you pretty much have an amazing view. Only thing is dont bring big backpacks, or big purses, they wont let anything bigger than a letter size envelope

name: Gerry Beathard
text: Great concert venue. Will be back soon.

name: Glyn Boren
text: A very well maintained, clean venue. Even better, services are organized (lawn chairs) although the festival beverage pricing is shocking. Overall it is a top flight, open air experience.

name: Mo Dominick
text: Great venue! Seating was comfortable. Plenty of staff and security. I wish the fans worked better. They were not circulating air by moving extremely slow.

name: Heidi Tezyk
text:
It was awesome except for the outrageous cost of food and drinks.
$16 for a beer, from the bottle.

name: Courtney Barrett
text: Love the lawn. Take a blanket, sit out and enjoy.

name: Sunanda Pandian
text: It's nice to be outdoors,  but not on the hottest day in summer.

name: Kim Y
text: It was awesome night enjoy with my best friend son.

name: Brian Jacobs
text: Great venue for concerts.  Granted, there's no way I'm going during the summer months due to the heat.  With that being said, just went to see the Counting Crows and Matchbox 20.  The show was awesome.  No complaints or issues at all.

name: Michael George
text: Fantastic venue. Love the setup with the banked lawn area

name: Marcus Brown
text: Friendly service but slow process

name: Al Williams
text: Super hot. Too hot. Pricey drinks.

name: Deborah Richardson
text: Omg the Korn concert was amazing!

name: Ross whitby
text:
As much as you can enjoy being outdoors, in texas, in summer, surrounded by a sea of sweaty people...

The things we do for music...

name: Everythang Texas
text: Awesome venue, plenty of area to party & have a good time, a ton of square feet for concert's.

name: Jeff Ketcher
text: Huge, clean and always an awesome experience. Every time I go, I get the lawn seats to have the freedom to move around, sit where you want, and not have to disturb others if you need something like if you were sitting in a row

name: Rebecca McGinn
text: Good venue. Headsup ladies do not bring big purses or bags. You may not being in anything that's big. I'd bring the bare minimum with you in there. Phone keys wallet maybe a lipstick for touch ups or whatever. But I'm just recommending to bring as little as possible. On the lawn watch out for potential mosh pits. name: Gina Smith

Perfect venue for taking in a concert

However, you might run into the occasional drunk, extra friendly concert goers who often accidentally spill their beer on you. Get there early to claim your front lawn spots. If you're in a seat - well, they aren't going anywhere.

Ladies, keep your big bags at home and save yourself the hassle.

text: Visually its amazing but many things could've been better. I graduated from there a few days ago and the ceremony was very well put together. I think if the signs had been a bit bigger and much more visible and if there were just more visual improvements made, it would be better to help other people find what they needed and where they needed to go. Casual, relaxing atmosphere

text:

Sound is normally amazing! Definitely one of the best sounding venues around. Lawn is always fantastic, and so are the seats. Lots of parking, and not crazy expensive like Downtown.

name: Eisha Khan
text: Incredible scenery and plenty of amazing photoshoot opportunities, especially during golden hour! Parking was free for a concert I went to, not sure about other events. A single 1 liter water bottle was $7.50, and they threw away the bottle cap, which was dumb, because then you can't leave the bottle alone.

name: Kevin Wolf
text: It is good place to work for seasonal job

name: Stephanie Manley
text:
This is a great venue for a concert.  I have been to many concerts here.  I have sat both on the lawn and in seats up front.    For the most part all seats are good both on the lawn and in regular seats.  There aren't many obstructed views.  The obstructed views tend to be where the seats are, this will be noted on your ticket.

If you can get there early when there is lawn seating you can get some better spots, again, get their early.  They rent chairs.

I find the security very intrusive here.   I carry a prescription with me they have always demanded to see my ID when I go in.  I think this must violate some measure of privacy.

The concessions are on the higher side here, so you may want to eat and drink before you go.

The drawback of this place tends to be during the summer when it is extremely hot.  I don't recommend this venue during the heat of the summer when they offer all day long concerts.  The heat is a bit much and you may go broke buying bottles of water.

name: B R

text:
My second visit here; this time for a July 4 concert by the Houston Symphony Orchestra, along with performances by a guest vocalist.

The pavillion is a great place for performances. Based on my two experiences here, it seems you can see and hear the performers from just about anywhere you are seated.

The program included a lot of patriotic tunes, although there were several Sinatra numbers as well (he performed at the pavillion's opening) -- and of course, there was the performance of the 1812 Overture (complete with cannon fire).

The evening was quite enjoyable. I'm looking forward to my next concert here.

name: creenamaki
text: In my teens and early 20's, I lived out of state by an outdoor amphitheatre. I loved every minute of it!  Imagine my JOY when I moved right down the street from Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavillion? 🤩  I love the variety of acts/music - some are obviously from past shows.  From Iron Maiden to Dio to Motorhead to Judas Priest... from Snoop Dogg to Jill Scott to Charlie Wilson to Janet Jackson.  From Korn to Alice in Chains to Steely Dan to.. you get the idea!!  I've been fortunate to have seen a LOT of great shows with wonderful friends.  I've ALSO been to venues with disgusting restrooms!! 😖  But considering the large amount of people constantly moving? CWMP does a pretty darned good job of keeping up with all of us and our messes, and I really appreciate that..!  My only real complaint is NO Birdie Water!! If it can't be FREE, then:  Birdie = cheap, cheap, cheap!!!  Why a small fortunate for H20?  All in all, a most excellent place to enjoy a day/evening out with the one(s) you celebrate the joys of life with MUSIC!! 🎶

name: Montgomery Gossen
text:
I went to see the Dave Matthews Band a couple of weeks ago at the Pavilion.  I believe that this is the premiere music venue in the greater Houston area.  I really like the lawn setup, and the "circus tent" awning.  The Woodlands also provides vast options for accommodations, dining and entertainment options.  I would say it is very walkable getting to and from everything, being that it sits right in the middle of the woodlands, right across the street from the Woodlands Mall, which also provides good free parking.

The only problems i had was the volume level on the lawn, and the cut off time for the concerts.  I felt i couldn't really hear or 'feel' the energy of the show.  I felt i was merely just listening to the band on my computer.  The concert also ended at 10:45 which is due to a noise ordinance put on by The Woodlands.

text:
Note: Review based on visits for rock concerts.

I've been here for a couple of Buzzfests, and several rock concerts (Linkin Park, Slipknot, Lana Del Rey, for reference). It's a nice venue in a very nice area. Don't ever look forward to traffic to and from here but once I'm parked I'm set. So the walk to there and over the little bridge from the side I come from is nice. Looks like a nice area for walks and picnics, if you're into such activities. Food's expensive, naturally, but not bad for the one time we bought food here. Seats are okay if you're planning on sitting. Lawn area is cool to thrash around in, especially if muddy. It's too bad the pit area is so small and, therefore, pricey which makes it inaccessible for a lot of people. Place looks great at night, so couple that with a great headliner and you're in for a good time.

I was upset and angry, had no choice but to abandon my purse at the entrance right by a trash can and use a grocery bag. When the show was over, I went looking for my purse, only to find it IN the trash can. I was so mad. That's a great way to ruin a good night. What makes no sense is that the tote bag they were selling at the merch stand was WAY bigger! Unbelievable! I believe that if they come across big bags, they should have at least a small office or something where they can keep an eye on their items and when the show's over, they'll come and pick it up. People, if you come here to see a show, make sure the bag you bring is no bigger than 8.5 x 11 and no backpacks either. I have been coming here for years every summer we see atleast 8 concerts.

We did the VIP experience for 3 doors down last night, by the way it was a totally awesome show.  Anyhow,checking in at will call no one had a clue where we should
go. After waiting 20 minutes or so we finally just found out on our own. We were not the only ones having trouble.  So when we finally got checked in,I told 2 different staff members to alert Will Call so the next person doesn't have to go through what we did. The first staff member could give a darn and I knew he wasn't going to call.  Then the lady that works outside the lounge was about the rudest ever. My son and nephew come every time they are very well mannered and polite but it seems everytime there is always a rude staff member to them.  Like teenagers can't ask a question???
When we started coming here 6 years ago it seemed more laid back friendly people. When we were leaving the show One of the older guys said come on you got to go,go,rudely. I said one second my son is headed this way with car keys. I wasnt standing there 2 minutes. IJust dont like the way we have been treated. Instead of being so abrupt and sounding angry try to tell me politely and friendlier. It makes a way better impression.  Every time we come we spend atleast $150 food,drinks,4 people. I liked the more laid back Woodlands 6 years ago.
Shout out to the sweet sweet lady that works serving the food in the Whiskey cafe,not sure if that's the name! But it's the little food place in the lounge. Wish I would have got her name and the rude ones  too ,but I usually dont follow through and post bad comments.
Anyway the food lady was just willing to go out of her way to help and just a super nice person, great service.

My husband and I went for the 4th of July show.
What I loved- it's fee! Every year they do a 4th of July program that's free to the public. There's plenty of seating. My husband and I like sitting out back in the big open lawn area. Free lawb chair makes it an easy seating choice.
The entertainment is always good. Of course the orchestra is amazing. There's always a guest entertainer. One year it was a painter, another year a couple danced and sang, this year was a singer. Always top rated performance.
Not so liked- the bathroom all though kept clean are very hot.
It's a free event so where they really get you is food and drink. Be prepared.
This last part is not a dislike or a like, it's a respect. I respect how strict they are what you can and cannot bring in. When they give you a bag size they mean it. They do check everyone who comes in.
Overall it's a great experience.

I wish there were more places for big artists to come besides Cynthia Woods. This place is mediocre at best. I've seen many performers here from Rob Thomas to Fall Out Boy and Chicago. The security measures taken to gain entry are so ridiculous and time consuming, and completely ineffective.

My wife and I went to a show a few months back, and called ahead to the pavilion to ask what was allowed inside. We were told blankets and water bottles, and a few other things. We get to the show and were denied entry until we threw away our expensive reusable water bottles. When we told them we were given permission to bring them in when we called we were told that the performing artist (Fall Out Boy) made a last minute special request to not allow reusable water bottles into the pavilion. I have no idea how that works or if there is any truth to that, but we were forces to throw away our bottles to get in.

Again, I wish there were a better place for artists to perform.

name: Rosie Chavira
text:
Nice reputable venue, but rated 2 because I dislike paying $13 for 16 fl.oz. domestic beer served warm.  I come here to let loose and enjoy myself and rock out with my rooster out (responsibly of course... Uber: 4he48ue    Lyft: Roseanna39521 )

**** WARNING****

-------------EXCESSIVELY LONG THAT BELOW THIS POINT! READ AT YOUR OWN RISK---------------------

I have seen the price of the beer rise to $13 from $4 over 15 years. Sadly, the price increase was at the cost of quality of product quality of service. I never said anything before because I simply didn't notice.  We have all been trained to lower our standards and concede to the rules of supply and demand. It wasn't until recently that I figured out what I was demanding wasn't being supplied. As our world is becoming more instant, our demands are literally at our finger tips and we now have options.
When I saw the beer was $13 I  subconsciously started weighing my options,  but with no re-entry to the venue I had no options.....

So my mind went off the deep end stayed creating options for me.....drink or no drink....Beer or no beer.... have a drink or quit my job on Monday.... wait... what?

(Thought)[If I have 3 beers tonight, that's $39 or... that's 2 1/2 hours at my dead-end job where I am constantly reassuring my insecure boss that he is "doing a GREAT job" ****smile**** reassuring as I continue to correct his mistakes... discreetly (because God forbid this already insecure man get the notion that I may be better at his job than he is). The job where I pretend to have common interests with the ego in office to left of me, the tool in the second cubicle, the adrenaline junkie sales rep, but MOST importantly the bosses pet (who doesn't seem to have an actual job or purpose for her presence aside from maintaining a certain amount of constant pressure from her lips to the boss's ass at all times.) I sometimes pretend to envy their co-dependent relationship because it's a perfect smoke screen... For my stealthy attack. I hit them both with atomic mind bombs and passive-aggressive comments disguised as praises and compliments so that I can get a kick out of using their stupidity as my entertainment. My favorite is the land-mind bombs. (These work when I speak such a subtle insult, that I can walk back to my office and sit at my desk and watch them as they stop in their tracks and realize that I may have insulted them, but yet they don't quite believe I would deliberately devise such an attack. As they question it, they slowly turn and look at me, I suppose they are looking for me to say "gotcha" or something catchy, but no.... that's not my style... I carry on as if I said nothing or of the ordinary. This is when the bomb is detonated... when suspicion meets deniability. Ha ha ha ha)]

Yes I will have three beers because it serves dual purpose... celebrating my victory in surviving another work week and preparing for the work week that is to come. I will probably repeat the same thought process every time I come here to see my favorite band, unwind from my hectic week and enjoy an overpriced, underrefridgerated domestic beer until the price is so high it offsets the work:play ratio enough for me to deem the beer "not worth the price". At which point I will definitely choose to stop next time at the nearest "convenience store" and thoroughly enjoy paying $1.75 for 16 fl.oz. domestic beer served as it was intended... ice cold. Eventually more people will do the same. As it gets harder to move the warm beer, eventually the price will come down.

Until then I raise a toast to the people who relentlessly exploit the laws of supply and demand....

"Here's to settling... for now... until something else will do... or until our option is assigned to us"

name: BB Christian A Child Of God
Diane Sheets
text:
Room was comfortable, staff was very nice and mostly accommodating. Had a couple of issues  (toilet paper holder falling off the wall, not enough places to hang a wet towel, food stains on desk and 2 chairs) but really minor inconveniences in my book. Hand sanitizing wipes were left in the rooms for us - nice touch - and lots of signage to wear masks and be socially responsible were present (if only people cared).

We came for a soccer tournament so I'm not sure if they were unprepared for the higher volume after covid restrictions were eased, or if they were unprepared for the absolute lack of respect shown by teenagers and adults who refuse to clean up after themselves.
*trash sat in the hallways for far too long (IMO). there were bar glasses in the hallway upon my  check-in Monday evening that still hadn't been removed late Tuesday night despite housekeeping being up and down the hall that day (just one example).
*trash (torn down cardboard) was left in the east stairwell on the 4th floor impeding access for multiple days.
*food and trash were left to sit in public areas, trash cans overflowing near elevators and front desk.

I didn't see alot of staff present other than in the lobby and housekeeping, so I'm guessing there just weren't enough people to keep up with the animals posing as humans - sorry, not typically THAT person, but my faith in decent human behavior is failing - not entirely the fault of hotel staff but unfortunately the reflection lies with their handling of it.

resp.text: Thanks Diane for your review! Its not that we weren't prepared but like many we are understaffed and trying to hire but having a very hard time getting any responses to our job posts:( Housekeeping was definitely working hard but just couldn't keep up! We are running with about 30% of our normal staffing levels to put in perspective!

Security always said hello in passing and made me feel safe. The hotel does seem a little out of date. But you can tell they've tried making some upgrades. I was pleased we got a room on the 7th floor. I was thinking with the Groupon discount we would be and in a room with no windows. But we actually got a great view. The shower and bed are the my only complaints. They weren't horrible but new ones would give it the 1 star it's missing. You do have to pay for parking which was a little weird but it was only a few extra dollars and it worked out fine. I would stay here again.

resp.text:

text:
