text: Food was fresh, customer service was great.  Highly recommend this place

name: Khristina Mari Ancheta
text: Suprisingly good! It is our first time to try mongolian hotpot here at little sheep's. We've been postponing going here because hotpots don't usually entice us but were glad we finally tried it. We we're able to get our money's worth for the hotpot. Their broth is really good and they don't skimp on meats. Also their shrimp are fresh and the taste mixes well with the broth. We will definitely go back. 👍👍

name: Tyler Brooks
text: We went recently and the food tasted okay. Unfortunately we found a small roach in one of the dishes. That is obviously not good but the worst part was the casual attitude of EVERYONE who worked there about it. Server and manager both just seemed like it was some everyday occurance. To top it off we were comp'd 7 dollars on our bill, which isn't even even the full cost of the dish we found the roach in.

name: Andrew Logan
text: The food was hood. Atmosphere was cool. We went for a  team event and we all loved it.

name: kiet luong
text: Nice place, fine food

name: Anthony Pepe
text: Ate there yesterday after the restaurants were allowed to reopen. If I could give this a hundred Stars I would. I highly recommend premium at 27.99 AYCE I'm not a i I'm not a lamb eater so I didn't have this spring lamb but I did have the wagyu beef and the ribeye along with the assortment of seafoods and the meats were stunningly delicious

name: Korey Pilon
text:
My friends and I tried this place after learning was Hot Pot was and were super excited after seeing the reviews. We got there earlier than 5:30 and one of the servers said we could go ahead and wait at a table if we’d like. He was very friendly and even showed up how to order off their menu. We got the half and half broth with the all you can eat option for $20 each. The pork belly was amazing, as were the noodles, corn, potatoes and chicken. We even tried their chicken wings and little fried rolls. We enjoyed most of what we are, the meatballs and imitation crab were the only items no one liked. And we all needed up proffering the spicy broth. We didn’t care for the flavor of beef and lamb meatballs and the texture for the imitation crab was off putting. Overall, the food and service was great and will definitely be back soon.
Pro tip: dip the rolls in the broth ❤️

name: David Coffin
text:
Fantastic food and service. I'd go here with a large group, because you'll have a lot of food. You can get multiple kinds of broth in one hot pot, separated by divider, so one half can be spicy and the other not, in case some members of your group don't like spice.

Get the pot stickers. Trust me.

name: Rami Ayoub
text: This was a great experience. The food was great, the service even better. Highly recommend. Definitely coming back for more.

name: Paige Rappleye
text: Very clean with friendly service

name: Jillian Tippit
text: Amazing.

name: Yi
text: Very yummy and flavorful! No dipping sauces needed. Service was fast and the food was fresh. Great variety. First few times we went we did all you can eat. But in reality, can't really eat that much. This time 6 combos for 9 people with some extra of our favorites was enough. Really liked the lamb and beef, shrimp (comes with head and shell), fish balls with roe. Noodles and porous tofu really soaks up the flavor well.

name: Erin Griggs
text: Great place. You will be hooked. They were very helpful our first time.

name: Brian Rohde
text: Great place to just eat as much as you can. Only wish they had fresh chili peppers to go with the hot pot.

name: Sam Cook
text: Okay, the only reason I'm giving it a good rating is because I love the food here. Other than that, the service is quite horrible and be prepared to be given the wrong food items and for the items that you DID order to never show up if you do the all you can eat option. You're not going to have many problems if you order from the menu, so there's a tip. In spite of those huge cons, my boyfriend and I come to this place nearly every week because there's just something about hot pot that hits the spot.

name: Anthony Mondragon
text: This Little Sheep Mongolian Hot Pot location is excellent! It is slightly less busy than the Chinatown location, but expect a wait if you come for dinner! This place has excellent, top quality food and the service is excellent, I think even better than the other location! Come with an empty stomach and try out the all you can eat! It is slightly discounted for lunch during weekdays. Try out the half and half soup so you can have best of both worlds. I would highly recommend this restaurant and would come back often.

name: Chelsey Shelledy
text: If craving hotpot this place works. They are all you can eat semi serve yourself

name: NL
text:
Thanks for the wonderful service & food~
Had a good time at here.
Definitely will be come again😋😋😋

name: Rena Patel
text: Excellent hotpot the broth is amazing and the variety of ingredients is vast. Delicious. Wish they had a few more Asian beer options but it's a minor thing. The service is pretty good as well.

name: Amanda Ulmer
text: Great as always! Plenty of good food and the servers are always very attentive. I love there lamb dumplings!

name: Bethany Garza
text: Wonderful fun fun and service...

name: Normal Person
text: Delicious, delicious and super delicious. You won't go wrong at all. Great quality food, tables and sitting are very comfortable, great atmosphere. The hostess was very polite, waiters and runner are very nice and cordial, the server in my table was super kind, attentive, careful and listened to us well. KUDOS to the wait staff!. I will be back. Please, people be nice to the wait staff, I saw some getho customers being rude.

name: Allan Holtzmann
text: All You Can Eat - good variety of meat options, a wonderful experience to be certain.

name: Robert Ayala
text:
We went here with a good friend who recommended this restaurant for hot pot. We were not disappointing!

The spicy broth was awesome, only wish it was a little spicier :)  Since we're new at this, we let our friends pick most of the meats and veggies. We loved them all! I'm not a big tofu person, but I even enjoyed the raw tofu. The Glass & Udon noodles were my personal favorites.

Will be returning next week!

name: Jayla Sylvester
text: GREAT EXPERIENCE!!! If you have the chance to eat here...DO!!! Just don't plan on going anywhere after you leave here. You will be full and smell like the food. 🤣

name: Jessica Danford
text: Great food and service for a unique dining experience!

name: Xilu Ma
text: Just renovated and rebranded, loving the new decor and AYCE buffet style with just having to order meat. Great for the kiddos and drinks/dessert are included 👍👍👍 ALSO now the hot pot is set in the table, great for not having to worry the kids are going to knock it over.

name: Rebecca Nye
text: The services is good and the food is tasty. Cooking your own food is always fun, if you are not in a rush.

name: Russell
text:
Paying $30 including tip for boiling broth and having to cook your own food is a concept I am not a fan of. It was enjoyable only from the standpoint that it took longer to eat and therefore elongated the get together.

Service left something to be desired. Plenty of parking.

Will not be going back on my own accord.

name: Jeffrey Chang
text: Excellent service and food. Renovated interior is very nice.

name: Chad
text: Love this place.  Super tasty and a real neat experience.

name: john howell
text: Great service and food

name: Pierre HUYNH
text:
the food was good, although the original broth didn't taste much. the spicy broth is very flavorful, and is spicy enough to be tolerable without hurting. but of you are scared, take the half/half which is a great idea. the pot is divided and you have one broth on each side.
The variety is good, lots of different options. some is fresh, and some are frozen, but it's ok, you cook them in the broth anyway. i just hope the frozen meats are made on site, because they were pretty good. the garlic beef was excellent
service was not on point, depending on who were serving us. one dude was not smiling at all, but was still helping, some lady refilled the broth but spilled a little around because she was trying to do it fast. and another guy was great but spoke little English. so like everybody was trying to do good with a little that is off. the general impression is still good, tho. for around $25 per person, you eat pretty well. i will try other hot pots (this one was my very first) to compare.

name: Emily Weisenbach Nickel
text: Delicious and fun!

name: Daniel Wojtasik
text: I came to Little Sheep's in search of a big delicious meal.  I cannot say I was overwhelmed with satisfaction at the end.  Initially I was served a very bad tasting wasting (faucet?) and got a bad feeling.  The portions where superiors and the taste was 7/10 overall.  The taste of the meats was not good.  Although, the taste of the sea food was good.  In addition, I did not feel rush during the meal and felt relatively welcome.  I'm inclined to say three stars but because it was a good experience, deserving of 3.5

name: Xin Huang
text: Not the best one in Htown，but still good

name: cupcake cc
text: Food is fresh. Restaurant is clean. Waiter waitress are professional. We love this place

name: Carl Perry
text:
AYCE hot pot is amazing. The value cannot be beat.  Been here a dozen times and will keep coming back.
Good for small to medium size groups. We've even done a group of 16 on 2 tables and that worked out well.
Go for the spicy broth, it's not very spicy.  Get the chefs sauce too, you won't regret it, it's great on everything.
Tons of items, including seafood that can be thrown in.  The beef and lamb are great.  Intestine is my favorite.
You'll try 10-20 things you've never had before.  Be open and try things out.

name: Gaurav Verghese
text: Meh food but great prices

name: Hector Parada
text: So good.

name: Jade Jackson
text: I've never had hot pot before so this was a different experience. I did enjoy the variety of food offered. The garlic beef was by far my favorite with the spicy broth. The non spicy broth just had no flavor. It's $22 for all you can eat. I'll definitely be back to try more items.

name: K T
text: Not really my thing I guess... me and a friend basically paid $50 to cook our own soup?  I don't get it, compared to every other restaurant in Houston this is as basic as it can get.  Ingredients looked OK and the soup was not bad, anyhow.  Decor was old and the whole place was not very clean, which is to be expected when you cook on your table I suppose.

name: Jennifer Penchas
text: Our large family loves hot pot and we go very often. We like this location, they are always very nice and accommodating. The manager Andy, has been amazing every time we need reservation for our family. The food here is good and they have a big selection of different meats, seafood, and vegetables. If you want to try something new and like to have large family dinners, I recommend this place!

name: Janene Sleem
text: Tasty and different.

name: Andy Vu
text: They have an option of "all you can eat" which I think around  $20 per person. That is the best deal because I can order as much meat as I want. The broth is so yummy. Good service. Highly recommended.

name: Alex Smith
text: I've eaten here many times. I've been there in groups of 2, 3, 5, and 10, but be sure to call ahead if you're going to have a big group. Since you're cooking your own meal, they need to give you a table with room for multiple pots. Everyone I've taken has enjoyed it, including the vegetarians. My only complaint is that I always end up eating way too much.

name: Mike X
text: Great selection and quality of meat

name: Melody Li
text: Pretty good food, come here often to do the half and half, all you can eat hot pot. Their lamb is good and a good variety of dishes. But I came with a friend and both of us feel a bit awkward in stomach when we left.

name: Stefanie Wozniak
text: All you can eat is so worth it here. Clean, busy and super delicious

name: Vee Tran
text: The place was pretty good. Went on a friday about 7:30PM. Seating was pretty quick for that hour. For 5 people our bill totaled in the 100s for all you can eat hot pot. The food was good but the broth can get pretty salty. Parking can be a hassle because there is like 7 other shops in the plaza. On that note it can get pretty loud so dont expect cafe conversations. We spent about 2 hours there.

name: Iyaremis Velazquez
text: I have been several times and always is been beyond good. They offer so many variety of vegetables, meat and fish. They also offer Vegetarian menù. Service is wonderful, food is fresh and the broth (original, spicy or Vegetarian) is fenomenal!!! I moved in Florida and I wish they will have a Restaurant like Little Sheep Mongolian Hot Pot over here...

name: Kathryn Hatfield
text: Simply fabulous! 6 of us ate a feast of epic proportions and paid just over $20 per head - and that's with tip. We tried a variety of meats, shrimp balls, a mushroom assortment, at least three different greens, some dumplings, quail eggs - everything was delicious and fresh, and service was attentive. We waited for over an hour to be seated (we arrived at 6pm on a Saturday) and if anything the crowd out the front had gotten bigger while we were inside, so be prepared! But regardless of the wait, this place is highly recommended.

name: Dax G
text: My best friend brought me here for a fantastic dinner. We were so excited that there was a genuine vegetarian option and ate way too much food. I loved the convenience of the table-top plate to keep the broth warm. The ability to customise a meal only sweetened the deal.

name: Richard Perales
text: Don't let fear of the unknown scare you, the food is fantastic and experience is always fun.

name: James Syring
text: My wife and I visited this restaurant for lunch and it was absolutely spectacular. The facility was clean and the service was quick and polite. The food was clearly of quality and care given to each bite. The blend of spices and taste was amazing and I would definitely giving this place a try if you are in the area.

name: Ashley Shem
text: I love eating hot pot here.  Their broth is AMAZING.  They also offer smaller lunch portions for single diners which is a nice change.  This is my go-to hot pot place in Houston.  I like that they have such a wide variety of food to cook.  Definitely come here with a group of friends so you can get a wider variety of things to try.  If you eat a lot, get the all-you-can-eat option.  The only downside is that the all-you-can-eat menu is limited.  I love getting the house special egg noodles here.  The food is delicious, but kind of  pricy.

name: Franco Aguilar
text: Shabu shabu. Go for the all you can eat. 10/10 if you’re hungry.

name: Rosalie Guerrero
text: This is the only Mongolian Hotpot restaurant I've only been to in Houston and honestly I don't care to find another one. They have an extensive menu of items you can get. I definitely recommend getting the $21 all you can eat with the spicy broth. It's worth the up charge honestly.

name: Michael Alfaro
text: Very good Hot Pot.  They bring you selection on multiple ingredients you can add for $20.  If you can manage three rounds go ahead.  But other than having a very spicy soup and normal soup.  I would say the flavors mix very well and you can stay as long as you want to keep ordering.   I've enjoyed myself multiple time come here with my friends and family.

name: Ling Watson
text:
If you are into shabu shabu, this is your fix.

I love hot pot in general. This place offers a nice combo option includes a choice of meat, veggies and other hot pot usual suspects. We had lamb, beef and pork. First of all the quantity is plenty. We ordered 3 combos for 4 ppl and had left over. The meats are very nicely sliced, very thin. Veggies are fresh and the broth is super flavorful. Oh that reminds me, no need to order dipping sauces because with flavorful broth sauce muddles the flavors.

The appetizers are nothing to be excited about.  We didn’t even have room for dessert so no comment on that.

Happy eating

name: Ali Shamsher
text: The service was excellent and fast. The food was good, and the experience was nice, but it is a bit pricey. $60 for 2 people just for the meal and sauces. They did give us 2 $5 vouchers because they were running a special.

name: Dan Nguyen
text: One of my favorite places for hot pot.  Mongolian style is flavorful compared to others.  I usually get the dinner for 2, it could fill up 2-3 people easily.  Chef Special sauce is also delicious for dipping.

name: Marisa Collura
text: Great Place to go for groups! My friends and I went and enjoyed the atmosphere and dining experience. For warned it is pricy but the all you can eat is the best! There were five of us and we went for 3 rounds and we were all full at the end of it. We tried both broths but prefered the original more then the spicy. For sure if you do not know what certain items are on the menu ask or look them up because we tried the different mushrooms and variety of meats and was not dissappointed. If you want more bang for your buck go to this place during off season and the prices will be slightly less. Other then that, I will be visitng this place more with my friends because it ws a perfect setting for us all to interact and enjoy a meal versus just ordering food from a menu and sitting across from one another. Great for family and friends!

name: Amanda Among
text: Loved it. The portions were really big. The food was delicious. The spicy soup base is REALLY spicy. Next time I will get the regular soup base with the peppers on the side so I can add a few for a little kick.

name: Raymond Wang
text: Very good hot pot.  Smell great, good $20 all you can eat deal, just have 4 plates of lamb, you are breaking even already.  :)  Anything else you can eat from the menu, you are making money!  :)

name: Sandra Pham
text: I love hot pots and this is my favorite place to go. The parking is typically horrible unless you go during lunch. Beside the parking, this place is hard to complain about. The vegetables and the meats are always fresh. The broth is flavorful and piping hot which makes for the best soup base. The service could be a bit better but it is what you would expect from a tiny place such as this. You literally throw everything in the pot and let it cook and marinade and voila you have an incredible meal.

name: Jessica Lee
text: The service was great. The hot and spicy broth was amazing. It was all delicious and for a fair price. I can't wait to go again.

name: Celina Ortiz
text: This was my first time going to one of these Mongolia grills. First when I walked in it smelled like seafood which would be normal since they do have raw seafood at this restaurant. Our waiter seemed a little on edge I'm not sure if he was new or if he just didn't know what he was doing. I wasn't sure if I would like the idea of cooking my own food. But there are few things that I thought about when double-dipping my food with others into the same Bowl.

name: David Wong
text: Best Hotpot place in Houston. The soup is spicy and very flavorful. The lunch dinner combo is good enough for me but for a few dollars more you can have all you can eat.

name: Ashley Brooks
text:
All-you-can-eat Hot Pot is the best thing to happen to me in a while (I met the love of my life 4 years ago... I was due).

Go at lunch. Throw down $20 and dig in. Splurge for the special sauces. We love the My Oh My. Here's the beautiful thing. It is all-you-can-eat. You could order 12 plates of the same thing. It will come. Try the spicy broth. Try a mushroom that looks like a stingray. Live a little.

Eat lots of Tong Ho and Dandelion greens. If you are intimidated by chopsticks, use a fork. Don't be shy. Whatever needs to happen to shovel all that amazing food in your face.

name: David Zhang
text: Good service good food

name: Yvette Yanez
text: Had an awesome date night here! Definitely a new experience, great food! Chill environment very laid back and good serving staff! Very helpful with your first time!! The lamb was uh-mazing!

name: HopeSunlightRises
text: Best pot in the whole city!  Delicious.... A must try!

name: roy slocum
text: Great new experience. We did the all you can eat so we could try a little bit of everything. Fun interactive food experience.

name: David Norelid
text:
Bring friends and an appetite! They have all you can eat all hot pot day long, and it's crazy good. Get the spicy broth, don't waste your time on the regular broth. Get the My Oh My sauce and mix a raw egg yolk and some soy sauce into it. Get all the mushrooms you see. Get plenty of tong ho and wide noodles.

PROTIP: If you have any room left, you can just drink the broth from the pot when you're done. You just spend the last hour steeping beef and veggies in it, of course it's going to be amazing.

name: Kevin McAuley
text:
First time getting hot pot. Thought his place was really good.  Better with a larger group then just a +1 though.  So many options and you want to try them all, but the dishes are sized for 4 or more.  There is the "all you can eat" option too, which might be better for small groups.

I did not like the meatballs, very rubbery after being boiled. He bok choy and taro was awesome in the spicy broth.  Be careful with the broccoli! It hold the broth for a while and stays super hot! Noodles were sort of a pain in the butt, i don't think I'll bother ordering them next time.  We got glass and udan.  The glass noodles were easier to wrangle, the udan was so slippery i just gave up and had more vegetables.

name: Aden
text: The soup is delicious! My roommate and I come here and always leave happy. The waiters are nice and I wish we could take it to go when we can’t finish.

name: Robert Waltz
text: Love the hot pot here. Food is fresh and service is good

name: Trey Rouse
text:
This is a unique family dining experience.  The atmosphere is fun, the food is somewhat unique.  Be warned the 'spicy' option is very spicy for the American pallet and the 'mild' has some spice to it.  I like the spicy, but its too much for others in my family who eat picante like apple sauce.

It is tricky to rate this place, as you are essentially cooking your own meal.  What you prepare is dependent on the raw ingredients you request and how long you allow it to cook in the pot.

I will say, I find the all you can eat option to be a bit over priced and avoid ordering that way, but maybe is a good option for people who want to try a little bit of everything.

name: DinhChuong Jason
text: Wow iam very impressed with delicious hotpots and services.

name: Daisy Sonia
text: It was really good.. however since it's a shared meal, each person could bring cash to make the splitting up of the bill easier

name: Julia Alaniz
text: This place is really great to take a group of friends or someone who will appreciate an interesting dining experience. The whole concept is that you order  thinly sliced meat and veggies in rounds and then cook it in a pot of broth at your table. The broths are flavorful, and the meat and veggies seem to be of a good quality. It's get pretty packed on Friday and Saturday nights, so best to plan ahead since the wait can be a little long.

name: Rocker Uhde
text: Tried this place due to a great Groupon deal. I have been here 3 times since and it is amazing every time. Looking forward to going again soon. Get the 1/2 and 1/2 with all you can eat; it is the best food to price ratio.

name: Michael Byerley
text: The all you can eat hot pot is good. They do get reaslly busy on the weekend. So service can be a little slow. Also the wait can be long during peak hours.

name: J KL
text: Love the food and vibe

name: Daniel Dinu
text: I absolutely loved the food here. I recommend the all you can eat option for a first visit so you get to taste a little bit of everything. I'll return here for sure.

name: Sook Lee
text: My favorite places. I can eat every week.. fresh food. Great prices.

name: Maria Dupre
text: Yummy! What a cool experience! We got the bowl with 2 divisions, one for spicy and regular. The buffet had 3 rounds where you can pick multiple ingredients and feed a large group!

name: Samantha Syring
text: The food is amazing and flavorful. Iced tea was crisp and refreshing.  Service was great. Overall, it was a great dining experience.

name: Karina Garcia
text: One of my best eating experience, so many choices we had to go with the all you can eat so we could try as many as possible. The spicy broth is amazing and the kids really enjoyed the whole experience.

name: Richie Nguyenphat
text: Great selection of meats and veggies. I get the all you can eat with half and half broth. Garlic beef is a must try

name: Cammie Cooley
text: Fun environment, great drinks, and amazing food! Try the half and half mix!

name: Davi
text: Delicious broth! The flavor is outstanding! I love the enoki mushrooms! A+ food!!

name: Paulette
text: Fresh and good service, especially with the senior discounts

name: Brian Truong
text:
Awesome place for hot pot.

Really recommend the all you can eat option so you can try a bit of everything.

Make sure you don't wear nice clothes because it's all going to smell like hotpot when you're done.

name: Lorie Yuen
text: I love going there to eat hot pot you can have a couple choices either have a buffet choices where you can eat anything you want all you can eat for one price but you cannot take the soup home or the food but there's another choice you could have which is you can split in half if you don't like it spicy they can make it less spicy if you want a real spicy they can have the other part of the soup real spicy that goes for the buffet one too you can have it all spicy or no spicy soup the one price that you could pay but it's not Buffet you can take home the soup and the food whatever you don't finish :-)! You could have it all mixed match you should have only vegetables only or seafood or combination of lamb which is delicious or beef or chicken or pork anyway you like it :-)! I do recommend those side orders BBQ beef stick or pork or chicken and it's only a dollar which is worth it :-)! And they have the world's best sauce which is called House sauce I normally order a raw egg and put the egg on top of the sauce and dip my hot food into it it is so delicious :-)! The sodas and tea is all free refill but if you want extra meat extra extra vegetables of course it cost extra it depends on which one you order your bills in up being pricey total bill it's wonderful come with a group and Friends! There is no dessert that I see but there's so much food you get stuff so you end up don't want dessert anyway! There's one thing I don't like is that when you ordered that particular non Buffet meal there are things that you choose from and I don't like eating them so I don't want to pay something I don't want to eat and it's hard to sometimes but you had to talk to the manager he's a really really nice guy to substitute like Napa vegetable I hate eating those and tribes I don't like that either! I think they need more Waiters because sometime we don't have good service and sometime we do it depends who's the waiter! The best and wonderful time to go there in the season is winter because if you're real cold this hot pot will keep you hot or warm it depends on your body temperature what it enjoys to handle! They do have a bar there it's depends on what time you go there sometimes there is weight and sometimes there isn't! In some sort of way I also think it's romantic and you could take your time and of course it does take some sort of time it depends the temperature of the Boiling Pot of soup how long it takes to warm it up you can have a romantic conversation and share the delicious and healthy food to eat with your families :-)! What's so wonderful about this place which is the first time for me normally the Hot Pot soup is contain hot water only but this place even if he doesn't want it spicy and it's so delicious and healthy they put herbs and healthy spices to make your health very healthy I have not found any restaurants that would put all these spices to make sure that your health be in great condition it is a very healthy place :-)! Have a great time there :-)!

name: Jazmín Méndez
text: Love the mongolian hotpot and this location is really good!

name: Logan W.
text: Food was very good, service was very helpful with showing us what a hotpot was and how to use it. Fun if you like playing with your food as-well.. Prices were not bad ether, $25 for two people..

name: ninh PHAM'ily
text: Great place. Way better than the one in Bellaire. Can get super busy in the weekends during the cold winter. Sometimes over salty. Come early. Leave stuffed.

name: Koby Wilbanks
text: Large selection of meats, vegetables, and noodles for hot pot. Fun group experience (as long as you like to eat the same food!). Make sure you get there early as the wait list can get long because most tables take over an hour (minimum) to finish their meal.

name: Suraj Berry
text: We had a party of 7 and all of us had a great time. The staff was helpful and the food was delicious.

name: Daddy McPalmer
text: First time there and I must say I was impressed as well as stuffed.  The meat portions were more than generous and I felt as if I got more than my money’s worth.  I want to go again when I lose all the weight I gained from this visit.

name: Ryan Kinler
text: Food was pretty good, but didn't get a good waiter. Didn't really want to talk to us. The waitress for the next table over was much better and gave us advice on what to order for next time.

name: Jason Fang
text: Skip lunch, and head for Little Sheep! You get three rounds of all you can eat selection, pair it with the Chef special sauces , and you will be a happy camper... with you belly fully and taste buds satisfied.

name: khatrahajur
text: Good place for family hangout with good food...good choices and amazing soup

name: Jay Vargas
text: I tried hot pot for the first time here and I had a great experience! I highly recommend the spicy broth

name: feed back
text:
Must try, go for 50-50 hot new spicy soup.

Lunch Menu 10.99, can't beat that.
you get soup with meat n veggies.
cook ur own food on the table in the boiling soup.

name: lauro leal
text: great

name: Ramon Robles
text: Inexpensive place for lunch.  My 1st time there and I was a bit overwhelmed with the menu.  Our waiter helped a lot and we enjoyed our lunch.

name: Hans Gonzalez
text: Their all you can eat option is the best and if you're not going for it then youre doing something wrong. I recommend trying out everything at least once and see what you like because everything is pretty great

name: Le Minh Chau
text: Good hot pot. Services are nice. However I got some sort of stomach burning after eating

name: Celia Leung
text: Great authentic hot pot spot. We ordered the combo, the portion size and selection are good. Sauce is additional to any meal.

name: Gabe M
text: The new experience at this site is leaps and bounds better than when it was Little Sheep Mongolian. Everything is better, the layout, the food, the broth, and even the service!

name: Hi Li

text:
Mongolian Hot Pot on Westheimer - 4 stars

First time coming here. Five in our group. We were seated within five minutes. Menus were a bit hard to follow. They have combos that you can choose from that include meat, vegetables and a bit of noodles or you can a la carte everything. You can also choose from a variety of soup bases to cook your meat and veggies in. We chose half spicy and half original plus 3 combos to share. The spicy broth was perfect but may be a little too spicy for people who aren't used to heat. The kobe beef, pork belly and seafood all looked fresh. Loved the mushrooms, Napa cabbage and bok choy that came with the combos. The sesame bun does not have meat in it in case you were wondering but was soft on the inside and crispy on the outside. Great place to go with both friends and family. Even better place when it's cold outside.

name: Elijah Edwards
text:
First, let me start, this isn't a bad place.  There's not a lot of places like this out there, so I am excited that we have at least this place. Also, I understand that this is a Chinese restaurant and it's different than what I am used too.  However, living in Japan for several years, we've gotten accustomed to their way of cooking "hot pot."  They call them Shabu-shabu restaurants​,  It's one flat fee (about 25 dollars) and it's all you can eat in an hour and a half.  Two types of rice, chicken curry, dipping sauces, lamb, pork, beef, 5-6 different broths, 7-8 different dipping sauces (all included at no additional charge). They have Ice cream, slushes, alcohol (for more Yen) and a huge salad bar with tons of different veggies, pastas, salads, etc. Understanding where we came from, we had high expectations.

So onto the review:
You are given two base broths,  the house special and spicy.  The house original is kind of bland and is miso based. The spicy is really spicy (warning) but also very good.

They have one dipping sauce that you can dip your veggies or meat in. It's okay.  They do have an​ all you can eat for 30+ dollars as well as a  lunch special, or the combo. I know the lunch special and combo do not include the dipping sauce and pasta.  Those are extra and you are charged more.  It may be included in the all you can eat.

The meats... was awesome! Quality choice cuts, finely sliced that you flash cook were spot on just like in Japan.

If I go back, I'm doing a combo (like tapas) and just ordering meat slices and nothing else.

The service quality is excellent and the items on the menu are very unique. Some of the outdoor sitting area are also equipped with patio heaters. Everyone has the same idea and ordered a started to hold off the hunger pains. Deviled eggs. Well the garnish had more depth than the deviled eggs.  No flavor or imagination.  I debated about getting a drink because of the pricing but ventured out with trying the Prickly Pear.  There were several that order that cocktail. I’m not sure if it was premade but it came back quickly and everyone has a different taste from the same drink.  We gasped by the non-mixture of the cocktail.  I can deal with a boozy drink but this was straight liquor.  I didn’t finish it.  Lastly, I ordered the stuffed brioche toast.  It was fine.  I would have wanted my syrup on the side instead of it already smothering my dish.  It made it soggy. I did enjoy my side of bacon  I added a la cart.  I can get over the meat being blah but I would have wanted my drink to be better.

Lunch is ... well ... it's not good.  Make the mistake of occasionally making it to lunch ... like when visiting the DMA, we walk across, sit down, only to be reminded the lunch menu is current.  Dang it !  You know it's bad when you order the hamburger ... and even that is bad.

Delightful meal. Klyde-Warren is one of the consistently positive things about downtown Dallas and it is enhanced by wonderful and elegant gems like this restaurant. Right in the middle of the main park,  Savor roses above being just a park eatery. It has a charming and comfortable decor,  making the most of its eccentric elongated architecture.
The menu for brunch had a wide variety and food was able without being overloaded. Flavors are subtle and well balanced. The cocktail list is smart and fun and there are a lot of good wines and beers available.
Eating at Savor after strolling(or romping) in the park feels like a civilized,  "old world" thing to do.

We started by being greeted by the host and brought over to a beautiful table with a great view of the park. Our server came and took our order and quickly brought out an appetizer. We ordered the calamari with shrimp which although delicious was a little saltier then we liked so we let our server know and he went above and beyond to make the experience wonderful. He brought out our main course and it was really wonderful as we were finishing up he let us know that he took the calamari off of the bill and had desert (on the house) on its way. We finished the meal with the most amazing banana pudding and chocolate cake that we have had. Edwin made the experience for us and we would be happy to go back.

text: Horrible management.  I sat in the outdoor seating area in Klyde Warren park with my daughter at 7 PM on a Thursday night. I ordered a kettle of French press coffee to share and an appetizer. My friend came to sit with me with food from the park's food trucks. We were asked to leave due to my friends food truck food. I then asked for the check and 2 to go cups for the KETTLE of EXPENSIVE coffee I had. They then brought me one cup. I asked and waited for the second, then I went in and asked for the second  to go cup. The manager then approached me at my table about "the problem you are having". He then had another employee bring me 5 cups, and called me "ludicrous" for allowing my friend's food truck food in. I told him to just let me pay my check and leave,  but he stood over me staring while I signed my check. He definitely came to my table to confront me instead of just letting me leave in peace. The security guard outside of the restaurant in the park said it best, "they are hoity toity".

name: Scott Burdette
text: We made a last night dinner reservation at Savor this past Tuesday night in an attempt to break our trend at eating at the same restaurants. Upon arriving we were impressed with the ceiling to floor glass walls and the bar atmosphere. Our host promptly greeted us and we were seated immediately. The cocktail list was impressive with some twists on the more traditional cocktails most bars in town have. Wine list was also decent, affordable options with nothing on their that would be over the top; however, it would've been nice to have a few more options in Cabs. The food was presented tastefully and the menu possessed an obvious southern spin throughout. Both the wife and I had the maple tenderloin which for its quality was very affordable at $38; it was actually more tender and pleasing than my 32oz Waygu I had at Nick & Sam's a month ago. That being said, what sounds like a nice experience was completely obliterated by a horrible server (per receipt Edwin B). I have worked in the service industry before so I rarely say such as it is usually due to other factors but in this case we were one of three tables in the restaurant by mid meal (i believe the only one to our server) and every request or recheck was pain staking responded to by him. We actually wanted to get desert and a port but it took closet to 20 minutes to get the menu so we refrained knowing the placement of said order would be prolonged further. I'd say this is a nice spot for mid range price-point fine dining but the service would keep us from trying again.

name: Nicole Whistler
text:
Below is the review that I posted and this is my edit:

To the credit of Savor, management responded to my concerns promptly. I was assured that they were taking action to make sure that changes in menu are updated online so that this doesnt happen again. They also offered to take care of my next group visit. They were very professional regarding the prior review, and I'm glad that I can jump to 5 stars because the food was amazing and the atmosphere of the location is exceptional and a must see for anyone planning on visiting klyde Warren park.

Mistakes happen. The professional response is much more in line with the Savor that I have known in the past.

Original review:

I'm struggling to leave this review because first of all, the food was incredible. This is an amazing patio to visit in downtown dallas.

But last night I was going to an event at the Perot, and chose savor as I was in charge of finding a pre event snack and cocktail meet up.

According to their website, savor has a happy hour until 7 on fridays for patio and bar patrons. I told everyone about the specials and I was dead set on a menu item that was
Not even possible.

When we arrived, we weren't offered the happy hour menu, and in the end 3 drinks were purchased that on happy hour would have been less expensive.

When we asked our waitress, she just said that savor changed its menu and it hadnt been updated online. There were issues with availability, for example I was told Manhattan project had closed down...but only kind of. They were out of the backup choice.

My main issue is that I took a group of people here for a promised happy hour menu. One that did not exist. Its embarrassing to have that happen when you've been placed in charge of finding a place for dinner.

Drinks were not discounted and we were there at 615. Menu items online did not match availability or price in the restaurant.

Insult to injury, it said on the site that one must be on patio or bar for happy hour. So I opted for patio even though it was a compromise so that my friends could enjoy the happy hour menu.

I planned an evening for others based on your website and the information provided. I had a friend uncomfortable because of pricing...and I'm the one who put them in the unexpected position. Straighten out the site because I can only see this as a huge problem for your business. You dont want people to be embarrassed that they planned a trip to your restaurant.

Again, food, amazing. False advertisement....huge bummer

-Adam

name: Brian Connery
text:
We came to Savor at about 7;30  on a Friday night and it was moderately busy but emptying out, probably as people headed to events in the nearby Arts District.  Lots of seating was available in both dining rooms, on the patio, or at the bar.  We were seated at a sort of out of the way table in the passage between the two dining rooms, close to the rest rooms.

We shared a Caesar salad to start: yum!  It looks a little spare, especially when spread out into two plates, with the individual romaine leaves fanned out in a circle, lightly covered with parmesan and drizzled with dressing, with warm croutons of fresh fried cornmeal or grits (?).  But it was just right and very tasty.

The entree menu is not extensive: shrimp and grits, a salmon dish, scallops, a chicken dish, a veal dish, and a beef dish or two. I had scallops that were sauced and covered with a variety of savories and came with pureed potatoes: it was terrific, no like anything I've ever had anywhere else.  My partner had the filet, with scalloped potatoes, which she said was perfect.

We also had a side of stir-fried broccolini which was perfectly done -- though the sauce, with its ginger and red pepper seasoning, tasted identical to a sauce I get at the supermarket.

Maybe it was our location between dining rooms, or maybe it was because the bustle of the evening was dying down, but service was generally slow, and we went for relatively long periods of time without seeing our server.  Otherwise, it was a great meal at a reasonable price with a nice view out the windows at the park.

text: Not Good! Not good at all... Went to Savor for the first time with a group of 10 people and everyone sat through the meal in discomfort because the backless seats were terribly awkward. The food was about the same quality that you'd expect from a Chili's or Cheddars except 4x the price. None of the food was fresh. You can tell it's all been frozen and microwaved. While the waitstaff was nice, the service was extremely slow. Didn't matter if we ordered 1 drink or 10, it was at minimum a 10 minute wait. 3 appetizers took 40 mins and they were all awful... We debated whether or not to send them all back. Main entree took well over an hour and left a lot to be desired. They recommend the short rib as the top choice on the menu but it's literally a piece of pot roast with brown gravy on top. I got the shrimp and grits... Bad idea. Shrimp undercooked, grits were decent and the spicy red sauce with sausage that they smothered the entire plate with made it almost inedible. Drinks were ok but also way over priced. There are a ton of bars in the area with much better for less $. All in all, the average cost per person was $100. Next time we'll save the $150 and go to Chili's for this type of food and service.

text: This is Pho Binh opened during the daytime. It's on a corner of a plaza with some limited parking. The broth is often pretty delicious but at times, I've had it taste a bit watered down. The menu is a bit bigger than what it use to be as a hole in wall - large or small bowl. The younger girl server is cute and gave us a smile as she took our order. text: I went a couple times previously and the pho was okay.  I happened to be in the area for lunch and thought I would go back.  I ordered a bowl pho dac biet (combination) and the bowl I received had a fishy smell to it.  I gave it a quick taste it didn't taste like beef broth.  I went ahead and ate it anyways since my lunch break time was ticking.  There would be moments while I was eating it where I would get a hint of fish smell.  So my last visit isn't anything to rave about.  The price isn't bad but on par for what you get.  I'm willing to try this place one more time, but if I get the same experience later, I'm avoiding this place.  There are too many pho options around that I can go to. They should realize this and up their game because they have a lot of competition.

name: Brandy Egege
text:
I received one of their products as a Christmas gift, Gucci Guilty Eau de Toilette. The manufactures price was approximately $98. Purchased it on sale for $$49.49. Total spent at the store was $233.24.

Customer Service:
Called on 2/13/2021 and spoke with assistant manager Samantha. I explained to Samantha that the fragrance I received as a Christmas gift does not last no longer than 30 minutes. I also shared before we went into conversation that I believed she might tell me she will not be able to help me as I had read their policy. I explained the situation to her. She shared unfortunately Gucci scents did not last long and that sales reps at her store normally try to warn their customers of the lack of elasticity of the fragrance. She recommended I purchase a lotion that would help with the spray fragrance and shared beyond that she was sorry that she could not help. Samantha was friendly.

Products:
Many products in store to choose from.

My view:
I don’t want to muddy my view with the engagements of the sales reps at this store with the products sold at the store. I do think the staff are friendly; However, do not expect them to educate you on what your buying. It is a business-the goal is to make a profit. What one has to decide is how to make that profit: 1) By building loyal customers who would return based off good products and good customer service. 2) Customers buying a product under the wrong understanding of what they are buying. As a result, an unhappy customer that have spent their hard earned COVID money on useless products that look pretty but does not serve its intended purpose-to smell nice. (One sale customer who may not return)

CONCLUSION:
I don’t recommend the products from this store.

text:
Definitely a great first impression park. Lots to do, nice views and well maintained.

Well, after another visit or two, you begin to realize the effects of overuse and neglect.

Trash is everywhere after game days, and cockroaches infest overflowing trash cans. Water fowl leave their fair share behind as well.

I want to want frequent this park, but there are others, closer to home and better maintained (McGrath in Meadow's Place) to spend time at.

If Pokemon is your thing, there are over 10 PokeStops here, spread out amongst the fields, with the minority behind on the actual trails.

Not a terrible place to relax, but you can do better than Eldridge Park.

Pilar Hernandez
text: Awesome experience. Met great people. Got great products. I made those chocolates with some goodies I bought there. More chocolates to be made 😅 soon.

name: Ann La
text:
A great way to start off your weekend at the farmers market. They open early from 8am-12pm every Saturday. Get here early for good parking. There is a parking lot near a building, a short walking distance to the farmers market. I like that this farmers market is chill and small.

There is live music with a few tables. You can grab some food as you shop and enjoy the music. There are a variety of vendors here from fresh produce, fruits, meat, coffee, sweets, plants, to beverages such as organic juices and wines. Most let you sample the products before buying.

There are also food trucks around and a pottery making on the spot for a good charity. Everyone is very friendly and welcoming. I enjoy the casual and easy-going vibe here. Overall, an easy and fun activity for the weekend especially if you love fresh produce and organic products. Most vendors do accept cards.

name: Amy Miller
text: It will be incredible when no masks are required to be outdoors. However, I love the vendors at this place.🌟

name: Emily Philpot
text: Pleasantly surprised by the quality of winter produce and the amount of vendors with ready made product. So many of the vendors were friendly and willing to discuss their product, sourcing, and suggest methods for use.

name: Chiem A
text: I go here to get local honey usually. Lots of fresh veggies and locally made dips, bread etc. Also a bunch of stands with organic meat. There arefood trucks here as well.

name: Carlos Ramirez
text: Large farmer's market in the shadows of St John's School, home of some famous alumni like Wes Anderson, Christy Haubegger, Benjamin Moser and others. The market itself has many rows of local vendors and a decent layout.  Parking is in a convenient multi-level structure.  Notably, there weren't any Keto vendors the Saturday I attended.  This Saturday market closes at Noon. Looking forward to my next visit.

name: Olivia Maynard
text: I love it. So many great vendors and delicious food.  I go several times a month.  Nest pimento cheese in Houston for sure.

name: Qimar Alfasi
text: Everything here is amazing. The honey the mushrooms  the coffee. Wow

name: Fumi Balogun
text:
Very cool and inspiring famers market in Houston! I learned about this through a Yelp Elite event invite and I was so shocked I didn’t already know about this. This farmer’s market is held every Saturday from 8am-noon. I visited for the first time yesterday and was impressed with how organized everything was especially with COVID-19 precautions in place (no mask, no entry of-course). Parking was well organized, and the lines moved smoothly and quickly. No trouble at all finding parking.

The market itself is such an uplifting environment in an open space with so many different local vendors including cooked meals, produce, plants, fresh juice, ice cream, cheese, and so much more! I thought it was interesting and cool that they also partner with SNAP so everyone is welcome and provided with the opportunity to purchase locally farmed food!

This is definitely a great place to come to stock up on clean groceries or just hang with friends or family. I really liked that each of the vendors I purchased from (The Baker’s Man & Local Fruits) had Samsung Pay. I look forward to coming back and absolutely recommend a visit.

name: Michael Fulmer
text: Plenty of parking. A great resource for local/Texas products (mostly food related), look for new vendors throughout the year. Very well organized & run.

name: Chris Kvistad
text: Great variety of vendors. Always seemed to be ample parking with the parking garage right there. The parking garage can get a bit tight for larger vehicles to maneuver.

name: michael perkins
text: Haven’t had fresh until you’ve had farm fresh.

name: Holly Walrath
text: Now this is a true farmers market! This place has about 6-7 veggie and fruit vendors. There were a huge amount of total vendors - maybe over a 100. Lots of selection from local plants to bbq to steak meat and kombucha. We got some to-go dumplings that were to die for. NOT dog friendly though- which I get because they serve food. You can’t take your dog here. Parking is in a garage right next door. Very accessible. My only complaint is it’s so far from me!

name: Ms. Mercy
text: Love love love this place! I go every other weekend to get my vegan treats and fresh vegetables and fruits! The food trucks are always good! They’re changing locations on September 22 and I’m excited to see the new place! Especially with more parking spaces!

name: Brian TheFlorist
text:
MORE THAN A FARMERS MARKET
This is a wonderful destination for foodies to explore.
✅Beautiful fresh produce.
✅Culinary products such as local Honey, cheeses, meats,infused oils, fresh cut flowers and a few veggie plants.
✅♿ High accessibility to the vendors.
✅There's also food 🚚 trucks all assembled into a courtyard type atmosphere.
It's complete with limited seating and a performance stage area.
An enjoyable weekend morning stop.
MUST SEE 👀.

name: Christopher Roza
text: I’ll give it 3 star for now. There is an abundance of vendors but no product really stood out to me. I came at a bad time during the season because most of the fall produce was not ready yet. I’m planning to give it a second chance in a month, when more produce should be available.

name: Tommy Bahama Texas
text: Great vendors! Lot of Fresh produce! Best Houston farmers market for chefs.

name: Brandon Toppass
text: Cool place with local growers. Sauerkraut and local mushrooms stole the show for me.

name: Josh Eidenberg
text: This is our favorite Saturday farmers market in Houston. Vendors are so friendly. The food is incredible. You really have a lot of variety from freshly baked breads, to seafood from the gulf, eggs, soups, cold pressed juices, dumplings, organic produce and so much more. Every week we come to urban harvest there is always something new for us to enjoy

name: Victor Hoffman
text: This farmers market has lots of fresh veggies. The vendors are nice here. Sometimes I see some exotic fruits here and little be pricey.  The parking is good here.

name: Kristin Citan
text: The venders are so friendly and careful.  It feels very safe to pick up fresh food and enjoy the environment.

name: Jim Griggs
text: Fun vendors with great products. Like stepping back to the 60s and 70s.

name: Jon O'Bryan
text: Easy parking, friendly crowd and vendors, and tasty food. Prices are on par with what you'd expect for a typical farmers market.

name: Tony APA
text: Large number of vendors, great range of offerings, great atmosphere, not too crowded (at least when we've been)...will go back often.

name: Tracy N. Harris
text: Nice to see so many vendors. I got there @ 11am. Many were sold out.

name: Jonathan VandenBerg
text: Went to the farmers market this morning with my baby boy and mother. Enjoyed the atmosphere with music, fresh produce and tasty treats including dumplings and a great almond chocolate croissant. It was a beautiful day and many people roaming around. Greta spot to watch beautiful people picking up some fresh but moderately expensive farm to table treats! The venders are all so friendly. Especially enjoy the stand with different varieties of mushrooms!

name: Anita Morton
text: Really had a good time. Very interesting place.

name: Baran Koç
text: Nice farmers market with fresh veggies and fruits as well as some artisanal food items. Limited number of vendors with overpriced items.

name: Thomas Traynor
text: There are always a wide variety of vendors with lots of fresh produce, bread, flowers and more!

name: Mollie Gilthorpe
text: Favorite farmers market. Willing to drive 45 minutes. Great variety.

name: Lauren Gayden
text: Great variety high quality products! You can't miss out on Cake and Bacon bread, Bee 2 Bee honey and finally got to try Feges BBQ!

name: Amariee Collins
text: Very nice people and growers. They even take SNAP now and will double your snap!

name: its_bum _brie
text: Great products! There are food trucks and lots of booths with delicious foods to try and of course buy.

name: Yosdee Arenas
text: Lots of vendors, food, & coffee! You really should check it out if you want fresh produce, eggs, honey, stuff like that. Pretty much all the vendors are very friendly. Make sure to get there when it just opened so you can get what you need with not so many people!

name: Ajit Vyas
text: Nice Farmers market off of Westheimer. Easy free garage parking. About 40 food and produce vendors. Small area with tables to eat plus live music. Looking forward to checking it out again.

name: Diane Pitchford
text: Although I'm a certified raw food chef, impressed and delighted about being able to get fermented and sprouted foods without all the muss and fuss in my kitchen. Love this place.

name: Stef P
text: This farmers market is probably the best one right now in Houston. There are quite a few stands that have a variety of merchandise to choose from such as produce, flowers, and meat. They have a couple food trucks and some stands serving cooked food. Some of the stands do overprice and you have to know your prices to find the good deals. It’s a nice way to spend a Saturday morning, but it can get a bit crowded. I would love to see the market get bigger. I would probably go back again.

name: Jenny Low
text: Should go if you like fresh foods!

name: Saloumeh Ebrahimzadeh
text: Love this market! My Saturday routine the food selection, the veggies, bread and baked goods are really good.

name: Rita
text: Of course local fresh foods are the best so where better to go than this place. Parking isnt the best but only because i dislike parking garages but its still pretty close. Just remember that the early bird catches the worm. The later you wait, the less the vendors will have left in variety of things. 8am-12pm. Tons of veggies. Main fruit was strawberries, fresh eggs, fresh meats and great food trucks.

name: JG
text: So many great choices from vegetables, meats, honey, breads and more.

name: sophia clarke
text: One of the best comprehensive farmers market in Houston.

name: Hannah Chen
text:
Easy parking situation with the parking garage. Currently four-legged friend admission is on "paws"

As for vendors-- wide variety from produce to prepared foods as well as health products, pet food, flowers as well as a knife sharpener. Pictured: Bread Man Co. Bakery (Everything Cretzel), Artisana Bakery-- haven't tried a single thing I didn't like, and she rotates through lots of different breads and pastries, from 'proper British scones' to a dark chocolate/candied orange peel filled brioche bun I tried today. Also got a veggie pie from Relished West African foods-- haha she was incredulous we could handle her spicy sauce, but it was good! Altough the pie was certainly well-seasoned enough to go without it :)

name: Sean Parker
text: Great experience, great vendors, good food, great prices 😄

name: Emily Su
text: Great selection of food and produce that are reasonably priced. Lots of vegetarian choices and organic and sustainable products. Easy parking. Nice way to start off the weekend!

name: Nic
text:
It's great that they have a lot of cruelty free products, but it would be nice to not have to sift through all the cruelty products.
The definition of three stars. It's just okay.

name: Abdul majeed Abid
text:
It was one of the best farmers markets that i’ve been to, in Texas. It has everything from freshly-made breakfast (choice between tacos and omelettes and falafel sandwiches) to farm-fresh eggs, vegetables, salsa, macaroons, coffee/tea and much else. It is well worth a visit on a Saturday morning.

On my second visit, i bought some tomatoes and jalapeños (to make salsa) alongside organic eggs and pickled vegetables. My partner and I had extra-yummy goat-milk popsicles at the market.

name: Joe DeReuil
text: Lotta good stuff

name: Rozina Kara
text: Always the best finds at this market, support your local farmers!

name: Ben Mescher
text: Our favorite farmers market in all of Houston.

name: Nancy Salazar
text: Great vibes! The organic veggies always the best!

name: OnionComb
text: They had a lot of different things but it was a lot smaller than I had imagined. I saw some giant roof structures in photos I didn't see when I was there. It seemed as if a lot less vendors went on that day. Still they had a great amount of different things to get. Hoping to purchase some meat next time I visit.

name: Hazel Shaughnessy
text: Wonderful organic and some conventionally  grown vegetables. Grass fed beef. Eggs. Jellies and other homemade items. Longstanding market. Highly recommend.

name: Kathleen Milligan Manuel
text: This place is simply awesome!!  I love going to see what they have.

name: Lauren Keefer
text: One of the better Farmer’s markets I’ve ever been to! A wide variety of locally sourced foods are available and they bring in food trucks as well. It’s best to go early, as lots of things will sell out by 10am. Plus, parking can be tough as it gets busier.

name: Denise Ereka Peterson
text: This farmer's market requires locally grown products and does not allow vendors who are selling products that are not locally made

name: Sammy Peters
text: I enjoyed this place. A lot if options. Nice people. Good eats and coffee. Bring a wagon or cart if you're really here to buy a lot.

name: mollie g
text: They have almost anything you need. Lots of produce options and tasty places to eat from while you shop.

name: Jon Bradshaw
text: First timer it was wonderful especially to be out of the house.

name: Mark Feferman
text: Love this place every Saturday.

name: Beli Z
text:
We have been going to the Farmer’s Market for quite a while now (I fostered and adopted from one of the pet rescues that went there), but had a bit of a lull. So when we went back at the beginning of the year we were so excited to see the new location...parking is so easy now!!!!!! This was everything!

Aside from location, we love that we can grab coffee and breakfast before we purchase the goodies from local farmers. There’s a band usually playing, which is always nice!

Lines aren’t usually ever overwhelmingly long so if you want to do a quick trip you can. Going early also ensures that you get everything that you need! Otherwise, you could ask the vendors if you can pre-order. Some of them will allow for that! We do it for our whole chicken.

name: Chuck Graham
text: Urban Harvest is a farmer's market. The Gulf Coast Woodturners were invited to demonstrate turning wood bowls in conjunction with Empty Bowls which benefits the Houston Food Bank.

name: Alexander Beck
text: One of the best farmer's markets in Houston, basically a full grocery store but all local and organic food!!

name: Ida Diamond
text: Love this place. Yes, it's pricey, but what price do you place on health and wellness? There are beautiful veggies, herbs and fruit, yummy food items (bakery goods, cured meats, cheeses, beef, pork, chicken, lamb, fish, eggs, breakfast bowls, tacos, smoothies, gourmet coffees), plants (fruit trees, vegetables and herbs), and even pet items. Everyone is easy going, informative and friendly. The only problem is parking; if you get there after 8:20am.....good luck.

name: Dave Ohmer
text: Little bit of everything. Coffee, food to eat there, locally raised meats and produce, cheese, pecans +++. Brisket Kolache at 3 Sisters farms are outstanding. Like the new location.

name: John Bemis
text: Not a humongous market, but a better than average selection of actual produce vendors with a good selection of vegetables and fruit, everything I saw was at least plausibly local in origin.   There was a small but varied selection of food vendors.  Approximately a half dozen vendors offering organic/exotic meat and a smattering of others selling cheese, plants, honey etc.

name: j l
text: It's an ok farmers market. They should try to get more food venders and different venders in general.

name: Alex Agne
text: Best farmers market in Houston without a doubt. The new location really suits them well, and there were more vendors, more people, and better parking. I love strolling around the stalls and sampling a lot of food. Also a great spot to do focused or general produce shopping as well. Live music and several places to sit down and eat.

name: Sue Wittie
text: Great fresh local food, music, bread, fresh flowers, vegetables,  fruit, and an ability to help local farmers make this Saturday morning outing a treat. I see people I know, have a chance to see a local chef show how to use what's fresh, and leave with a sense of community. Saturday morning at Urban Harvest is special.

name: Jonathan Clemmer
text: Nicely spread out so no crowding. Nearby (free) parking deck. Great variety of vendors and lots of produce. Even on a cool windy wet morning they were doing a good business.

name: C Lynn
text: Always a great experience. Be sure to go early so your favorite vendors don't run out of what you need! Some vendors are on a rotation, which is nice, helps change things up a bit.

name: Luis Perez
text: Great selection of produce, food trucks and stands, and tons of honey. Dogs welcome!

name: Andrew Yarov
text: Everything is so good and fresh. Great meats, fruits and vegetables. Bought cuts of Bison there and it was the best. Will be going back for more.

name: Sherrelle Thomas
text: Great venders. Very clean and safe.

name: Andy Pham
text: Lots of vendors, good parking lot. Lots of farm products you can get in here. From veggies to chickens.

name: Zack Carballo
text: Great amount of food and fresh local produce. Make sure to bring cash just in case vendors may not accept card. There is an ATM on the premise, but I'd recommend getting cash before hand.

name: Carrie Haley
text: This was my first time at the new location on Buffalo Speedway.  The parking area/Garage is very nice.  Ample parking.  Easy access.  I plan to visit more often.  I always find what I am looking for and learn about and try new vendors.  I love shopping here.  I have my favorite vendors.  I recommend shopping here.

name: Christopher Rhodes
text: Best farmer's market in the entire city, hands down. From fruit and vegetables to wine and fresh flowers, this place almost literally has everything that you're hunting for. Also, as a bonus, some of the nicest people in the history of life front the stands.

name: Christine Beck
text: I enjoy coming out to this farmers market. Plenty of farm fresh veggies, meats and eggs. Soaps, oils, raw honey and plants too. Lots of organic foods-raw and also prepared. Indian food, coffee drinks, breakfast tacos, baked goods etc. Live music. Most are the same venders week after week.

name: Shannon Snider
text: Great neighborhood farmers market!  And if you know your local chefs, chances are you will see quite a few there on Saturday morning getting their products and inspiration for the week!  In addition to locally grown veggies (all within 180 miles) you can get cheeses, meats, pastries, flowers, plants, and novelties.  Don't worry about trying to get your coffee and breakfast before you get there - they have several delicious options and tables to sit down and enjoy some live music.  Definitely bring a bag (or two) along to help haul all your goodies.  Parking across the street is open to the public.

name: Glenda Reyes
text: Love the selection of things being sold (fruit, veggies, coffee, Popsicles, beauty products wild flowers and more). If you get there early it is not as packed. However it's not as big as I expected. Awesome experience though!

name: Eddie Rivera
text: Pretty awesome place. Lots of different, delicious produce. Selection of herbs is limited and pricy tho so you may need to end up hitting a grocery anyway. Love the seafood stall (air shipped from the gulf; fresh never frozen) as it is fresh and prices are reasonable.

name: Cynthia Marie Cardiff
text: Great Farmer's Market!  Lots of fresh, locally grown food!  Friendly vendors and great food trucks!

name: Douglas Jones
text:
The parking was free and nice and alot of vegan selections....Love it....
Doug aka Fresh

name: Lisa Miller
text: Great little farmer's market. Had a nice mix of fresh veggies and meat and some delicious food to buy!

name: Monique Vu
text: I've always been a fan of this famers market, but this new location and set up is a million times better. Better parking and more vendors and restrooms! This is my favorite Saturday morning brunch option.

name: Kirill Volguin
text: Good food, produce, music and vibes. Make sure to visit all the vendors they each have something amazing to offer you’ll find nowhere else!

name: Emily Hinson
text: Love this place. Lots of options to choose from for produce, lots of dogs everywhere, everyone is very nice.

name: Christina Yim
text: It's a pretty nice farmers market. Can get really packed and there's hardly any parking if you arrive after 9ish. Even around 8:30am it's already kind of packed. So arrive early!!! Open from 8am-12pm on Saturdays. Family friendly. Dog friendly as well. Handicapped parking available. 🙂

name: J C
text: Good market.  Wish there were more veggie seller though.  Things sell out.  Go early.  Good food options too , so eat breakfast or lunch here.

name: Phat Deez
text: Dont like the looks people give me.  But hey,  we're in the south

name: Kristen Brockman
text: Love the farmers here, great produce, great selection of meats, breads, juices, etc.

name: Michal Houston
text: I always love my Saturday morning visits to the farmers market. The Urban Harvest market has a great variety of veggies, proteins, cheeses, sweets and flowers. Great one stop shop!

name: Joshua Adams
text: When I first moved to Houston, I tried to find a farmer's market like the one I frequented in North Tonawanda, NY. The Urban Harvest Farmer's Market is just excellent. I love having the options of so many local farmers and vendors along with food trucks for a great breakfast or early lunch. From meats and cheese, eggs, vegetables and fruits and much more, the market has quite a variety. I make it a point to purchase all of my local honey from the market. Anyone living in the loop should consider coming at least once a season!

name: TROB TROB
text: Celebrity cited this morning and also Tyler is the greatest farmers market director ever!!!!-Thomas

name: Michelle Monaco
text: It's a lovely market with lots of great vendors but I'm disappointed they've recently put a ban on bringing dogs.

name: Jason Cook
text: One of my favorite farmers markets in the city. We try to go every 2 weeks. On Saturday mornings they have live music, great coffee and the vendors are super friendly and have brought their best farm to table. I love this spot.

name: David Biniek
text: Good produce. Good amount of meats. Some sweets, some cheeses. The breakfast tents are all super good. And of course some good coffee and a cold brew place.

name: Michael Jeter
text: Wonderful fresh food, including hot food for breakfast, courteous helpful, merchants.

name: Brad Wright
text: A great small, farmers market great for fresh produce and meats, as well as wide variety of food and drink for sale. A great way to spend a Saturday morning.

name: anshul prakash
text: Small but an amazing place to start your Saturday! Lots of options to eat, drink and buy veggies.. Also great live music!

name: Renae Rainman
text: Thank goodness they are moving to a new location next week at St John's School. Parking at the Eastside market is practically impossible. The neighboring business keeps squeezing farmers and merchants into a smaller area.

name: Kathryn Hatfield
text: Great market with seasonal produce as well as lots of prepared food and EXCELLENT breakfast options. Things change pretty regularly so if you go with your heart set on something specific you may be disappointed - but if you go to see what there is and get something fun, you'll probably do fine :)

name: Marvin Freedman
text: This is a wonderful farmers market for great fruit and vegetables.  I haven't tried the seafood, but plan on it for my next visit cause I've only heard good things. Conveniently located in the upper Kirby area.

name: Melissa Murphy
text: Great variety of vendors to meet your produce and local food needs. Parking can be challenging so get there early.  Some prepared foods and coffee available.  Minimal seating available.  Live entertainment for ambiance is nice!

name: Diksha
text: A very nice and vibrant market

name: Taryn Hryc
text: Adorable vendors who offer cheese, eggs, veggies (not so much fruit as you'd think), meats, coffee, juices, flowers and more. Love starting off the Saturday morning here. Get there early, parking fills up fast.

name: Sheryl Winters
text: Great marketThe dumplings are the best they cook them in front of you The   crepes which are next to the dumpling stand are wonderful

name: Amy Quinn
text: A great way to grab a coffee, hang with friends, talk with local farmers and business owners. Not too big and not too crowded. I always get some staples here, try the infused olive oils!

name: Nicholas Lockhart
text: Great variety! Come for a wide selection of local and seasonal veggies, grass fed meats, eggs, baked goods and flowers! Love this place!

name: Claudio Cairoli
text: We try to go there every week, most of the times we get breakfast there too. There is a good variety of vendors, and we tend to get all of our meat and fish from here, so that we can get them directly from the farmers. Lira Rossa for cheese is great.

name: Marco Miguel
text: Great food and ambiance, prices are not low.

name: April Williams
text: Very pleasant with a plethora of options to choose from

name: Lori Johnson
text: Gotta get there early as stuff does tend to sell out rather quickly!

name: Alex Hancock
text: Love this market! Great options for all your needs: seasonal organic and conventional fruits and veggies, locally raised meats of all varieties, eggs, pre-prepared foods (from breads to salads to more) from a variety of foodways, ferments, desserts... everything!

name: Holly Feray
text: I love this place.  I can so easily overspend!  The vendors are wonderful, kind, and amazing.

name: Mik Hastur
text: Love shopping here

name: Victoria Tom
text: Cute little farmers market with all the basics! I've always found street parking with no problem. I regularly get the quiche at the stall on the left side that also sells omelettes.

name: Judy Shilling
text: Lots of fresh organic produce, fruits and meat, including bone broth and honey.  Entertainment while you shop and food trucks.  8 to 12 on Sat. Mornings ONLY, on Buffalo Speedway and Westheimer.(new location 2019)

name: L G
text: Great place for fresh fruits veggies meats and food

name: S Walters
text: I love the fresh greens, and farm produce. The home made items are always a treat. Remind me of my island home with local produce. LOVE IT!

name: Greg Buchold
text: This is the oldest and biggest farmer's market in Houston. It offers the most variety of pastured meat products, organic and local vegetables, plants, prepared foods, . Saturdays typically offer chef and master gardener demonstrations as well as live music. The venue is child- and pet-friendly. At peak times of the year parking can be a challenge and requires being aware of the spaces reserved for non-market visitors. Overall I like the market; my biggest criticisms are the predominance of prepared food over fresh vegetables and fruit, the high meat prices, and the lack of a farm tour to get to know the farmers. The market is situated very close to the offices of a large number of environmental advocacy groups and those connections benefit the market patrons.

name: Benjamin Craft-Rendon
text: Having gone to this farmers market for years, I've been a tad surprised by the growing number of ready-to-eat items but remain happy with its wide selection of staples. From mushrooms to greens to eggs to goat cheese, multiple vendors are present for almost everything. This encourages exploration and gives more chances for compatible people to find one another. Definitely recommend.

name: Kelly Turnage
text: I love this market they have a great selection of vegstables and lots of other goodys. You can also have breakfast and there is usually a band. Sometimes parking is hard because of road work.

name: Terry Schweitzer
text: Great selection of locally grown produce and other local items, include breads, sweet treats & cheese. Also great place to find breakfast.

name: Tina Zelaya
text: Enjoyable stroll. Great produce

name: Matt Duran
text: My first experience with this venue. Lots of fresh vegetables, knife sharpening, bought some plants and great fruit trucks.  There was even live entertainment.  There was more offered!

name: John Gilmore
text: Wonderful market and vendors. Great variety.

name: Stephanie Castillo
text: Love this little Farmer Market in the middle of busy life happening.

name: jess motter
text: Want a farmers market in the city? This is it!

name: Lauren Aragon
text: Its a fairly small farmers market but we found some delicious figs from one of the farm stands.  Would love it if there were more craft type vendors and more variety in the produce.

name: Tiffani Aswad
text: I love this farmer's market. Great produce, food and music. All around a great time!

name: Bullfrog 92020
text: Really nice place! Great vendors and quality products. Everyone was really nice.

name: Ken Smith
text: Fresh

name: Frederico Lundgren
text: Good selection of vegetables, family oriented. Some good “food trucks”. Definitely worth a visit...

name: William Higgins
text: Gudbelly + coffee is some of the best morning combination I've found. Really like going to this little market, and being able to find vegan/vegetarian options all over.

name: glenn austerfield
text: Great for getting locally produced products.  I got duck eggs,  ground lamb,  and local honey just to name a few of the things available.  Live music too.   Not a huge market,  but enough vendors to make a morning out of it.

name: DJ Tex
text: Excellent!

name: Jacob A
text: First time visit. Was pretty neat and inviting. Wish they had more vendor stalls,  but I'm sure that'd come over time.

name: Ravi Deva
text: Very pricey. Interesting looking vegetables that are unlikely to be seen in stores. Bought some radishes at a ridiculous price and they weren't even juicy! The only reason I would go there again is to buy bread.

name: Shutterbug. dean
text: It was nice but hopefully they will get bigger. It was a small market with alot of the same vegetables. I would've liked to see more fruits.

name: Kate Nilsen
text:
This farmer's market has a pretty good variety of vendors -- from organic veggies to soap and candle makers, to dairy products, meat and prepared foods. Parking is pretty much a zoo, but once you park, you're able to walk around a parking lot full of interesting vendors.

I also saw several families just hanging out with their kids. There's live music, food and coffee. One last note: no dogs allowed. A wise call. It is kinda close quarters in the walkways so I could imagine the issues with skittish dogs or a canine skirmish.

name: Onnie Fletcher
text: Great place to buy fresh fruit and vegetables and much more.
