name: AJ Ramirez
text:
I've had the opportunity to stay at Hilton locations in numerous countries across multiple continents. However, I was a bit disappointed in my stay here for several reasons that hopefully they address in the near future.

PROS:
- The staff was very friendly and accommodating.
- The view is the best available in the area, specifically with the Eastern facing room that overlooks the marina and has the chance to catch the beautiful sunrise.
- Location is close to restaurants, activities, and has ample parking.
- Facilities are clean, restaurants are updated, and the grounds are well-groomed.
- The staff immediately took action when we smelled our neighbors smoking in their room (it came into our room through the adjoining door).
- Beds were comfortable (we brought our own pillows).

CONS:
- Probably my biggest complaint was the mold in the room. I had trouble breathing for the entirety of my stay, and the room smelled like we were staying in an old, damp basement.
- Bathroom did not have a fan, contributing to the moisture problem each time we took a shower.
- Humidity in the room meant that the sheets felt wet, which was disconcerting and made for a clammy sleep.
- The struts for the soft-close doors were clearly in need of replacement throughout our floor - doors were unintentionally and very audibly slamming, which makes for disrupted sleep.
- Rooms are outdated and a little the worse for wear. Cabinets are chipped and warped. Shower fixtures were old and had hard water and mildew stains.
- The food at the restaurant was both confusing and disappointing. I ordered crab cakes with aioli and what came out was... well... I have no idea. It was certainly crab, but we jokingly called them "splatties" instead of patties. It was essentially two crab pancakes that were falling apart sitting in what appeared to be a spicy marinara, coupled with a bowl of (frozen) microwaved/steamed veggies that were sadder than a public school lunch. Everything was incredibly mushy.
- There wasn't an ice or vending machine on our floor - we were told to go to the lobby.
- The televisions are old, cable quality was poor, and the use was more difficult than anyone traveling wants. Many of the small selection of channels only worked periodically (stating "no signal" when they didn't feel like coming in), while changing the channel was a practice in patience that required careful pointing and a single press, wait a few seconds, press again, wait again. The sleep timer didn't work. I'm not a big TV watcher, but even to turn it on for background noise was an irritating experience.
- The bartender was oddly uninviting. Rather than feeling welcomed, I felt tolerated. Everyone has off days but, after he patronizingly questioned my choice in cocktail like I was an overzealous toddler asking for an adult drink ("Are you sure? Have you ever had one of those before?"), I got the impression that maybe that's just his personality. Or maybe he was trying to warn me, because the drinks were mediocre. Who knows.

ADDITIONAL COMMENTS:
- It would be nice to have a microwave in the room, which could easily be added if the fridge was smaller.
- Add USB charging outlets to the room - most hotels I've been to have them now.
- The bar is way too limited for being a hotel on the water and by a marina. No blender? You're cutting yourself off from an entire segment of the population that loves frozen drinks on a hot, humid day... which Houston has in spades.
- Add umbrellas or covered seating to the pool area.
- Move the smoking areas a little bit away from the entry doors. Every time we entered we were walking through smoke.

text: Nice at first glance, but needs improvements. The building is obviously very old, which is fine, but they seem to have gotten behind on maintaining several things. The carpet felt damp and the room smelled slightly like mildew. The restroom was updated recently, but the work was rushed. Paint job, especially on the ceiling, was uncompleted. You could see roller marks and that a second coat was needed. The most alarming issue was the shower. The water got scolding hot when it was in the middle of hot and cold. So I leaned more towards cold and got in. As I showered, the water flow hesitated about six times and when it would come back it came out scolding hot again. I had to jump out of the way until it went back to normal. Fortunately, I love a hot shower but I fear for the day a child is showering or what have you. Now, the staff at the hotel were all very pleasant and helpful. They even brought us a sewing kit when I called to see if they had one since I ripped my dress. The beds were lovely. The views are beautiful. Overall a good experience for my quick trip.

text: Amazing customer service!!! This is the best place to stay!! My parents got turned away from Holiday Inn after a 3 hr drive on their 27th anniversary! Due to forgetting a credit card at home but having cash in hand and reservations! Holiday inn wouldn’t even allow me to pay for the room with my card and keep all my info on file, plus my parents pay cash upfront. After complete rudeness and no help my parents walked out thinking they would face this at all locations in Kemah area and their anniversary would be spent on the road. Devistated, I started calling around. Hilton NASA was my second call. Maricella at the front desk and Viri Flores manager on duty saved the day!! Not only did they send me an authorization form and let me pay for my parents vacation!! They did a full upgrade and placed them in a suit FOR FREE!!  Maricella at the front desk made sure they had any and EVERYTHING they could need! A wonderful lake view, robes & slippers,  gourmet chocolates, water before they stepped away from the desk!! Then (OH YES ITS NOT OVER) once they made it to the room. They called to check on them and advised they would be giving them full access to the pent house and drinks included!! This place is amazing! The customer service Maricella provided was beyond amazing!! She took care of my parents like she was there just for them! She let them know when she would and wouldnt be there as well as who else they can call for ANYTHING they needed this weekend!! I’ve wrote a book and I still can’t say how amazing this place and their staff are!! This is true customer service and true hospitality. I will send EVERYONE I know here including myself. These ladies are truly angels and the people that allow them the power to make such decisions are just as awesome!! They have the right idea and will be in business for years to come if they continue like this!! Thank you again!!!

We left and the checked our reservation confirmation and verified it was a king deluxe room.  When we returned and talked to another front desk clerk we were told that this hotel was overbooked and we were bumped to a lesser  (deluxe two double room). That clerk offered to comp us a free breakfast.

It's not the overbooking, it's the initial lie that pushed the fault onto Expedia from the first clerk. If we knew the error upfront there wouldn't be an issue.

Beds were uncomfortable,  but honestly nothing feels as comfortable as our home mattress.

This is a disgrace in my wonderful city of Houston!!! They do not make the $$ to drop that much  on a room for a few hours. I sent a message to them, this was their response. I'm disgusted. Please share this!!! I'm beyond mad right now! #houstonhilton #nasahilton #hurricaneharvey #hiltonhotel #cajunnavy #harveyfirstresponders #houstonpolicedepartment

text:
I was aware of this particular Chick-fil-A for years but never visited the place until some students of mine give me a gift card for the place.  I went and was pleasantly surprised!  It's not the usual fast food joint.  The decor was inviting and the food was tasty and seemed much fresher than most other fast diners.  The chicken, (their speciality) did not taste like it had all the usual fillers and food substitute products found at some places.
Imagine a place with more actual food and not 50% food like products!  The portions were good sized too.  They certainly live up to their reputation!  Needless to say I kept coming back after that. The servers and cashiers have always been friendly, courteous, responsive, and almost always had a smile for their customers too.  Its been about 4 years now and they are just as good with updated quality offerings and service.

name: Philip Quan
text:
This place I believed opened in 2000, but looks much older with its 90's pastel and white toned colour pallette. The pandemic forced the owners to clean the market and the mall dramatically. It was actually cleaned throughly for the firat time. The floors are not dingy and the foul smell of rotting garbage around the produce area is mostly gone. Restrooms in here and the mall are now resonably clean and lack the smell of stale urine that has plagued many a patron in the past. Much better enviroment right now.

Now this is the largest asian grocery in the area with wide variety of produce, meat, seafood and goods that cant be found anywhere else. This may be intimidating, but if you have the time, you will find many a item that may be interest you.

Quick of tibits about this place

The asian vegtables sold here are typically locally grown some quite literally in people's backyards. Just humble families earning extra money. No virtue signalling here.

There is a abandoned expansion in the back, rumor is that the owner lost a signicant amount of money due to embezzlement by a familiy member amd had to put the the project on hold indefinitely.

name: Shawn Nguyen
text:
Good market for all the unique hard to find needs for the Asian kitchen & garden (plants to grow at home, from fruit bearing to ornamental).

Some highlights:
-Large fish market.
-Large fruit and vegetable selection.
-You Can buy bags of bones for making soup broth.
-Large selection of Asian dishwear (from cheap plastic to very nice Japanese, and anywhere in between).

Tip: be prepared to wait a long time at the fish/seafood section. They have a team of people working the fish with a larger crowding in demand, so you will take a number at the obscure hard to spot kiosk that is on a support beam next to the frozen section, and then wait a long time looking at the obscure LED sign on the back wall behind where the men work preparing the fish. Going as a team is recommended - one person taking a number to wait for fish, and the other person continuing the shopping. Also, I like to grab two numbers; much later on in my wait, when an elderly person walks up wishing for fish, I give them one of the numbers, so they won't have to stand and wait as long as the rest of us ;-) Bless someone's day.

I'd give them a fifth star if 1) they had people anywhere on the floor of the store to actually help you; there are typically no employees in any identifying clothing to be found, so you're on your own to fend for yourself in the massive store, and 2) if they would keep the store cleaner. Those are my only two "gripes".

The food here looks and feels fresh and good, and everything is organized into categories that make sense. Drinks leads to chips leads to jerky leads to cookies leads to spices leads to canned food, and so on. They even have a dedicated candy aisle, and the potted plants (only some of which are decorative) are right inside the entryway so you walk through a calming jungle of peacefully nodding leaves as the overhead a/c blows the summer heat off of you.

Wonderful store, will definitely be back. I absolutely found everything I went in looking for, as nothing was out of stock and the variety was on point.

name: Big Boi
text: Baytown Nature Center was great if you are a salt water fisherman. I mainly do fresh water. But I had a great time. I would say cast as far as you can. There is alot of stuff in the water to get caught up on. A boat or canoe would be really great to go out past all the rocks and stuff. Overall it is a nice area, good for family, BBQ, or just kicking it with friends. Good for kids, they have a playground. Fresh air, clean, Porto potties so take appropriate items. 4 stars because of the fishing from the bank, you loose your gear or the blue crabs eat your shrimp. If you want those bring a big net because they are HUGE. Oh they have fishing piers but the space isn't that big. It's first come first serve. Don't let that discourage you. You can still have fun with family and fish. Just cast out far.

name: Sherman On
text: Wish we could’ve spent more time here. Great children’s playground which was open when we visited on Saturday, August 29, 2020.Great different spots for fishing as there were many people fishing. Lots of picnic areas to be able to have a sit down meal in shade under a pavilion. Would definitely enjoy coming back in the future. There is a cost per adult (13 y/o + and child (3-12 y/o) but we felt it was worth the price for the family fun we had.

name: Ronald Howell
text: Well for me as you will see in the pictures, in 1950s it became a neighborhood, which I grew up in till 1970. Now it a very nice wetland due to subsidence. Trails are well kept, designated picnic areas and fishing areas some concrete foundations still exist. It was a neighborhood that everyone knew everyone and the kids no need to lock doors and windows. Worth the visit ck with office about bike riding.

name: Jeremy Yeakey
text: This is a great coastal area that has a playground for children and even a musical instrument area outside. Lots of people come here to fish, crab, and barbecue under one of its many pick nick areas. There is also a small nature center and learning plaques throughout the parks nature trails. We hiked 5 miles here today and only covered about half of the available trails.

resp.text:
Thank you, Dan, for your review. I apologize for the unclean condition of the port-a-potties. I would have been upset about that too! As a nature center, we do not spray pesticides for mosquitoes, so there are times that we seem to have more than our share. I appreciate the kind comment about the children's Nature Discovery Area!
I might suggest that you try a visit again during the winter or early spring... it's really pretty out there! Maybe you can join us at our Nurture Nature Festival on April 13, a free family event for everyone!

"...M a k e - y o u - f o r?"

It appears the owner has told everyone employed at this location to say this, because almost all of the employees that I've encountered here in the past six to eight months ask for your order this way, all the time.

It is very annoying.  If it was said just once or twice by someone from whom such colloquial "Yoda-speak" was demographically appropriate, that would be fine. But when people whom you know would never say the aforementioned of their own volition, say it every time you place an order, it gets really old.

How about, you spend half as much of your meager didactic capital on training the employees to correctly fill orders that were entered into your system, correctly.

That would be much less annoying.
See the photos I posted for this location.

The food here is ALWAYS prepared sloppily, at best.

text: A wonderful serenity has taken possession of my entire soul, like these sweet mornings of spring which I enjoy with my whole heart. I am alone, and feel the charm of existence in this spot, which was created for the bliss of souls like mine. I am so happy, my dear friend, so absorbed in the exquisite sense of mere tranquil existence, that I neglect my talents. I should be incapable of drawing a single stroke at the present moment; and yet I feel that I never was a greater artist than now. When, while the lovely valley teems with vapour around me, and the meridian sun strikes the upper surface of the impenetrable foliage of my trees, and but a few stray gleams steal into the inner sanctuary, I throw myself down among the tall grass by the trickling stream; and, as I lie close to the earth, a thousand unknown plants are noticed by me: when I hear the buzz of the little world among the stalks, and grow familiar with the countless indescribable forms of the insects and flies, then I feel the presence of the Almighty, who formed us in his own image

name: Julie
text: This shopping center has a variety of stores to choose from. Although some are high end merchants there are also choices available for all budgets. Charming Charlie, Kendra Scott, Gap Kids, and Lush are a few of the retailer's you will find. You can spend quite a bit of time in Sur La Table just looking at the display of kitchen accessories and gadgets. And if you are looking for good cookie cutters or baking items this is certainly the store for it. Market Street is a wonderful place to go for a stroll after dinner and there are a several restaurants to choose from. The green space is nice as well. You can basically accomplish a lot in this one shopping area: HEB for groceries, a dry cleaner, a couple of banks, eye doctor, dentist, day spa, European Wax Center, Massage Envy, hotel, Starbucks, and a movie theatre. And it is all walkable.

text: Beautiful shopping destination. Generous parking areas. Fantastic amenities. Varied choice of restaurants. Easy walking on sidewalks. Charming green space & water feature. Convenient location. Some wonderful stores and shops. Favorite long-term places: HEB grocery, Banana Republic (store & restaurant), Sur La Table, Tinseltown, La Madeline's, Aaron Bros (art & frame supplies), Border's (miss it), Eddie Bauer & Orvis!  --- Yet some residents wonder if management expectations are reasonable. There is frequent turnover with shops closing and new ones taking the spaces. Is rent too high? Are the wrong stores for the area being courted? Are the prices more than their average shopper will pay, therefore not providing enough revenue for smaller retailers to stay in business? High end, speciality stores are nice if sufficient clientele is present. I'm not sure this is the case, so Market Street leasing appears to have a revolving door.

name: Gustavo Velazquez
text:
Elena Q. With Champions Real Estate Group was a great partner and advisor in the process of rebuilding our house after it was flooded during Hurricane Harvey. She gave us excellent advice on what to do and what not to do during this process to accomplish the goal of selling our house without issues always trusting reliable contractors and keeping a record of every step of this process (professional water restoration process, licensed and qualified electricians and plumbers, trusted contractors and even suggested paint colors ) . Once our house was completely rebuilt following her guidelines she carefully inspected every inch of the house, analyzed houses for sale in our area and suggested the market sales price to put our house on the market, we were really amazed by the results: more walk ins and offers than we could ever imagine in just ONE day on the market, we even had to decline receiving offers and stop showing the house by the second day. Thanks to Elena our house was sold after being just ONE day in the market and for a very fair price, we even sold it for $5,000 over the asking price.
We were so happy with Elena that we decided to trust her with helping us buying a new home, after visiting her suggested properties we found our perfect new home...we absolutely couldn't be happier.

Thanks Elena Q.

name: Maria Galiotos
text:
I am a REALTOR with Champions Real Estate Group and having seen some of the negative reviews about Champions Real Estate Group, I would like to say that not all agents or REALTORS are the same.

A real estate agent is someone that got a real estate licence, a REALTOR® is a licensed real estate salesperson who belongs to the National Association of REALTORS®, the largest trade group in the country.

REALTORS® are held to a higher ethical standard than licensed agents and must adhere to a Code of Ethics.

Now, maybe some of the people commenting, that had a bad experience with the company, received some bad service from some agent, doesn't mean that all agents are the same, and also please note that Champions has over 2000 agents under their brokerage. I, for instance pride myself on giving the best possible customer service and being a problem solver and offering an easy exit guarantee to all clients that work with me. That means that if any client is not completely satisfied with my service, they can get out of any contract they've signed with me and I offer that in writing.

Thank you!

name: Disabled Dave
text: It is a very large flea market on Airline Drive near Houston. It is easy to see from the road. The parking lot fills up and is not paid. It can be dirty if it has been raining. Most of the Stalls are outside under a cover it is not air condition. But it is a very pleasant walk and lots of vendors. The vendors have a variety of goods. You will easily find whatever you're looking for. It is mostly a Mexican market. they have food booths and restrooms. It does get a little crowded on Sunday. The owners are helpful and friendly. Vendors are eager to sell and Haggling for price is Welcome. It's better to bring cash as not all vendors will take credit cards. It takes up many acres and has several hundred vendors it will take many hours to walk the entire Market. It is a typical Mexican flea market. Mercado. The Mexicans make it entertaining and fun. There are statues of wrestlers that you can take your picture with. It was my first time here and I will be back. I highly recommend this to anyone just don't go on a rainy day.

resp.text:
Hello there Tristan,

We're very sorry to hear about your experience, but we can assure you that we are working on solving the current problems with parking. The increase in bargin shoppers has caused a dramatic spike in attendance especially on Sundays, which has led to the clearing of another 1.5 acres of land to better accommodate everyone. Love sunny flea & the other connected markets... So many different foods and traditional foods, breads and candies brought from Mexico & central America! Yes lots of walking and gets crowed on sundays, I suggest to go early. I guess another reviewer must of been rushed or something because there is used stuffed here too...I never seen an advertisement saying this was an antique flea market... Nor is there a law that states that all flea markets have to be the same or have antiques or such. Houston is diversed so get over it.. I see they have some kind of new attraction of miniature figures of china..I believe they bought them from the forbidden Garden of Katy ... But it hasn't opened yet I asked a while back on there facebook page when they open and they said soon :( Hope they raise money for them to finish!...

name: John M. Oyerbides
text: This is a very nicely decorated restaurant. It has the feel of a Korean, Korean place.  There are 3 all you can eat menus. The prices vary based on the offerings on each menu. The most expensive had the seafood. I wasn't quite sure about the difference in the other 2. I think the next most expensive had a couple specialized beef dishes. Everything was fine just not outstanding. We had a nice waitress to start but then you kind of get whoever is available. This kind of gave us a mixed bag. My wife ordered a chicken dish which we never got. It didn't affect the price, but was annoying. The one waitress told us she didn't hear our signal. The tables have doorbell signals to alert the waitresses. Overall it was fine. I liked the location and the private rooms.  Bathrooms were clean. Still not the best Korean BBQ in town; I am still searching.

name: Brooke Gutierrez
text: Great tasting food, salad was tasty too. Were definitely new customers for life.  We come atleast once a week for a family meal

name: Joseph G.
text: All you can eat Korean BBQ has 3 different level of prices. The top tier includes all you can eat squid and shrimp which are not included in the other 2 levels. Overall, food was very good and service was equally good. Only downside was some BBQ dishes were cooked in the kitchen rather than by the diner. Maybe good for some but not for me since part of the reason a place like this is good is the fact that you cook it in front of you, you control how well done you want it cooked then you eat it while still hot. It is just not the same coming out of the kitchen. This place also had a lot of typical Korean side dishes that were delicious. The price came with a choice of soup include a variety of ramen soup - that's if you still have room in your stomach. First time here and very good experience. We will be coming back.

name: Thao Phan
text:
We came on the Wednesday night, surprisingly there were only 2-3 servers. Thus, it took long time to serve the food, but it was alright. We got the $32.95 menu and ended up paying around $45 each (3.95 for drinks, tips and taxes included). And to be honest, i think it’s pricey since the food was just alright. The dish size was medium, but since it’s all you can eat then that’s acceptable. They also gave us 2 choices of soups, dumplings fried and shrimp fried, corn cheese, steamed egg, and tok. But all those size dishes were small as well.
The important part: the meat did not taste fresh to us. And the short ribs were thinner than usual. Usually, i love to eat the meat around the bone but there were no meat around it unfortunately.
Overall, just because it was kinda expensive than usual and the because of the meat, I do not think I will comeback soon.

name: S Miller
text: When you walk in and look around the place looks dark and dingy, however once seated the colors and tone, the decorations and smells bring comfort. Then you like the feeling of privacy the seating brings. You can't be in a rush here. The service seems slow if you are in a hurry, but then again don't be in a rush when you go. The food is excellent, as long as you don't leave your food on the grill too long. It's pretty hard to mess up as long as you remember no more than a min or two and it's done. With all that said, the price tops it off. It is very fairly priced for what you receive. Enjoy and relax here.

name: Dawn Callahan
text: This was an unexpected surprise. From the outside, I wasn’t sure what I was getting myself in to. This was only my second Korean BBQ experience and the first was ages ago. Leave it to Houston to provide the best of the best. I’m not the person you wanna bring to an all you can eat restaurant but this is the only way to go. The experience is fabulous. The food is fresh. And you will walk away stuffed and I mean like Holiday dinner stuffed! The service was ok but I think, like most places, they’re still working out the Covid changes. Overall, highly recommend.

text: Great establishment. Good prices. Walking in I felt welcomed and the customer service was superb. Food portions was well enough for three people. Overall, full and have a food baby now.

name: Kim Nguyen
text:
I almost frequently venture to this location. And almost always the experience has generally been difficult to hunt down a waitress to trying to get the next course of meat in for your meal.

While the food has always been worth the wait, it's always been difficult to actually get the meat let alone track the waitress/waiter itself.

Whenever I have a friend who asks for me to show them a place they've never been to before, the first thing I will always think of is Korea House. Any time I've gone to any place else, this place has always been my number one let alone their meat is hard to compete against!

My only issue is there appears to be a passive/aggressive fight with the staff when it comes to trying to cook your meat.

Usually the staff will replace your grill plate frequently to coming around to check in. As of late, some of the waitresses would be passive aggressive about changing the temperature of the dial on the grill. This is my reasoning for the four star review.

While I can whole heatedly agree that this is a place of business and restaurants have costs they need to account for, please let me cook my meat in peace given I only can have two hours to eat!

I highly recommend if you intend to maximize on your time at this restaurant during it's two hour maxmium during high volumes to order your wings and raw meats in one go.

Pork will take the longest to cook and beef will take the quickest to cook next to chicken.

I recommend ordering one portion of the pork and change up the other servings while you wait in between courses.

It's definitely worth the experience and the money!

name: Jeannette Lopez
text: Great culinary  experience. We came to the restaurant by coincidence, just wanted to try something new and where to eat. Great service, waitress explained us every dish.  It was funny when he said “and now you start cooking”. We spent a great time, food taste was awesome and we learned about Korean food which is great.

Tried for the first time. There was a learning curve with the menu options, but it's all good!

name: Kathryn Hatfield
text: HOW have we lived 5 minutes from here for more than 5 years and never tried this place before today?! Gross negligence, that's how. We will now rectify with many repeat visits. Loved the ambiance of the place with the fun decorations and many booths and private rooms, and the food was great. The zucchini pancake didn't topple my local favourite but was more than good, and we enjoyed the spicy rice cake and the delectable dumplings. We want to come back and try BBQ one day soon. Very friendly and kind people work here, too - always a bonus.

name: DUDEVADERPLAYS
text: Great Korean BBQ. Good selection and price isn't bad either. Service was quick and very friendly

name: Ram chakradhar
text: The overall experience was nice. It is always better to go in a group. People are nice. The place gets very loud. Fun experience. The food was good.

name: Quynh Nguyen
text: It’s my best Korean Bbq place in Houston. They have a good menu with all of my favorite foods. You should come here at least one time.

name: Lovenia Kirkwood
text: It was so good!!! I shall be back. There was absolutely nothing to complain about.

name: Lovenia Gill
text: Fantastic as usual. Super clean and friendly staff.

name: Tsuki Fujiwara
text: If you like korean barbecue or wanna try it out, I suggest coming here. They have 3 different menus for barbecue and a regular menu, as well, if you don't want K-BBQ. I have tried both options and they have plenty food items to choose from. A must visit and try.

name: Ham String
text: Great Korean food. Served pretty authe toc Korean food and they have some sushi and BBQ. Good service. Nice decor and everything. I will definitely come back.

name: James Walker
text: Delicious food, i mean seriously incredible. Their bugogi is to die for. I come here a lot and truly appreciate the service and attention to detail, the owner is also very nice and makes sure everything is perfect. If I could rate more than 5 stars I would.

name: Denise Logue
text:
So, this is an update to a review I left almost a year ago.  Last night the service was so bad, we will never go back again.  We literally had to stop 5 different people to get more items to cook.  Horrible.  They charge you $35 a person for all you can eat, but never return to ask what else you want.  Having to stop servers clearly ignoring us was very aggravating, especially since we were there for my son's birthday and this is the place he had chosen.  We should have drove 5miles or less down the street and gotten both fantastic food and over the top service at the Brazilian steakhouse.  I would avoid this place if I were you.  Not only were we obviously ignored by the servers, again I can only assume that they really don't want it to truly be an all you can eat but just a way to lure you in, but there were at least 3 men walking around filming the guests and the goings-on.  Oblivious to the fact that there were us at table 8, and another table behind us complaining about the same thing.  Horrible experience yesterday and I rescind my previous review .  Then to top it all off, after we finally did leave, the men who were taking pictures inside earlier were right out the front door smoking cigarettes, so after a pretty lousy experience inside, we had to walk thru cigarette smoke right out the front door.

. This was my review from almost a year ago.
This was really a fun restaurant. We had heard about it from a friend so decided to give it a try. It's kind of a new concept for us, probably for most people as a matter of fact. There's three different menu price points each menu representing a certain amount of proteins available. They bring the raw protein to your table and you cook it on your own little hibachi grill in the center of your table. Like I said it was a new concept for us but we really enjoyed it. It was pricey, we chose the highest price point menu, $35 a person, but it was an experience that we are glad we had. We probably will go back again.

name: Andy Nguyen
text: Been going here for years now, always a good time

name: Danny Hoang
text: Quality has went down but definitely still really good :)

name: James
text: I highly recommend Korea House for the experience, value and the quality of food.

name: Crystal Leffall
text: Don't get a private room, you'll have a heat stroke! Im normally cold-natured, but i was sweating so bad in one of their semi-private rooms that has 2 grills in the table. Very uncomfortable. Also, unless you pick a marinated meat,  you need to bring your own seasoning. They only give you 2 dippinng sauces, one is made of oil and the other peanut butter(i hate peanut butter). I suggest they put salt and pepper shakers on each table,  because the unmarinated meat is DISGUSTING. Also they brought out all these appetizers and didn't explain what they were, after we kept telling her it was our first time there. That was rude.

name: Troy Jarboe
text: Again good, enjoy the meal.

name: Hojung Jung
text: Good but pricy

name: Raw Raw
text: The food was great, the prices a bit high. I asked for forks and never got them and we only saw the server when they took the order, when they brought the food, n when we got the check.

name: L K
text: The downside to this place is they only have all you can eat set meals. It really was a waste to bring out the appetizers because they all looked and tasted bad. The only good side dish was the kimchi, but also wasn’t amazing. The meat was good and came out in small portions and the soup was good too. But since I judge a place by their side dishes, I’m not recommending this place.

name: Marcy Abadeer
text: They are very polite have excellent the food is really delicious especially love the spicy Ramen tofu  I recommend you to try all you can eat menu it's pretty pricey but is worth

name: Joshua
text: Amazing food, can't type, too full

name: Teya Grayned
text: The BEST Korean restaurant in HOUSTON.  Owner and staff are friendly and the food is amazing. Love this hidden gem.

name: Andrew Kim
text: I loved the food and price. Try their all you can eat meat. Service is great too.

name: Ebey Soman
text: Highly recommend going as a group, but make reservations first and come super hungry. Food is absolutely amazing! Do the all you can eat menu that costs more, meats are higher quality and plenty of choices of things to eat. You won’t regret coming here, some of the best Korean bbq in all of Houston.

name: Steve Moore
text: Food ok, wait staff half good, half pretty poor. They are sneaky about your bill for large parties, so make sure you look over your first ticket carefully because they won't bring it back to you know matter who or how many times you ask. Seems like they're hoping you can't tell if there is a tip added for large parties or not. Seemed very shady for the bill.  If my kids didn't like this place I probably would go someplace nicer.

name: Richard Halferty II
text: Great Korean fare of Looking Point

name: Lien Le
text: Amazing service, great food, good vibes.

name: Doug Ferro
text: Not great food for the price and the waitresses only come around after long periods of time.

name: Angie Diaz
text: My fiancé and I went on a date there and it was wonderful. The staff was incredibly nice, service was outstanding. We didn’t spend more than 35 dollars in total and we took the leftovers to go. Like I said the waiters and waitresses were very cool.

name: Denny Do
text: Great price during lunch time , around $20 for all you can eat. Mostly pork , only two beef dishes but the pork belly is really good here. I drive 30-45 minutes to eat here instead of the ones around me because this one is more worth it for its value to quality ratio.

name: Javar Levingston
text: Absolutely spectacular. I am in awe! All you can eat with a 2 hour limit. Well worth the money!

name: Scott Day
text: Great food great service

name: Robbie O'Donnell
text: Great service and super delicious food!!!

name: Roger Gutierrez
text: Food was delicious and service was excellent. First time there, definitely will return.

name: Pup BuckBoom
text: This is my favorite place to eat by far. Amazing personable service, fantastic choice of beer and other drink, and mind blowing food. If I'm going out to eat, I'm always going here. 👍 👍

name: spidahjan
text:
Thank you for the Korean taste. We are rating low because the quality of the food took a hit and with those prices we had expected more. We ordered the garlic chicken and unfortunately it came out extra dry and had tasted as if it had been left out on a hot plate. The second chicken that we ordered was the sweet and sour chicken and unfortunately suffered the same taste, old dry chicken. Side dishes were decent and the service was actually pretty good. The grill was changed out frequently and the waitresses came by asking if there's anything we needed. I suppose we did fail to notify the waitresses of the dry food but there really was no point because the desire for the flavor had came and gone after it being dried out twice.

Overall the place was great, atmosphere was brilliant. There isn't too many places like this in Houston so I suppose the prices would be affected. Bugogi, pork belly, and pork belly wine would definitely be the number one hits in my book, but that was the only highlight in the food options we tried.

name: Chris Hsu
text: Good food and excellent service

name: Vi Vu
text: Decent Kirean bbq all you can eat restaurant, fast and friendly service

name: MAK Straw
text: They put us in a dark and dingy back room that had no ventilation. My elderly father who suffers from COPD ended up having an asthma attack. I am not even sure how the fire marshal allows this. We will not be going back.

name: Victor
text: Came in a party of 7, and sat in one of the private rooms. It's a bit claustrophobic. The space was so small, our server kept reaching in front of me to serve the other side of our table. Sodas are served in a can and you'll pay for each one. The food, though, is great! It's the first time Ive seen shrimp at a Korean BBQ. It's all you can eat, so bring your appetite!

name: Anna Lee
text: Really enjoyed the food. Meats were well seasoned and marinated. The side dishes were plentiful and tasty. All of the servers were helpful and ready to refill anything requested. We'll definitely be back!

name: Cesar Muniz
text:
After going here multiple times over the past 4 years, this place has consistently gotten worse. I am currently bedridden as the meat has forced my body to start vomiting since 2:00 AM. I definitely don't want to eat here again as I noticed the quality has deteriorated over the last few years... especially during COVID-19. It's sad to see them add Yellow American Cheese on traditional Korean dishes as well as take even longer to serve my family.
As I sit next to the sink examining the little pieces of meat that I vomited...I cannot help but sum up why I am downgrading my review from 3 to 1 Stars:

TL/DR: They poisoned me. It was horrible.

name: khia jordan
text: The meat and the experience was really good

name: Christ Constantine
text: Good food so far. Been there a lot before

name: Kandy Lee
text: We s place is amazing. The service was excellent and the food was great. I loved how we get to grill the food and all the sides are great. Totally will go back

name: Patrick Blummer
text: Well worth price of admission. The pork is excellent

name: Ice Queen Dalton
text:
This is the best restaurant I have ever been to in my life. I had never experienced such attentive service before, we go here at least twice a week after finding this restaurant a few months ago.

All the staff knows us already and they remember our preferences, they talk to us and help us with our korean words. They introduce us to new korean side dishes every time we go. The owner is always there to greet us. Everyone is so quick and friendly.

I've read many reviews complaining about slow service but all you have to do is ring the bell and they'll assist you, they have a really big place so the staff is always busy.

Their side dishes are delicious, the prices are really good for an all you can eat buffet, and the menu items are really good (best bulgogi bibimbap I've ever had)

I've introduced many of my friends to Korea House and they all love it.

name: Natalie De Los Reyes
text: We really enjoy the food! Great buffet selection, we always get menu A. They off all you can eat options of you can order certain items. The staff is so nice & so so friendly. The prices are very reasonable. We go every week! The seafood ramen is so so so good! You really have the check this place out if you’re in the mood for Korean BBQ.

name: Eagle T
text: Horrible horrible service, we had to go get our water several times, no one come by at all. I told one of the waitress for a fork. She said yes and then just left. After 19 minutes still nothing, I had to walk around grabbing a waiter and ask for a fork. When I said I want less spicy for the ramen, the waitress had no clue what I’m talking  about. My friend had to use a dictionary and translate it into Korean for her and then she understood. Apparently this restaurant is only for Korean speakers. Won’t come back again.

name: Johnny Dixon
text: Meat here is tasty. Very friendly service.

name: Tine Cross
text: Delicious food and friendly service! Next time I’ll do the all you can eat which is offered at an awesome price

name: Jennifer Sone
text: We five of us are all you can eat meat and salad $25 per person and well satiated with good authentic taste and price. We are planning to go this Saturday again!

name: Mikey H
text: Was very good. Worth the price.. staff should be attentive to diners that dont usually dine in place like this.. they should at least make sure diners understand the concept.. 5 stars if they were attentive

name: Susi Bellamy
text: The food is good, but the service is slow, also they forgot bring me napkins and some meats. I paid a lot for the bad service.

name: Tabitha Overstreet
text: All you can eat

name: Gina Sanchez
text: Fantastic!!! The all you can eat meat selection was amazing.   Go hungry for sure.   Cost $$

name: Zerby Zerby
text: Favorite buffet spot. Great food options even for the price. Always great to feel like your a great chef cooking your own food. The service is good, always checking in for refills on food or drinks. Even the manager/owner comes by to greet and ask how our time and meal is.

name: Rodney Stahl
text: Amazing

name: Peter Nguyen
text: Jae was a great and knowledgeable server. Atmosphere was sleek and modern with a nice twist of traditional in the side rooms. Ate in one of these rooms, and it was perfect for our group since we can be boisterous. Good value for all you can eat. Would have liked a wider variety of soju brands like Chum Churum. All in all, great time

name: Jacob Kratavil
text: The service was friendly and the quality of the meat was good. Probably one of the best KBBQ places in Houston

name: Darrian Goode
text: Great place to pig out and really good prices as well

name: Sophia Cu
text: I will not return to this establishment. After dinner I spent most of the evening making frequent bathroom visits. My first complaint was we order an app, the waiter brought it out and one of the items fell on to the table and he picked it up with his bare hands and put it back on the plate. He didn't bother offering to re-fire another app. This just shows what type of place it was. The kimchi was was not authentically Korean made and we were looking for other side dishes/banchan, but they didnt not have available. The food and service was mediocre. There are other restaurants around the area that offer better overall experience.

name: rehughes86
text:
We enjoy this place! The food is great and the people are accommodating.
Never fails to satisfy our hunger for Korean dishes!

name: Defessus Ibis
text: Something new for people who are not familiar with this style of eating. I think it's great these places exist!

name: Charles Sulzen
text: This was my first time eating Korean food. My tasty, I will most certainly go here again. Very friendly, and helpful staff. They were very kind and understanding of a "noobie." It is a very quiet place, that invites one to sit and stay for as long as you want. Perfect place to bring someone special.

name: Tuan Hong
text: My go to Korean BBQ place.   We go for the all you can eat option.  Not worth the price of the all you can eat option if its a small party.  The meat is well marinated, the veggies are fresh, the sides dishes are never ending but you have to request more.  They don't just bring it out to you after you finish. Good lord...I'm craving their food just writing this review.  Lol.  Service was prompt, friendly, and helpful.   They will change our your grill surface if it gets too burnt.  They will also help you cook the meat if you aren't familiar with how it works.

name: Taylor Smith
text: The food and the atmosphere are top notch. Easily the best Korean BBQ in Houston. The owners are friendly and always greet you, and the staff are extremely nice, although sometimes a bit difficult to communicate with in English. I always look forward to coming here and have never been disappointed.

name: Neil b4Zod
text: Really good authentic Korean BBQ...all you can eat style for right around $30. Succulent, salty sweet, marinated meats and traditional side dishes. Many of the staff do not speak English which can be a challenge. Still worth going.

name: Elizabeth Garcia
text: Great service- good food!

name: Tracker Nation
text: Great service, great food, everyone was really nice and polite. I had lots of fun with my friends

name: Bianca Diaz
text: The overall atmosphere is very welcoming and I enjoy eating all the food here! I enjoy everything about the restaurant. The first time I came, I had 김치찌개 (kimchi stew) and it was delicious.

name: Justin Speed
text: Love this place. Service is pretty good and a great venue for hosting small parties. All you can eat Korean BBQ with an assortment of soju. Recommend the ribs, as always, and the octopus. Come hungry and wear pants that have an elastic waist.

name: Jose Reyes
text: Service is a bit slow. I wish they would explain everything that is served as accompaniments.

name: S A
text: I really enjoyed the goat soup. My kid loved the fried pork. There were more sides included than I anticipated and we took a to go box home since we couldn't finish. The quality and taste of everything we had was pro prepared. Servers are super polite. Would recommend.

name: Christine Phrasavath
text: All you can eat Korean food? Yes please! Lots of traditional meat plates and sides. The meat isn't flavored quite as well as other Korean restaurants but is still delicious!

name: Alayna M
text: If your looking for an Interactive dining  experience this is it. I throughly enjoyed the atmosphere. The staff is very friendly & upbeat. Since it was our 1st time here we had a few questions. They took the time to explain and was very attentive to our needs. They went over the menu and gave us suggestions on how to eat and pair the different sauses. We visited this place on a Friday and it wasn't a wait for seating. The food was delicious. You cook your own unlimited protein and they bring as much soup salad AND appetizers as you can eat. To top it off you get fresh fruit & rice milk after your meal. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to try something different. Overall the flavors were familiar enough to be enjoyed for underdeveloped tasting pallets or picky eaters.

name: Scarlett Jh
text: Price was ok, food kinda accepted, service was quick. Looks beautiful inside

name: Gabe Perez
text: Great quality food with plenty of meat options. Not great for vegetarians or pescatarians, but still a very enjoyable experience.

name: Chuong Ngo
text: Very attentive staff and great food! Atmosphere is very relaxing. I love the private dining rooms! Overall very nice place for any occasion!

name: Na Li
text:
Not many Korean buffer in houston , and this one is great. Very traditional decor inside, collections of Korean dolls displayed at the entrance and main corridor.

Service is implacable, price is decent for the good quality of the meat. The most intriguing thing is that there are around 20 different selections for the B choice. And the price at dinner is $28.99, not bad, probably same amount I spent st a decent Korean Restaraunt without trying out so many different meat.

You have to try all the bacons, they are different sauce and flavor. beef tongue is my favorite, tender enough to melt in your mouth. Shrimp with head is super fresh, and it comes right away each time we re-order. You can ask tell your nice waitress the quantity you want to avoid waste. Isn't that awesome?

The combo comes with 3 side dishes besides the million Korean side dish it usually comes with. Rice cake with cheese, miso soup pot and shrimp tempura. It's definitely a feast! I was bloated when I got out of there. Fully satisfied of course.

Will go back again for sure when I'm in craving for meat feast.

name: Albert G
text: I have had a great time every visit! All of the servers are really friendly and accommodating. Both the raw and cooked meat are very tasty; you also get fruit and a sweet rice drink for dessert which complement the meal nicely. I definitely recommend this place to anyone who is looking to try an all-you-can-eat kbbq joint for the first time.

name: Itzy Villela
text: My friends and I had the best time here. The service is very friendly and the food was delicious here.

name: M T N
text: Love the rice drink here... service could be a bit better (more attentive)

name: Diana Alvarez
text: Family portions, everything we got was delicious and the staff was very kind

name: Peter Chang
text: Great selection for all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ! $28.95 per person for the set A (which gives you wider selection of meat option) for dinner; it came with few appetizers as well (shrimp tempura, fried and steamed dumplings, spicy rice cake) and fruits at the end.

name: J O
text: Good selection meats with an "all you can eat" option.  Selection of other dishes too. The cold buckwheat noodles were excellent.

name: Cat S
text: This place can be a bit of a hit or miss. Sometimes the marinated meat just doesn't taste like it was marinated, and other times it's the best Korean BBQ in the city. I've noticed if you come as a big group for the all you can eat combos your service gets spottier the longer you're there. They take longer to bring your meat and "forget" several of the dishes you order. It was funny the first visit...but when every visit we weren't getting a third of what we ordered.... Then again I haven't gone as a big group in a year now so they may have improved that aspect. But when the meat is good....it is GOOD. I love their marinated galbi and their salad.

name: Francis Vo
text: This place is good but service really sucks they do not care about their customers and I think that it's ridiculous that the employees sit and do nothing while customers are waiting for their drinks and food. When I first came in they pretended to be busy bit the restaurant was empty , it took forever to get seated at this place. There are several spots that offer great food and service.

name: Agnieszka Villanueva
text: Worth the price. Great selections of meat. Staff was very attentive

name: Sanjeev Joshi
text: Good experience, although I prefer another Korean BBQ in cypress.

name: Stephanie Elledge
text: Amazing Korean BBQ place. Great staff.

name: FAITH M
text: It was fun to BBQ with my family. They are accommodating of children and the servers are very nice. And gave us extra servings when asked.  I wish I took a pictures of the food.

name: Princess Ugale
text: Best Korean bbq place in Houston! During happy hour is the best time to go here. You’ll save  more while having the same great tasting food.

name: Amber Rose
text: Food good just tasted different from American food

name: Heath Casey
text: Some friends brought us here and I loved it.  Nice selection, family style and table top cook stove.  The sides were good also.

name: Pamela Wyatt
text: korean food at this place - super good. It has a good feel to it.

name: Anthony Spadafora
text: Lived in Korea for 7 years and this place is very authentic and welcoming even for newcomers. Absolutely worth giving it a try!

name: Sooyeon Kim
text: Clean, kind, food was taste good.

name: Liet Le
text: Good service. Felt like I got beef scraps for bulgogi when order was cooked in the back. Overall, still good experience.

name: Farah Diba Binte Luba
text: This place was amazing. One of the best korean bbq ive had

name: Manuel Garcia
text: The all u can eat Korean bbq is really good. They explain in detail what u get the place is nice and spacious. Make sure to bring a friend ...the price point is a little high but the food was worth it.

name: Mike Sheehan
text: Excellent menu. Prompt service. It's served DIY style but totally worth having to cook it

name: Erik Cao
text: One of the very few places in Houston that use charcoal with their gas grill giving the meat a different flavor. It is a little pricey but with 3 different  menu and 3 different prices something for everyone.

name: Noor Alnahhas
text: A fun experience and great food. You choose between different meat options that include a wide variety of beef chicken and pork with some options that you grill at your table. Service is fast and friendly and the food is great. A great for groups.

name: C. Sheppy
text: I found it strange that we were seated in a separate part of the restaurant only because we ordered from the all you can menu. When we were seated the music playing in that section was way too loud. The food was just OK but the service was pretty decent.. I might give this restaurant a second chance but not anytime soon.

name: HappyHair Day
text:
My first KBBQ experience and it was soooooo good!! The staff is really nice and the private rooms are effectively a must, if you're coming with friends.
It's especially nice in the winter, because the rooms get pretty warm when you start cooking. I'm for sure going back here.

name: HT BULL
text: Always a wonderful place to eat. Great tasty food and great service. Great selections of meats and big servings.

name: Syed Raza
text: Quite the typical Korean bbq, fair prices, good selection of meats.

name: Michael Tran
text: If you're ready to feast then this is the place for you.  Many will compare to Seoul garden down the street and i will do so here as well.  I'm a big eater and getting full at Seoul garden can be tough for cheap.  That's where Korea house comes in.  For roughly the same price i can get stuffed.  The short ribs are a good cut, the pork belly choices and cuts surpass that of Seoul Garden.  Korea house has sides but most are not that great compared to Seoul.  You really miss out out on the potatoes and spinach.  You can skip the pork ribs at Korea house, as they are plain and rely on the sauce to give them any flavor.   Cooking at Korea house is different from Seoul.  At Seoul you get a real grill to cook on and the flavor stands out more.  At Korea they give you a skillet with aluminum foil.  Make sure remove the foil or you will be simmering your food.  I believe there are tables with proper grills but you'll have to get lucky to get one otherwise you'll be skillet cooking instead.  So in short if you can get past the odd setup for Korean bbq and are more focused on the meats than the sides (that's me) than you'll enjoy Korea house.  If you aren't that big of a meat eater then go to Seoul.

name: andrea k
text: Really expensive💔 but they have great quality meats

name: ashley b
text: The food was absolutely amazing and they offer a wider selection to choose from than other places I've been to. The reason I gave ⭐⭐⭐ was due to the extremely slow and lackluster staff. They would never refill our waters, only exchanged our grill top once, forgot several people's sauces... But when it seemed like we had been there for a while, we were possibly overstaying our welcome (not sure how you can do that) because we started noticing the infamous check hover. I was in town for an event, but I would definably go again and recommend it, just maybe approach the staff differently so you aren't left burning on the inside from some spicy squid and have no drink left. 😂

name: Christopher Nguyen
text: Good friendly service.  Food is good here and great for family and friends. I frequent this place because of the quality and value.

name: Kene Ugw
text: A tad pricey as opposed to going to a regular Korean BBQ restaurants and their menu was confusing. I came with a group, so we shared everything. There was something for everyone on the menu and in the end, we all liked what we ate. A little odd for the way they have their KBBQ set up but it was all good eats!

name: Jingjing Ng
text: good

name: Kelareh Seif
text: Really enjoyed my visit here. They were really accommodating of it being our first time there and of our really outspoken 3 year old

name: Cheryl Czerewaty
text: Great food and nice atmosphere.

name: Sushi Deflare
text:
Had a great time,new experience. The only reason they're not getting 5 star is because the portions were so small, we could've ordered as many times as we wanted but it was very little at a time I guess it minimize waste.
Nothing to be scrared of take the meat and put it on the grill then eat. I was bit confused about the appetizer and sides we can order. But they were all nice.
Price run between 25_30 person for dinner. Worth it to me.
Lots of Korean people eat there(like 90% of the patrons that night),so must be somewhat authentic.

name: myisha simpson
text: Love this place. Great place to eat at. I will be going back.

name: KEN Miller
text: First entering, very lovely staff. Everyone here is some friendly. I came in at a time not to busy, but it seemed to be a while b4 we were acknowledged. (7-10min). It has a nice set up, and a great atmosphere. While eating I asked for soy sauce and it took until the end of my meal to receive it. Yet, they weren't busy. With a restaurant that everyone has rated with such high regards, it sure doesn't seem like it matches the reviews. Aside from taste of food, and the manager being so nice. THERE WAS DRIED FOOD ON MY PLATE. Not a particle, but a piece of food. Korea Garden is far superior, and recommend them. They are a few streets over and I've always had a pleasant time. (unfortunately, this is my first and last time here)  side note, my gf just pointed out, there is a bell you ring for service, this may have led to a better experience, but, as this is not common place in most restaurants in had no knowledge of this. (she is Asian and will probably disagree with my post here) I'm just rating service overall.

name: Justin Raine
text: Houston really lacks Korean BBQ options. This place was pretty solid, with three different levels of BBQ service. We chose the cheapest one (can't remember what it was called - maybe A?). The variety of meats was okay; the menu was pretty heavy on pre-cooked chicken, so it would've been nice to have more self-cook options. Serving sizes were kind of small for a four-person group. Appetizers were okay. Overall a solid experience.

name: Richie Nguyenphat
text: Great traditional Korean BBQ setting. There is an A, B, and C menu. I usually get the B and order bulgogi, wine pork belly, and brisket. Lots of nice side dishes and lettuce to go along with the meal. They give you a nice fruit cup and rice juice at the end of your meal. Great place to eat some good KBBQ with large groups.

name: Dre Roy
text: I love all the different options of meat. Food is great!

name: Kendrick Wee
text: A 15-20 minutes wait on Saturday night seems reasonable. Buffet price was on the pricer side. Meat quality is above average, way better than Jin. Seasoning wise wasn’t as flavorful as Jin. There isn’t a ready cooked food bar that one can pick their own side dishes or eat some cooked food while waiting for their bbq to get done. They will come by to change out the grill from time to time. Service is very attentive, they always came to check on us. There are two options. option A is everything on the menu and option B is only a selected portion of the menu. There is no such thing as Togo boxes here

text: They redid the floors and are making wonderful updates to the restaurant. This is our go to Kbq place because the food is great, but also the staff are helpful, kind, and attentive. Delicious all you can eat Kbq grilled right at your own table. Definitely worth a try- even if you've never had Korean food before. text:

Worth the money if you’re a big eater, would reccomend coming during happy hour if you aren’t too hungry.

I enjoyed this more than Jin Korean bbq, however keep in mind that depending on your preference(buffet(Jin) vs brought to the table(Korea House)), Jin Korean bbq may be more worth your buck(meat quality is on par, may be better or worse at times)

Still, this place wins in terms of variety and overall experience. Definitely a more authentic feel, and may be slightly more difficult for newcomers. Don’t be scared to ask questions; the staff is amazing.

Depending on the occasion, I definitely will be coming back. One of the most enjoyable and diverse experiences you can get in Houston food-wise, and that’s saying a lot.

Do yourself a favor and get all you can eat.  It may be pricy, but it's worth it every once in a while to gorge yourself on meat.  Everything you can get is delicious, but I recommend spicy pork belly and their special bulgogi.  You can easily just sit and eat for 2-3 hours, and it's a great time to bond with people.

text:
Great place if you are doing Korean BBQ. they have the BBQ tables with the vents and let you cook yourself if you are willing to trust yourself with sharp objects and raw meat you should go for it. I never really tried anything outside of the BBQ but i do recognize that there is a large number of sides that come with the meal and you could easily fill up on one order of BBQ if you really enjoy Korean sides.

The service may seem odd at first but in Korea waiters dont come check on you, they leave you alone (i find it nicer that way but others might feel a bit odd). they actually use a button system. you will find a button on your table and you press it every time you need something (refills or even if you are ready to order). i saw at least 1 review trashing service.... its probably because they didnt know about the button system. really this makes the best service you could ever want in my opinion.

My only issue was the price. Its a bit pricey for some of the meats and i could easily spend over 100 if you are with a group of 3. A good alternative to ordering several plates of meat would be to do the all you can eat, its 21 (ish) a person and you can choose most of the meats as often as you want... i think its for 2 hours at a time so you cant just chill all day until you have the meat sweats. Regardless the food itself is fantastic Its definitely worth the trip for some quality Korean BBQ.

name: Shana Shenanigans
text: I had the opportunity to go to The Grove on the Friday before Valentines day for GALLENTINE'S 🥰. Me and my friends had a lovely time. They featured a selected menu and everything we had was delicious.  Our waiter was so nice and attentive.  I had the pleasure of trying the Ginger Margarita 🍹, SO GOOD!! Definitely had a kick and it was yummy. The restaurant was decorated so elegantly for the occasion and everyone practiced social distancing.  They also offered free valet for those with a dinner reservation, which was nice.  (Even though when I was ready to leave, my car was stuck in the garage for about 30 minutes 🙃.  They eventually got it out lol.) After dinner they had coffee and cocktails in the upstairs patio/bar area. The decor was perfect and had multiple desserts, fruits and cheeses to choose from with a live classical music performance. Such a nice evening, I was so impressed with everything.  I will definitely be back to experience their Happy Hour. Thank you so much for a great first experience 💗.

name: David Cooper
text: My first time here.  Service was great and the food was a pleasant surprise.  My daughter and I spilt a half-price at lunch blue crab corn fritters, which were very fresh and tasty, with an amazing dipping sauce--great start to a pleasant outdoor lunch.  This was followed by our entree.  We both decided on the shrimp and crab salad roll and substituted the Maque Choux for the potato wedges that would have come with the rolls.  The restaurant has a very good beverage list (see menu on their website). We ate on the patio (see photos) with a great view and the staff were very helpful without being obtrusive.  Highly recommend!
