Best Regards,
The Pappasito’s Cantina Team

name: Troy Stuart
text: Awesome food always fresh. Staff is amazing and attentive.  The bar tenders are spot on and make amazing drinks.

name: Christopher Dawkins
text: Large last minute togo order on game day was no problem. 💣💥 Tasty as always! 10 people fwd well for 250.

name: Sina Ruiz
text: The tortillas were amazing!  I had the red fish and shrimp.  Great food and the service was excellent.

name: NolaBama
text: Giant chain of top notch restaurants. Ran by a good group obviously. Extremely popular. Good food. A little pricey for some folks. I like the shrimp en brochette. They have a name for it tho. It's still good.

name: Scott Gadd
text:
Myself and four work colleagues came here for a business lunch Wednesday afternoon. We ordered a medium queso to share (yum!) and I ordered the Chicken Fajita Flautas.  They were delicious!

The service was attentive and prompt.  It is located in a great location just across the street from Discovery Green in downtown Houston.

name: Diego Juan
text: Very good food for mexican stile. Enchiladas were great. Shimp brochette however was very salty. Desserts were great.Usually crowded. For our particular event it was kind of noisy and that did not contribute to our meeting.

name: Debra Setzer
text:
Table guacamole was great! Server was great!
Love the chips but not the salsa, wish they would offer a couple of varieties!

name: Mark Smith
text: Food was amazing. Drink prices were high, but comparable to the area. Walking distance to Toyota Center. Make sure your bill is correct if you open a tab. I had 2 drinks on my bill that were not ours. Bartender was cool and corrected it right away.

name: Doug Ferro
text: Drinks are strong wait staff is always friendly. A little pricey but always go there for Fri ks and food before a concert.

name: Lara Polk
text: Awesome service and great food. Located in the hotel makes it even better when you're staying at the Hilton. The sauce is amazing check it out today.

name: Jennifer Y.
text:
Pappasito's is my go to. Amazingly strong margaritas in a variety of flavors and great quality meat fajitas. What's not to like?

This location is right in front of the Toyota Center so it's great to go to right before events. The downside is that it will be incredibly busy. Went I went there was a 45 minute wait time (although I definitely didn't wait more than 20 for my table to be ready.)

If you're in a hurry you can order a drink and some small apps (or just go with the free tortilla chips and salsa) and sit on the patio outside. It's a great place to hang out. Although, the outdoor couches do seems a bit questionable in terms of cleanliness.

Service is pretty quick out there even though you're not at a true table - they like to walk around periodically and ask if you need anything.

Beware of the mosquitoes though! Especially at this time of year (in the summer months) they get vicious. Wear lots of bug spray and keep your body as clothed as possible (I know it's hard in the heat).

Bathrooms are at the back right corner from when you walk in - fairly clean and the hostess comes to refill napkins and stuff very often. Only 2 toilets in the women's though.

name: Nikolai Ommundsen
text: Wonderfully good service and tasty food. Remember that portion sizes in Texas are huge. We bought fajitas, size: 2-3 persons, and we were 4 adults. We barely managed to eat it all. You also get free chips and salsa when arriving at a table. The noise level is a bit high in some areas, but the food and the service makes up for it in large amounts. Thank you for a good experience!

name: Kristi Rodriguez
text:
We attended the Ronald McDonald House Boo Ball at the Hotel Americas this weekend. We had a room at the hotel along with the other guests in our party of 8. Most did not eat the meal at the Ball for various reasons so were looking for a late meal or snack. We all went down to Pappasitos around 10:45pm to eat. We sat at our table for a while and no one was waiting on us. Finally when a waitress walked by my husband asked if she could wait on us. She told us so and so was our waiter (cant remember his name) and he walked up about that time. In jest, my husband told the waitress "we want you to wait on us". She laughed and walked off. My husband and I, on the end, ordered drinks and the waiter took off without asking anyone else at our table.

About 2 minutes later a manager shows up. He proceeds to tell us he would not serve us because we had been over served and we could have dessert. Now of the 8 of us, only one very young lady was inebriated. She needed food. The others of us had only have 2 or 3 drinks at the most at the ball. We were all flabbergasted! We may have been a bit loud but it was more just excitement from ball and dancing. The manager continued to to tell us we could have dessert.

We left with no issues. I think they just did not want to serve us, not just drinks, because it was close to closing time. We frequent the Hotel Americas for many events and usually eat at Pappasitos at least once when there. We will not be giving them our service anymore. I can understand if we were in fact drunk and making a ruckus but that was not the case. We went down to the hotel bar and were served food and drinks no problems at all, isn't it ironic!!!!!

name: Kathryn Isabel King
text: Very delicious, decent service considering we were a party of 20. Waiters were very nice.

text: Great food but a little crowded and service could have been better... if your stuck downtown than yes but if not go to a different location.

name: Bill Chollett
text: Food and service were excellent. All the more impressive because the place was packed due to the Elton John concert next door. The chicken fajitas were the most tender and juicy I've ever had. Shrimp brouchette was also a special delight. ... The concert was all the better thanks to such a great "opening" act.

name: Rob Schaefer
text:
This location is located within the Hilton Americas and might explain our experience, which was not up to par with other Pappas restaurants in Houston.  The service was below average and for the first time ever, I had to return a margarita that was so sour it was not consumable.

The manager stopped by and instead of apologizing, he indicated the drink I returned would be comp'd.  I thought to myself, "Well of course I'm not paying for a cocktail that I did not drink."

I ordered a beer instead, my wife had a skinny margarita, and we ordered a small nacho and small quesadilla from the appetizer selection. Total bill was $58 before gratuity.

We are fairly easy going customers and generally do not leave negative feedback, but I will make an exception for this experience.

Ordered the churro and again, my dessert was the last to be served. When I got it, it tasted burnt. It looked darker that the ones they brought to the table to show you.

name: Plot Pandemic
text:
So. One year ago I ordered from this place during my stay at the Hilton. Not only did they "lose" my order despite someone on the phone taking my order. (I got downstairs and no one had any knowledge of my order. No apologies or attempt to fix the mistake was made. The staff was completely condescending.) The food was cold and over-salted when it finally did arrive. I couldn't even finish the tacos due to them being so salty that it made me squint a bit when I ate them.

I come back one year later for another visit to the Hilton. Despite not having a good experience, I thought I would give this place another try. Boy, was I wrong.

Literally go to ANY OTHER PLACE but this place. Even the Papa's Seafood is wonderful less than a half block away. There are great Mexican food restaurants nearby and WAY more worth your time.

I stood at the To-Go stand to place my order for a solid 20 minutes as the staff ignored me and pretended as if only one person was capable of taking my order, and she was "busy".

I was with my mother and it was mothers day. Since the wait was going to be so long for food, she wanted to sit down. They acted as if the only way that she could be seated is at the bar (My mother did not want to sit at the bar. She is 60 and we were there to visit each other.) She asked if she could sit at a table nearby in a restaurant FULL OF EMPTY TABLES and got a condescending, weird answer as if she needed to be fully seated off in some section on the other side of the restaurant where we could not hear our To-Go order. (Which is stupid, as we'd not be leaving a tip to anyone other than the bartender and were just there to wait for our order so putting us into the table rotation would have been ignorant.)

She gave my mother attitude when we just sat down at a table near the bar and informed them that it was Mothers Day, and we'd not be moving. She finally shut up when she realized she was very much upsetting and disrespecting my mother on mothers day, and was about to make me start a REAL scene if she continued to harass my mother. She had already gone way too far in her harassment and was about to really get a piece of my mind involving how she was speaking to her.

I am not sure who is hiring these mouthy, unprofessional 20 year olds, but you need to inform your staff to show a little respect or get new staff. I tip well and treat everyone with respect and have served myself for many years. I have never been treated well in this restaurant for the 2 years I have tried to give them a shot.

Terrible service. Mediocre food. I'm shocked that Hilton even allows them to take up space in their building.

Do not eat here.

name: Mike Fernandez

text: This is the world of Pappa's. Comfortable atmosphere; decent food; expensive. I had a salad. Between that, a beer, and a tip, it ran to over $30. Seriously? Honestly, it's good food, but Mexican food is cheap to make, so expensive Mexican food pretty much pisses me off.

name: Brittany Longoria
text:
EDITED:  Started off okay, we were sat immediately our server came within 5 minutes and took our drink order. But, it all went downhill after that. Took about 15 minutes to get our drinks, once we got them we still didn’t get my daughters milk. Had to ask for that again, ordered the zombie margarita and it came with a brown lime. In the photo it is shown with strawberries, pineapple and fresh mint. I asked what happened to that stuff because presentation is key. Waitress told me they didn’t have it at that station so she didn’t do it and handed me a cup of cut up pineapple and strawberries. Manager came over and compd our appetizer and my daughters food, but service was horribly slow from there on out, found myself with a cup of ice most the time and towards the end I had to walk my check up to the manager to get it closed out. In general I felt bad because our waitress was nice , but the overall experience was not that great. I prefer the nasa location so I’ll stick to that. I understand sometimes not everyone is on their A game but a basic meal with 3 people should not of taken 2 hours to complete.

EDIT : knocked down to a 1 star because this morning I woke up with food poisoning. 🤮 never stepping foot in this location again.

name: Candace Krenek
text:
Gluten free options available but they will cross contaminate. My coworker got sick from this. Not many vegetarian options. Not a good experience, however the management was very nice and helpful to fix it. I went with a large group for lunch, asked if they had any recommendations for a vegetarian without any dairy. They said they could do veggie enchiladas without cheese so cool I"m for that. Everyone else's food comes out, mine never comes. I'm informed the kitchen messed up and they're remaking it. Everyone finishes their meal and checks are coming, I still haven't got my food. I just told them to box it up because we had to leave. I get back to work to finally eat, and notice no rice but two sides of watery refried black beans and "enchiladas" which consist of bell pepper and one or two zucchini wrapped in a tortilla. This place is not cheap most of their menu items are $18 and up.  This is not an acceptable sub. Very disappointed in this meal, luckily they comped my meal because if they had'n't I would have been angry with what I was given.

Suggestions: We live in a large city with a variety of people. Just add more options to your menu.  Bell pepper wrapped in a tortilla is not enchiladas. Add onion and carrots, spinach, chickpeas, avocado. The ideas are endless!

Kind of stingy to-go portions for $50 of food. 4 tortillas for 6 or 7 fajitas, 1 fork for that much food, a tablespoon and a half of guac, pico & sour cream. Yes, I measured it because I couldn't believe my eyes. Good thing I keep some... I should've checked my order. Didn't think to because I've never had a complaint at other locations in the past. Y'all better be glad your chips n salsa are so good...

name: Frankie Mo. HD
text:
2 Star food, 4 Star prices.

The only nice thing about this restaurant were the decorations. Even the bathroom was decorated ornately. That's where it ends. This place serves mediocre food. It even applies to their selection of toilet tissue in the men's room.  How are you going to have a bath room is decorated so nicely and then use the bottom of the barrel cheapest toilet paper? All of that aside I was severely disappointed with their quality of food as compared to their prices. I ordered a quesadilla appetizer and it was just one regular size tortilla cut into four pieces. That wouldn't be so bad except for the fact that it was not even that tasty. And for a product that comes out with a maximum rating of "not even that tasty" how can they with good conscience charge $12. If I were the Hilton Hotel I would really hate having this place attached to my establishment. They're just taking advantage of the fact that you have so many people spending time at this Discovery Green and they invite their family to eat at this place since it's so close. The most expensive thing on the menu was a shrimp and beef dish that costs about $42 at the time of this review.  I thought that since it was almost $50 it's certainly must taste very good.  It wasn't.  It was just OK. Again I was so disappointed at the quantity and quality of food served. So many times throughout the evening I was remembering or thinking of all the throwdown taquerias or  hole in the wall restaurants in Pasadena  (The Ranchito on Preston for example) that outclass this establishment in every way except for the decor.  The waitress was kinda rude and not very professional.  I don't think she even realized it.  That's a leadership failure on their waitstaff management.  Aside from that, there were an abundance of children here which I supposed to be expected from the fact that its next to a park. So, this may be a great place for families and I would assume the kids here think the food is great.  I believe part of my disappointment with this place was because from the decor I thought I was walking into a nice restaurant. You really need to lower your expectations when coming in here. I suppose if you are a high school or middle school student with a cash allowance and you wanted to impress some friends on a day out for fun this might hit the spot perfectly. Otherwise, go eat better food somewhere else.

So much to see and do here.  The anchor store after which this plaza was named moved out a few years ago.  Great Wall Supermarket took over and has helped revitalize the plaza.

There's a place for everything under the sun here:  dental care, eye care, medical care, legal services, water systems, dance classes, karaoke, boba tea, desserts and ice cream treats, massages, hot pot, Chinese/Japanese/Korean/Malaysian/Taiwanese food, bakeries, gift shops, smoothies, karaoke, etc etc.

Parking lot is packed on weekends and the evenings.  There's a parkage garage for the overflow.  Bring your walking shoes and appetite to explore the many eateries.

name: Sandy Soul
text: The breakfast here is superb! By far the best hotel breakfast buffet you may ever find! There are some Stranger Things though, paying for parking, not nice at all! Also restrictive hours for the jacuzzi & pool, not very nice, & the drapes on the windows inside your rooms do not close!!! They have a thin see through one that closes all the way but light goes right through it , but the ones that would give you actual darkness if you wanted or needed it are stuck in an open position & apparently they are not meant to ever close for some wierd reason. So NO sleeping in here people & NO daytime naps either! oK! One troubling part of my experience was that the security guards there will look at you like they actually want to kill you for some reason, I thought I was behaving well but they just may not have liked my face when I smiled at them, Also another Stranger Thing about this hotel is that they dont show you on  advertisements that its rather spooky there.. This is where "Grandma" comes in I went out to the jacuzzi when it opened early in the morning (5:30 AM) & It felt like I was reliving  a scene out of national lampoons Family Vacation when I saw what could only be described as "Grandma" please refer to the pics below, as soon as I noticed this damn thing just sitting there disturbingly out of place like a horror film, I was outty 5000! Walking back to my room with chills up my spine.. Why something like this is pool side I will never know, Nowhere close to Halloween either, but its truly disturbing as all get out when your all alone at night & you notice that damned thing just sitting there & you cant stop staring at it wondering if "Grandma" is underneath there. I didnt feel that words could explain how frightening this appears to the viewer, thanks to my cellphone there are actual pictures of "Grandma" check em out! I hope it wasnt an apparition! if so heres some evidence of the paranormal for you...

resp.text:
Thank you for taking the time to share feedback. We are disappointed to learn that we did not exceed your expectations. We will follow up on the areas where we fell short and will take corrective action.
We are deeply sorry. Please forgive us. We hope that you will give us another try in the future. Have a wonderful week.
Yours in Hospitality,
Schwanna

name: Michelle Wong
text:
Looks fairly nice and the AC works great.

The rooms smell like cat urine. Many different rooms, multiple people's opinions, and on different visits it always smells like cat urine. The windows unfortunately don't open to get that smell out, and it doesn't leave at all during even a 4 night stay. They don't always tell you that the parking passes are $20/night when they give you one. We had to go back up and ask because someone else was told when checking in. The lazy was condescending and rude and said "well yeah you were charged to your account, it says the cost on the pass."
This wouldn't have been a problem if they had disclosed this information before charging for it.

The TV's are bolted to the wall, so if you're trying to use a Roku or HDMI port for anything else, its extremely difficult and only possible if you have tiny hands/arms.

They do not have complementary breakfast. It's about $15, but the food is decent.

I would recommend getting a room away from the side close to the strip club. The music is loud and they have Woo girls swimming in the pool until around 4am and you can hear it pretty clearly thru he walls..

name: Cierrah Washington
text:
I was suprised by being nominated as the guest of honor. Upon check in I got my choice of drink and snack (if you know me, that's the way to my heart) and free breakfast.

But THAT is not the reason for my 5 star review. This hotel is AMAZING. Cheapest in the area when comparing like hotels. You do have to pay for parking ($19 per night) but its covered parking in a well lit garage adjacent to the hotel so it's easy to get to/from. We were able to park close to the elevator each time and it was easy to get in and out plus it doesnt pack us like sardines so it was worth the money. The entire bed set up was perfect. Different pillow options, soft and warm comforter, and medium firm mattress (if you like plush it's great and even if you like firm it's great too! - me and my BFF both loved it!). The shower had good pressure but the water didnt really get that hot. It was about 10pm so I'm not sure if everyone is using the water then or what? But we tried again at 8am and again it took so long we just skipped taking our showers. The soap provided was a bit drying to the skin. May want to bring your own from home. Within walking distance to The Galleria and many other restaurants. It's easy to get on and off the premise and the decor both inside and out is beautiful. It was very quiet at all time. Both the hotel staff and fellow customers were friendly and helpful. My favorite bonus, EVERYTHING IS CLEAN.....ALL THE TIME.

The breakfast is worth the $15. Its hotel breakfast - ON STERIODS. They have eggs....but offer you salsa (real, quality, salsa verde) and shredded cheddar cheese. Waffles....but offer granola, cranberries (2 kinds), whipped cream, caramel, chocolate, etc. Yogurt...but also cottage cheese plus all the toppings!! All the toppings and stuff is great but the real important part....IT ALL TASTED AMAZING!!

Bri (spelling?) at the front desk made sure our stay was perfect. I travel a lot for work and she was one of the best "faces of the hotel" that could be at the front desk.

When in Houston, come here!! You wont regret it!

name: David Helwig
text: I have stayed here many time for work since my company's headquarters is down the street. It's a nice, clean spot. Very decent breakfast buffet with the option for fresh omelets. I would avoid the Texas shaped waffle since they doesn't seem to cook evenly. The staff has always been polite and helpful, even when I was there during Houston flooding last spring and also the time one of the rubber pads from my earbuds got stuck in my ear. Do try to avoid rooms facing the adjacent parking structure, the rooms do not have fully opaque curtains that close all the way and the structure's lights are very bright. The bathrooms also lack exhaust fans, which is strange and seems like a mold risk. All the rooms have mini refrigerators with a freezer compartment and a Krurig machine with a handful of free pods each day. There are laundry machines on site, complimentary Wall Street Journals in the lobby, an acceptable fitness room. I have never used the pool. There is a gentleman's club next door which I have not been to, a pharmacy a block away. If you need to do business in the Galleria area, it is a short walk or Uber ride from where you woulf need to go.

text:
Nice stuff,  great taste , usually I don't give a 5 star , my 5 star here because its a first time I found  a company do and keep its promise relevant to the survey after sale ! I'm mean here the receipt. I will note explain more here ,just i encourage you to follow. The instruction in your receipt 🙂  and enjoy. name: Christopher W. Morris
text: Small donut shop with famously delicious donuts. The building is easily recognizable and very simple. They have a donut "conveyor belt" that is behind the counter and seen through glass walls and is quite interesting to see. They also have coffee, and a few other drink options. The employee that helped us was incredibly friendly and helpful. This place isn't much on extras, but is a great spot to pick up delicious donuts to-go or grab a quick bite in. We opted for the simple glazed donut and a coffee to take with us on the road. Next time we visit, I think were going to give the filled donuts a try. If you're into sweet breakfast treats, give them a shot, you're sure to like what you try.

name: Nicole Vargas
text: Service was low/average but it was so disappointing that the donuts were cold! We also didn’t get the full amount of donuts we paid for. I was disappointed with the quality of service at this location but I was craving donuts and the taste was good. Certainly not the best donuts I’ve ever eaten but at least taste-wise it was satisfying.

name: Alex Jimenez

text:
Floor slippery when the weather is wet outside. No one on the inside greets customer(s) and signs in display case is not what the donut(s) represented.

Coffee is always hot and delicious.

Went through drive through and were told they had no other options other than glaze. There is a reason nobody goes to krispy kreme in Texas. So many better options, don't waste your time.

text:
Tried to go to Krispy Kreme this morning (Sunday 4/19/2020 8:30 a.m.).. Fail.

No Answer. As usual.. NEVER answer their phones.. EVER
I went anyway.
4 people in line.  Took 20 minutes to get to the window.
No hot donuts. Ordered anyway.
Get to the window -
One person working. Wearing purple gloves.
Touching ALL MONEY and CARDS and boxes and food, etc.
- and then using those SAME gloved hands to touch EVERY SINGLE DONUT.  One at a time, loaded into my box...
I watched that one person serve all 4 people ahead of me and then looked inside the window and observed him touch each and every donut in my order.
I said nothing.. Did not pay and drove off.

They didn't do anything during time they asked.  I will take my business elsewhere and will keep telling friends and family to do the same.  My birthday is on valentine's day and I am not going to have my heart shaped donuts.  This place needs better management or should go out of business.

name: Sydney B

The staff here are always pleasant, no matter how busy they may be. I have had no issues redeeming member offers. Today, I redeemed 2 Dozen for $12 (2 dozen original glazed OR 1 dozen original glazed and 1 dozen assorted). Since I came quite late in the day, I wasn't expecting a large selection of specialty doughnuts. I was pleasantly surprised with what was available, and I was able to try a few newer flavors. I plan to return to this location for another order! Thank you!

P. S. I couldn't wait to have one before I arrived home. The apple fritter was amazing! I'm glad I bought 2 more.

name: tewania lewis

name: Asia Kay
text:
4.5 stars!
The place is great with delicious doughnuts to satisfy your dessert cravings! I keep constantly coming to this location because they always have their donuts hot and fresh whenever the sign is on. I never really have a bad experience with the sweets. Some of the staff to talk about how they do work a lot with no overtime pay which is kind of sad. Maybe they will do something about that to keep their employees happy and order for their service to continue to be good. I’ve been coming here for about three or four times the past few weeks. I love getting donuts for my staff as well so that they can enjoy something sweet on their break time. They have the best deals at Krispy Kreme. One of my favorites is the original glazed doughnuts hen it’s hot and ready. I also like the strawberry donut with sprinkles on top if I’m in the mood for a little extra. For those who watch their calories, one glazed donut has about 190 cal which is alright for a dessert! Some of the donuts that I have a lot of icing do you tend to get you on a sugar rush for a day such as the Strawberry filled, key lime donut, and pineapple. You can order a dozen or an assortment of different kinds. I love how Krispy Kreme is continuously having good deals and keeping their consumers happy.

name: Sarim Tirmizi
text:
I have been a long time Krispy Kerme fan so before I go on, I must clarify that my review is not about Krispy Kreme, its JUST ABOUT THIS LOCATION.

First things first, if you look at the picture I have posted here, it clearly shows the hours of operation for the location and the drive through. I have twin boys under 2 years old who start getting cranky pretty early evening but because we wanted the donuts we went here. I took the kids out of their car seats and went to the door. LOCKED. 40 mins before closing time. The 2 ladies inside completely ignoring us and when I pointed at the time sign, they just looked away. There was a young high school girl and boy inside chatting away with one of the staff members.

So here are my concerns.
1. Why is the location closed in operating hours? A 10pm close time is when you lock the doors and ask patrons to leave, not turn the lights off and leave. This means start closing procedures but dont lock doors till closing time
2. If the doors were locked, why were non staff members inside? This in many business practices could reflect as mismanagement or potential liabilities.

I would strongly advise management to fix this issue before you start losing business because of employees who are so eager to get home before the location is closed!

text: HORRIBLE experience. Virtually no donuts available on a Friday afternoon. No donuts being made. No samples. No hot donuts. No old fashions. No cream filled. No mini's. The bathroom was filthy. Trash everywhere. The "friends" of the employees hanging out inside the store was inappropriate. We were so disappointed in the product selection that we left without a purchase. There was my first visit and definately my last. I've been to Krispy Kreme's all across the US. This location is a disaster and a disgrace to the Krispy Kreme brand. CLOSE THIS LOCATION.

text:
Note this was my first time ever at a Krispy Kreme. Customer service is very poor here and the facility is not kept in shape. The last time I visited the drive thru's voice box was broken so I just went forward to the window behind another car. The car in front of me was casually having a conversation after receiving her order about God knows what. I was in no hurry so no fret. Suddenly a truck behind me came and the man didn't realize the voice box was broken so he kept yelling hello 20 times and then got mad and started revving his engine. When I finally got a chance to order I was greeted with a "whatcha want?" I was expecting an apology for the wait or at least saying something about the broken voice box. I placed my order and got it a minute later. I opened the bag and the donuts were COLD. Guess they don't serve fresh donuts at night. I heated it up when I went home and thought the hype this donut would be real. I was disappointed as the donut tasted artificial and had a weird aftertaste.

I do not recommend this place or the donuts. Go to Shipley's instead.

I don't eat eggs so when I checked online and found that some of their doughnuts don't have eggs, I called and emailed their company. And it checked out. They said certain doughnuts like the cinnamon glazed was eggless. So I went down there and just to confirm with the staff I asked her the same and she said "we use the same flour in all our products and the flour contains egg white". I asked her if she's sure and she was.
So I went back home and called the corporate office again. They told me the original eggless deal. They even called the store and spoke to the staff member who changed her story to say oh cake doughnuts are the ones with eggs.
I just hate going back and forth with this.. just get the story straight.

resp.text: Hi there, we understand your frustration. If you visit our menu at krispykreme.com/menu/Doughnuts, each product will have a full ingredients list for you to review.  While not all of our products contain known allergens such as peanuts, tree nuts, soy, milk, eggs and wheat, all of our products may have traces of these allergens due to processing on shared equipment and ingredient-sourcing from third-party suppliers. As some allergies can be very severe, we suggest guests with intolerances should consult with their doctor before consuming our products.

text: I hate having to leave 2 star review but I was extremely disappointed. I enjoy Regal Seafood, their other location and haven't been to the Galleria in a very long time so when we went shopping last week, we decided to grab a bite at E-Tao. The Asian gentleman next to us ordered Shrimp Fried Rice and it smelled amazing. They have an extensive pricey menu but we were excited to try their dishes. We told the waiter for starters we ordered the Shumai then we ordered Pork Fried Rice, Flat Rice Noodles with Beef, Crispy Eggplant and Lobster with Ginger and onions. We received the entrees before the Shumai. The rice tasted like it was quickly tossed and leftover as well as the Flat Rice noodles with dried beef. It tasted like it had sitting for days and quickly tossed. The eggplant was drenched in a sauce and what little crispiness was washed away in sauce. The lobster was delicious, the little that we had. My guess is it was 1 1/4 lb. barely enough for one person let alone 2. In my opinion is was Chinese Fast Food Leftovers.

text: This place is a gem inside a mall. There are essentially two types of food on the menu: Westernized Chinese & Authentic Hong Kong Style Cuisine. name: Na Li
text:
This is my second time here and since the food is very special I decided to write a review about what dishes I love.

The most memorizing dish was the deep fried poem ribs. I tried a lot of this dish in different place in houston but man their ribs are so good. First when they brought it to your table you can already smell it and It was greaaat. On the smell part I gave them 10 points, full score! And when I taste it I wonder how they can make it so crispy outside and soft inside. Highly recommended dish, and I hardly highly recommend things.

Second is their pancake, my friend loved it and that's a dish she order every time she's here, but it wasn't the way how I like my Chinese pancake.

Third is their vegetable with soft tofu. I finished most of it, veggies is fresh and tofu is super soft.

I also like their pork wrap, just a bit salty but other than that, super good!

It was a super busy day so the server might be just a little slow, but when he was with us he's super attentive.

Highly recommended place, thumbs up!

name: James Xu
text: The soup dumplings are perfect. They have juicy fillings and thin wrap. It is very difficult to achieve. Very few restaurants in the US won't mess it up, certainly none in the Chinatown. Usually the wrap of the dumplings is made either too thick like a bum or will break when picked up, leaking out all the precious juice you paid for. I will give five stars just for the dumplings but other dim sums in e-Tao are also seriously good. I would recommend it to anyone who loves dim sum.

text: I always get Oolong Green hot tea and the Dim Sum Sampler. Everyone else's food always looks delicious as well. It's a narrow hole-in-the-wall inside of a huge mall, but is definitely a good place for a unique dining experience.

text:
Overall a fine hole in the wall restaurant! A d that's what it is a hole in the wall near this outcropping of eateries.

The food is cooked wonderfully and fresh in the back, you can hear them behind you cooking it fresh!

The service is amazing compared to the other Galleria eateries who simply want you to pay and move along so they can serve the next customer.

The atmosphere slows you down from the hussel and bustle right outside the door!

We drove 45 mins just for this food, it's worth it every time we come!

These are generously filled, even the soup dumplings are larger than I'm used to. The prices seem a little high, but the portions are large.

However their sticky rice is just so outstanding and everything tasted freshly handmade. I wasn't too much of a fan of the green onion pancake, the texture was a bit gritty although the flavor was solid. I wished the menu had some more expansive dim sum things, like fried tarot. The shumai was pleasant, the pork dumplings were alright but had a lot of chives in them, the rice was “terrible”, and everything else was disappointing. The soupy dumplings were soupy but the soup was plain and tasted a little off, and the meat was also pretty flavorless.

The restaurant itself was a bit dirty with bits of rice and spilled sauce on some cleaned tables and napkins underneath another tables pedestal.

So other than the shumai (which was good) we felt let down and aren’t sure what others are raving about.

name: Stephanie Liang Hsu
text:
If we're talking about food alone, four stars.

I haven't ventured out too much, but I've had most of the dimsum dishes and they've all been generous portion sizes (they should be for the price).  The Siu Mai and Har Gow (dim sum musts) are both tasty.  The Szechuan Dumplings were not exactly what I was expecting.  When it says with peanut sauce, I thought it would be on the side, instead they're in a bowl, kind of immersed in the sauce.

The soup dumplings here were sooo good!  An order came out and the owner didn't think they looked puffy enough (not enough soup) and gave us a new order without us even asking (really good service!).

The Beef Flat Noodle was pretty good, not as oily as some places in Chinatown, but more expensive.  The Black Pepper Sauce in Sizzling Plate with beef was pretty unimpressive.  The beef was a bit chewy.  No good.

Lastly, the Scallioin Pancake.  I love this stuff, I grew up with my grandmother making this and it's one of my favorite things to eat.  The ones at E-Tao are actually pretty good, but they are SO FREAKING EXPENSIVE.  So besides that, it would be a winner.

Overall very good.  More expensive than Chinatown, but the real estate costs more.  It also might be a bit more delicious.

Thank you for your understanding with our return policy.

text:
I am too through with Guitar Center! So picture this, A few minutes ago I phoned my local Houston, TX Guitar Center located at 8390 Westheimer Rd. An associate, Hillary answered the call. I explained that I needed to return a Williams Legato III piano that I purchased because I decided to upgrade and get the next level of the same product which included some extras that did not come with the first order. I asked if it was ok if I brought it back to her location. Her response was and what do you need from me, in a tone, as if to say, and why are you wasting my time. I called an Uber and headed up here. I’m upset because I’m sitting infront of this store sweating I  the Houston heat and they don’t open and no one will come take this piano that i have packed up here to return. It makes no sense that the door can’t be opened so that they can take this piano back so that my new order can be processed and I can be shipped my new piano. I understand that COVID is affecting hours of operation at many businesses but if associates are going to answer the phone before business hours they could at least let customers know the hours of operation. Or here’s an idea: have a recording that states important information like this prior to your rude associates answering the phone. My Uber is here, I can’t deal with the heat anymore. On my way home to take a shower and put on new clothes because the ones I have on now are soaked with sweat. Thanks a lot Guitar Center and Hillary for your attitude and starting my day with another problem now I have to come back up there to handle. Out of uber money, gotta change clothes, and I’m hot and bothered. I think I might just get a refund and buy my piano somewhere else, where customer service is important.
Hot&Bothered!
Ugh!
Clairence C.

resp.text: Clairence, Thank you for bringing this to our attention.  I apologize for the inconvenience and the poor service you experienced at the Houston, TX store. I can assure you, this isn't how we normally operate.  We will reach out to the stores management team about this to make sure this doesn't happen again.  Please forward your complaint to yourvoice@guitarcenter.com and we will see that you are properly taken care of. Thanks!

name: J M
text:
UPDATE. It depends upon who you get to help you.

I wrote a 5-star review back in late June after working with one of the managers. During that time I dropped about $600 on gear and I picked up a backup microphone cable for a particular gig. I didn't use that cable and left it in its original packing. I decided the next time I was in the store I'd just exchange it for one with a switch on the end of the cable anyway. The store isn't close but I was fairly sure they told me the return window was 45 days.

So I go in with a brand new cable, and they won't take it back because supposedly it's a 30 day return window. This is not the BS where people bring in stuff they've clearly used and are essentially renting for free. This item was unused and ready to go back on the shelf. I was keeping the rest of my initial purchase.

So I left. Sadly everything I purchased from them I could have gotten from Amazon. And while Amazon has a 30-day return window I could do a return from my house / office and not wait until the next time I drive 45 minutes in to this part of town.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
Good selection and even better knowledge and service.

I can't speak for all the employees here but I can say that one of the managers, Elliot, is an audio engineer and great for providing guidance in making sure you get the right equipment for your job. Guitar Center really needs to keep and attract more employees like him.

I tried to use the Guitar Center Katy location but couldn't get past the millennial "don't care" attitude.

name: Rob Tipton
text:
I used to deal with many Guitar Centers around the country while I was stationed in Alaska. Besides buying new gear and accessories from the warehouse, I would buy used guitars from various stores.
when I retired and moved to Houston, I had a choice of stores. This is not the closest to me, but I will ONLY shop this location!  When the Orange Micro Crush was on sale a year ago, I called around and this store had a few left. I was talking with Nessa in guitats, so she held one for me.  When I went down to pick it up, I remembered that I needed to find a strap for the 1980 Ibanez PS10 I just scored. Nessa helped me look and found a strap DEAD-ON the one Paul Stanley used to have on his!!!  Nessa and I were having so much fun "shopping," that I decided I needed another overdrive pedal.  The 20 or 30 I had weren't enough and I needed something I didn't have. She sold me on the Fulltone OCD.  She was right--awesome OD.
That experience was so great, I called her manager the next day as well as GC corporate!  I've been there a few times, and ALWAYS call first to see if Nessa is working.
I love having a great store to visit, but it's even better having a "guitar girl" to myself while shopping.

name: Herson Eliseo David Gonzalez De Leon
Mudasser Zaheer
text:
Gorilla Go Go Curry is a Japanese curry place that offers all kinds of meats and multiple curry options.  There is something for vegetarians and also halal eaters who can get the fish with vegetable curry.  The food is great!

Please like this review and follow me for more honest and unbiased reviews.

name: Adam Schmitt
text:
Not a bad spot for a quick bite.

Food is readied quickly and the prices are about common. The food isn’t bad and the menu offerings are fairly minimal.
However, the food lacks anything special or overly tasty.

With so many good food options in the area, I doubt I’ll be back too often. 3.5.

name: Noel B
text: This place is small, but has a great atmosphere. I really did like the decor, but the curry was just "alright" in terms of flavor. It seems like it's made from a concentrate and they've just added water. The pork cutlet was thin and a little dry. Overall, it's okay. I feel like if they changed a few things, they could be great. Also, a thicker cut of meat and timed cook would prevent a dry product. I may stop by in the future to see if anything has changed. (Edit: Returned and had the same meal and the curry tasted better this time around. Increasing the review to 4 stars)

name: Gregston Chu
text:
The curry and the katsu are pretty good. The portion sizes are good for the price. The staff was friendly and the service was fast. The venue is bright and casual. The water cups are oddly tiny and kind of annoying.

The World Champion Curry is a giant plate that can feed a family of four.

As with all the other shops and restaurants in this plaza, the parking is always a challenge.

name: Metrotren
text: It's a nice little place with great tasting curry. The plates can be a bit expensive with a group, but the food is worth the tasty and hearty value. I only took a star off for the seats being uncomfortable if you have are wide bodied or with wide hips. Other than that the great food makes up for that.

name: Xiao Chen
text: They changed their recipe/chef... They were never as good as their NYC location but was still good. However I just ordered food today and the curry is watered down, barely any flavor. And their katsu is so flat and thin, you thought you were only eating breading. The katsu piece itself is also much smaller in size than before. If you are going to reduce all your ingredients, reduce the price too.

resp.text: Xiao, thank you for bringing this to our attention. As the quality of our food is essential to providing customers with the best possible experience at Go! Go! Curry!, we take it very seriously. Please provide us with more details about your visit at houston1@gogocurryamerica.com - the date/time, and the product ordered. We will check in with our staff in order to assure quality control, and hopefully resolve this issue with you. We hope you’ll give us another try.

name: Ham String
text: Solid Japanese Curry. Its location is great, the restaurant was clean and not crowded. Very polite service. Restroom was clean, water is self serve. Overall not bad. I would return.

name: Greg Degeyter
text: Quaint business. Nice workers. Good food.

resp.text: Thank you for your support, Greg! We’re happy to serve you. Stay genki!

name: Ada
text: I LOVED IT! They are not really busy when I went there with my friends and the place looks hella nice. Their pricing is worth it and if you don’t eat that much, you can also ask for the size :) I recommend getting this Chicken Tonkatsu.

name: Maria R
text: Fast food style Japanese curry spot. Unfortunately the service was kinda slow, this weekend was their grand opening and so I’m guessing the staff is still training, hopefully they’ll get better. The portions are good, but the menu is a bit confusing with the prices. We thought M katsu was $6.95 but I guess that’s before adding all the fixings, so a M katsu is actually $9.55. The curry is a bit too salty for my taste, but the flavor is pretty good.

name: j.m. slade
text:
Casual, relaxed place serving Kanazawa-style curry over Koshihikari rice, or udon noodles, and a side of thinly shredded cabbage, all topped with shrimp, pork, chicken, or fish Katsu.
Sausage, vegetable, tofu, gyoza, natto, boiled egg, cheese, corn, rakkyo, fukujinzuke also available.
Excellent service, from friendly and accommodating staff.
Prices and portions are reasonable.

name: Alice Chiu
text: Taste just like the one I had in New York. It's delicious. They are soft opening now so be prepared they're still training.

name: Aj Flores
text: Ok Go Go Curry is delicious!! Full of deliciousness it's hard to order just one thing. The service was great! They were very attentive and responded quickly when approached. The food was sooo good! I had to get one more to go!!

name: naomi garcia
text: This place is a God send because I have never tried curry before and when I watch anime or Japanese dramas, they'll have curry and I was always obsessed with how they made it looked so good. Now that I have tasted it, it is the best I've ever had, I hope this place does not shut down because I would be very sad.  You get your money's worth on the food. I always order the port katsu with a shrimp tempura, sausage, and boiled egg.  Also shut out to the server/cashier that was working today she is good and I hope that you continue your service there thank you!!! 07/17/2020

resp.text: Naomi, thank you so much for your feedback! We are honored when we exceed our customer's expectations. Hope to see you soon, and stay genki!

name: Kelly Eats
text:
What a great meal of Japanese curry. I highly recommend getting the signature dish Katsu (pork or chicken). The portion is pretty big for one person in my opinion.
The katsu was still very crunchy when I got it, the pork meat is soft and very juicy! It is great they were able to keep it juicy inside , not dry like other places.
The rice is special here it’s a particular Japanese rice starts with a K I can’t recall the name.
I find the add ons a little bit too expensive so you would rather get the Home Run and it already has everything on it. Definitely get extra cabbage though cuz it’s FREE!
Highly recommend this place!

name: Mandy Holverson
text: I like gogo curry, but, keep in mind it's kind of Japanese fast food. You do get very large portions of rice and curry. The curry was flavorful, if not a little salty. I really enjoyed my fried shrimp. The shrimps were giant, and cooked perfectly! My husband said his fried dumpling was good, but nothing special. I liked how thinly the cabbage was sliced, but I wish there was a dressing of some kind like they have at Katsu Bar. Something tangy and zippy would really cut the rich heaviness of the curry.

name: Charles Holtsclaw
text: They don't read instructions. "Curry on the side," isn't terribly difficult to understand. My order gets here and it's soaked in curry. Because of the distance from the restaurant, I knew it would take Ubereats awhile to get here.. hence the instructions. Now I have soggy food, a kid (picky eater) that won't touch it, and a waste of time / money.

name: C. Sheppy
text: Nice portions for the price and freshly made. Not the BEST Japanese curry I have ever had but pretty good! Good for a quick bite.

name: Brandon Parker
text: The food was good. But there was nothing very special about it. I wanted to love it because it's a cool concept. It would be good option for a takeout meal for me.

name: Vryaer
text:
I really like their vegetarian curry(they told me its actually vegan) and tofu katsu. The vegetable tempura is also good.

Downside is that it's a bit costly although the food quality is good and filling.

name: Sergio DLV
text:
Great Curry,

Came expecting a stronger curry, but I found out it is not as storng as traditional curry. The Katsu to rice portion was good. I can see how this can get expensive with additional side items. But just sticking to the katsu, rice, and curry. Its not bad.

name: danny morse
text: it took 45mins to get the food. The rice was mushy and overall meal was underwhelming. I had high hopes but was sadly dissapointed

name: A Deleski
text: Delicious japanese curry in Dun Huang plaza! Is still open but to-go only as of recent mandates affecting the entire city.

name: Chenbing Dai
text: This place has the best rice in the entire Chinatown, curry is great but rather a rural Japanese style (Kanazawa), so it’s not similar like other Japanese curry places from other part of Japan. Despite the lack of spicy and rice omelette choices, this is still by far the best place for Japanese curry in H-Town

name: Aliyah Martin
text: The curry here is so so good!! My boyfriend and I would come here sometimes after I leave work. I once ordered the World Champ Curry and it was soo good! You literally get a little bit of everything from the menu into a bowl! I also buy the Calpico drink that is sold there to complete my order. I’ve tried other curry that is sold elsewhere, but has yet to find a shop to contest the curry that is sold at Go! Go! Curry.

name: Bo Gonzales
text: Delicious, satisfying, and filling meal. I recommend the medium pork katsu for your first meal.

name: Wie G
text: Nice atmosphere and great food

resp.text: Thank you, Wie. We are happy to serve you! Stay genki and see you again soon.

name: Kenneth
text: A Japanese eatery with a casual atmosphere. Akin to a sit down fast food, the curry was solid and delicious but nothing unique and stand out. Would recommend as a quick bite to eat.

name: Thanh Tran
text: I feel a little sad giving this place only two stars because it would be nice to have a go-to place in Houston that serves Japanese curry. I've had curry several times in Japan and Japanese curry, specifically, is a staple on my home menu (once a month). I make it both from the curry packets and sometimes from scratch when I have time. The curry here is so-so; I don't think it is that flavorful. I wonder if they use actual vegetables to make the stock or do they just mix water with a powder or instant curry blocks (you can get this from the Great Wall market next door). When I ordered a larger size I got more rice instead of more curry. The rice was also a little firm/dry, not soft and sticky. I am looking at all the recent images, and I see that they have gotten smarter and put the curry separate from the rice. They should have thought of that when I ordered the food. It was weird that they put the curry next to the rice where the rice absorbed much of the curry. I though it was a little overpriced for what it is. I would recommend it for those who have never had Japanese curry, but wouldn't recommend it for those who have had the real thing.

name: ruendy zapeta
text: In my experience the food was amazing,  a bit expensive but good food, great customer service,

name: Ling Watson
text:
Mediocre Japanese curry

I was super excited about this store opening. I love Japanese curry especially the spicy one. This is bit of an disappointment as the curry sauce is thick but lacks the characteristics of Japanese curry, flavor.

The curry sauce tastes like a condensed combination of dark soy sauce with Worcestershire sauce.... that’s about best I can describe so not really exciting.
The katsu is great, crunchy and cooked perfectly. Rice is also well made.
The overall combination can use a little more cabbage.

Happy eating.

name: Vân ?
text: The employees are incredibly rude. The hours here say they close at 9:55pm. After being told the food could only be taken to-go at 9:15 pm, we received our food packaged in a to-go box and plastic bag at 9:25pm. They wouldn't even allow us to sit inside and eat our packaged food for 15 minutes, saying that they closed at 9:45pm. It's not as if they would have had to wash any extra dishes...

name: John D
text:
Go! Go! Curry is pretty great. I got the home run curry with the chicken katsu and it was delicious. The sauce wasn't at all spicy, but a soothing and feeling sauce. It's weird to put into words but the meal was kind of heavy and light at the same time? The rice, cutlet, and curry all compliment each other well.

I think it was around $16, but the drink was $3 (calpico original), so if you just use the little cups of water they have you'd save a little. I didn't think it was a bad price at all. I probably won't eat here all the time since I don't live in Chinatown but I'll certainly be coming back!

name: TSM
text: You have to get the pork here if you come. It's basically cabbage gravy and rice with sliced fried pork on top. Nothing like the traditional Indian or Thai curry you are thinking. Nothing wrong at all with the place or food but its my preference.

name: Justin Janecka
text: Curry was just a tad too acidic but overall the flavor was rich and delightful. I really enjoy all the extra options for add ins. This was a great curry place.

name: Samsky Rocket
text:
The katsu itself is pretty good. But the curry! 1 star. I can make it better from instant curry blocks..
Great location! Just lame curry.. Need improvement on this.

name: Derek Gantt
text:
I love their curry dishes, which are flavorful and satisfying, exemplifying the best of Japanese-style curry.  Since I lived in Japan in the past, I enjoy watching the videos that play in a loop in the restaurant about different Go! Go! franchises in Japan and the US.

I was a little disappointed that although I came on "Go Go Day"  (the 5th, 15th, or 25th of a month) I only received one free topping coupon, despite ordering two curry dishes; the coupon "bonus" is different in Japan.  Also, I was a little surprised to hear some pop music (maybe it sounded like Korean pop music?) playing inside; it didn't seem to match the images on the TV screen, which were Japanese programs and Go! Go! Curry! promotional videos.

I've been here a couple times and I'm glad this restaurant is in Houston.  Perhaps if they streamline the video and music content (or make it more appealing to people who don't understand Japanese?) and clarify the topping coupon policy a bit things will be even better.

name: Hitomi Gantt
text: I'm very familiar with Go Go Curry because I'm from Kanazawa where Go Go Curry originated. Their curry is dark and thick, and a little different from typical homestyle Japanese curry. The food at this location was pretty good; it reminded me of my hometown.

Ok so I used to go to Cafe 101 just for their curry tbh,but ever since they reduce the portion and increase the price like a mad lad I don't feel like it's really worth it anymore... but when gogocurry came to Houston. This is one of my new Togo curry place for a "Japanese" curry... The price is worth it. It taste good, it look good, the service was good, and it's a nice "big" portion.

text:
Good curry! It tastes like the stuff in japan for the same price. I guess that makes sense since they’re a Japanese chain. The sauce has denigras sauce in it which is why it’s so dark, and it still has the little spiciness. The rice is also good, which makes sense because it’s koshihikari.
It’s much better curry than ones you get at Asian food courts and stuff. If you’re looking for Japanese curry, this is the place.

name: Karen Tsang
text:
The first time I had Go Go Curry was in New York, for the price and flavor was SOOOO WORTH IT!!

The curry in New York had lots of flavor a little more of the spice taste but not the spicy feeling and not super salty.

The biggest one is call Grand Slam Curry that feeds 2 ppl was $12.50!

<3<3 This place is really famous in New York and the franchise is really amazing for it to come here to Houston. <3<3

However, Houston Texas location was a bit of a bummer, the sauce was mainly on the salty side and had a very black peppery taste, it was different from New York. Also the price is kinda confusing here (maybe its the way the menu was designed/it looks different than the one in New York), first, there is different sizes to choose from, then, you choose what you want as the main Katsu meat (price varies on meat and plate size) and you choose add ons for additional price (which is a bit high in price).

On the Side Note, Why is the Grand Slam Curry ($17.55) here in TX more expensive than New York?

text:
Its alright. Its more of 3.5 stars for me. It wasnt terrible curry. But -.5 star cause it came room temperature not hot or steamy like i would have thought. The egg in the photo wasnt like what i got; it was actually better. The photo makes the egg look overcooked. The pork cutlet is smaller than most katsu which means they likely tenderized it to expand the size for appearance. The hotdog/sausage was ok. It was like deep fried so the outer casing was crunchy. The shrimp tempura was nice til they threw on tartar sauce. It messed with the taste of the curry on the tongue. The specialty is curry so i dont think adding another sauce was a good idea. Maybe keep the tartar in a side cup or something.

Ive never been to Japan and had their curry so i cant say if its homemade or premade mixes. Judge for yourself. I had the homerun platter for $12.55 kinda high for a rice dish unless it really is scratch made, but it was enough to make me full. $3 ito en green tea is a no for me.

The taste was ok seems like you put rice then brown sause then toppings. The fish was a chopped up fish stick. The tofo topping was great.

If this was downtown or in a airport it would make sense . But on Bellaire there is so much you could get for that price.

name: David H. Nguyen
text:
If you're like me, I like to sample everything! What better way than getting the combo pre planned plate of the home run curry, it comes with either pork or chicken katsu, sausage, egg, and shrimp.  This all comes over a serving of rice covered in curry and a side of cabbage.

I opted for the pork Katsu and it was delicious! Perfectly fried, it comes with a tangy sauce on top.  The rice is tender and soaks up the curry well.  The sausage was really flavorful, the egg was plain, the shrimp tempura comes with a good sauce, and the cabbage was a perfect light addition that I was able to mix up with the rice to balance out the dish.

I'd come at an off time between lunch and dinner or wait until some of the hype dies down.  They are still working out the kinks so you've got to give them some patience.

text:
The first thing that I noted was that I really liked the ambiance! When it came to the food, it tasted fine. The pork katsu was cook well and had a great crunch to it. They didn't skimp on the curry, cabbage, or rice. What was unfortunate is that the ratio of the katsu to everything else was not good. If I took really big bites, I could have eaten the katsu in 3 bites.

Like another person had mentioned before, the menu pricing was a bit confusing at first; your order comes out to a lot more than what you might expect if you think that the prices of the meat just mean extra meat (it's not extra, that's just the base price of having the katsu). That disappointed me because you can get katsu curry elsewhere with similar quality that costs less.

I'd say to visit once and see if you're okay with the prices in relation to the quality/quantity.

text:
Quality- 4/5
Quantity-3/5
Pricing-3/5
Service-4/5
Speed-2/5
Environment-3/5

-Quality wasn't bad, was good expected as much but the curry is slightly more salty then what average people like, I prefer mine with a little more and has a lot of flavor. My only complaint is the rice is mushy Abit.
-Quantity is nowhere near where I can get anywhere for cheaper and faster. For a small measurement I  barely got any rice for the home run platter.
-pricing could be adjust cheaper from what u get. I heard this is suppose to be fast chain and go so not sure why it cost over $14(no drink) to feel like I got Abit of a decent meal,a extra gyoza or a small tempura was at least $1-$1.5
-service no real complaint nothing bad or good to experience.
-speed, ohserving around there was only 3 orders ahead of my friend and I, And the lobby was 3/5 full but already served. We waited for about 25-30min to get his dish then another 10min for mine next.  It is a sluggish pace which I hope they'll work on once they get the kinks worked out .
. environment- nothing fancy, bright yellow, aim towards a family friend environment,. Heard there was fresh paint still which I can't smell the fumes.
The soft opening of gogocurry was just this past weekend,  when anything new is open in Houston I expect a long wait due to lines., unfortunate I wouldn't be interested to try this place out again if it stays the same , there numerous places that could serve the same if not better for cheaper price without waiting as long. Was hoping for more but left slightly disappointed.

name: Whitney White
text: Cute store front. Nice presentation for the display cookies. Nice packaging with the pink boxes. I was greeted shortly after walking in. There was no wait in line. I like the variety in cookies offered. I played it safe and ordered the chocolate chip cookies. The size and thickness were great. However, the flavor was nothing special. It almost tasted like a prepackaged healthy alternative cookie. It was also dry.... maybe because we went at 9 pm? The cookie was also advertised as a “hot” cookie and the employee said the cookies were in a warmer. The cookies I received were not warm. I’ve had better cookies elsewhere. I would go back and try a specialty cookie.

resp.text: Hi Whitney! Thanks for the feedback! If you have any concerns please email us at support@crumbl.com!

name: Elaine Flores
text: 3.5 but I always go up. So today was my first Crumbl experience. Yes I'd come back which is why I didn't give 3 stars. But I guess these aren't my type of cookies. I'm conflicted- see the flavor is good and I like the lightness of them but these are half cake half sugar cookies and are a lot. (Is that really a criticism?) For me -yes. I would not recommend the chocolate chip cookie. The animal cookie was a 4/5. The churro was a 5/5 and the stawberry cheesecake on a double chocolate cookie was a 4/5. I also got their ice cream - chocolate cake. It was okay. Their service is really good and efficient they have both in person and virtual (screens on walls) ordering and it was very clean. Go check it out for yourself!

resp.text: Hi Elanie!  Thank you so much for leaving us with this amazing review! We are so glad to see that we are worth all 4 stars! Thank you again and we hope to see you again sometime soon!

text: Recently received these cookies as a gift and I was extremely delighted . Not only was the presentation beautiful the cookies taste great . The pictures posted don’t do this place justice. The cookies are perfectly round rather on the large side, they are rather thick which give the cookie a nice consistency which is extremely moist . The icing on top was aesthetically applied making the presentation beautiful.

name: Richard ward
text: I love the cookies, menu changes every Monday. Go there twice a month. The office workers love them.

name: Alexander Martinez
text: I feel so bad but my god the Chocolate chip was awful. Tasted like bread. Was looking forward to the ice cream but they only had one flavor, lemon poppyseed which I didn’t care for. I give it 2 stars cause they were friendly.

name: Luis Salazar
text: BEST COOKIES IN THE WHOLE HOUSTON AREA. I love how they are super friendly, and the cookies are freshly baked delicious and always have new flavors! Love it here!

name: Jackie Matranga
text: I have yet to find cookies that top these. Incredible marketing, concept, and best of all, FLAVORS! I love it so much I tried to franchise one about a year ago but they were all claimed for Houston already lol. If that doesn’t speak to the love I have for this place then I don’t know what does. #crumblgirl

name: Justin Ashar
text:
We're on a mission to find the best chocolate chip cookie in Houston.  We came across Crumbl Cookies in Bellaire.  It's located in a strip plaza and has plenty of private parking spots out front.  We ordered a "Single Box" for $3.48; this consisted of one large chocolate chip cookie.  We also ordered a chilled 16 oz of white milk (2%).

The cookie was quite soft, thick, and moist.  It was undercooked if you like that raw cookie style.  The chocolate chips were overly-sweet for my taste to the point it hurt my teeth.  Overall, the place was nice, but I thought the chocolate chip cookie was okay.  I personally like the chocolate chip cookies at Tout Suite or Luna Pizzeria much better in Houston.

name: Elizabeth Ashley Buck
text: The revolving door of flavor goodness is a spectacular way to keep me coming back, and checking the app like a kid checking the bottom of the cereal box for the toy.

name: Elizabeth B
text: Every time I come here I am greeted with a cheerful welcome! I love these cookies and wish I had found out about them sooner.

name: Kevin Rivera
text: The store is always organized and clean. Workers are really nice and always give a welcoming feeling. This place has easily become my favorite dessert place. Cookies are always warm. I have tried their confetti, peanut butter bar, Reese’s cup and original chocolate chip. I have yet to find one I did not like. Please come and try !!! Perfect for after dinner, sweet tooth moments or to bring to an occasion since the box is adorable.

resp.text: Thank you for the fantastic review, Kevin!  We are so grateful!

name: Diana Smith
text: Ok - do not go here! I’m warning you. You will keep going back every day. The cookies are SO amazing. The lemon is out of this world. I’m a huge chocolate chip fan, surprisingly this was not a favorite, but ya know, I didn’t turn it down! The sugar cookie is creamy and rich. Total decadence. I’m so mad at my friend for introducing me.

resp.text: We so glad you enjoyed ALL our delicious cookies! Thank you so much Diana for ordering with us!

My friends and I loved them. Also, in case you can't tell from the images, the cookies are massive (which I'm happy about 😁).

Each flavor was delicious! The Churro and Nutella Sea Salt flavors were my personal favorites, but there wasn't a bad one in the bunch.

Also, you can order using an app ahead of time to make sure cookies are freshly baked and you can get curbside delivery which is great in the time of COVID!

text: I was really disappointed, I went out of my way to go to Crumbl because I know from prior experience how good they can be. I can assure my experience was poor because of this location. Both of my cookies I got had weird white hard flecks of something in them. at first I thought it was part of the Cookie but then the more I ate it the more I realized it had been mixed or cooked wrong. I think it was big pieces of unmixed flour or shells something. Normally when I go to crumbl I scarf down everything in record time, I couldn’t even finish half the cookies because of how unpleasant it was. Weird experience, hopefully a one time problem, but felt the need to write the review because if I’m going out of my way to a crumbl it won’t be this one.

text: The 1st time I had the chicken sandwich combo it was hot and fresh along with the fries. The 2nd time I had the combo the fries were hot and fresh and the sandwich was room temperature but tolerable.

name: Suzanna Gonzales
text: Food was great, nice and hot. I gave them a 3 because the place was dirty especially the tables at a time like covid you would think they would be on their A game with wiping things down, you could totally tell someone ate at the table and it wasn't cleaned. My husband went and found a cleaning cloth and the spray they had out and cleaned it himself. There weren't very many tables in the restaurant alot of them had signs that you couldn't sit there it seemed almost all of them.

name: David Christopher
text: I don't eat meat so I can't tell y'all about the entrees, but I can let you know about the desserts. I had the peach mango pie and an ube pie. Both were delicious and it was the first time I'd ever been to jollibee. I found out about jollibee from Filipino classmates. They say the spaghetti and fried chicken is awesome!

name: Marissa Briones
text: Glad there’s a Jollibee in Missouri City (we used to go to the one in downtown Houston). It’s a newly-opened store (soft opening was June 7, 2020). The service was friendly. The food was delicious. The place is clean and nice (and brand new - the tables and chairs have never been used since they had a soft opening due to COVID-19). They have deals and combo meals available. They have a drive-thru service and delivery via DoorDash is available. The store is easily seen from the street (Hwy. 6).

name: Emma Blahblahblah
text: Some of the best fried chicken, not just by fast food standard. It's even better than some restaurants'. Spicy and juicy. Their deluxe chicken sandwich is amazing too. Too bad they don't have a spicy chicken sandwich. Fries are seasoned well. Mashed potatoes are so creamy.

name: Dennis Castro
text:
Haven't had Jollibee in forever. I'm glad I had stopped by(multiple times) It is how I remember it. But, it's time to upgrade the menu! Add more choices of hometown fave dishes!. And Please add more sizes for your Drinks!!!! 😁
Good place for quick grub. would have given 5 ☆'s, There is room for improvement!.
I will revisit this review when I see some changes. I'm sure other customers will agree. ✌

name: Jay Are
text: Grateful that there is now another location and much closer to home! Great tasting chicken. Awesome peach mango pies. Spaghetti is a must!

name: alhenry
text: Really good. Not the same Jollibee like back home in the Philippines but it's ok, quality chicken for sure.

name: Tower of Vape
text: I really enjoy the food here. The fried chicken, the Palabok (a noodle dish) and Filipino-styled spaghetti are worth the trip. Their breakfast of Tocino (a breakfast meat made out of pork) with rice is so tasty!

name: Vanessa M
text: Chicken is pretty good but it's expensive. Plus, they make you buy the chicken as part of a meal instead of letting you get it by itself like similar fast food places. Paying over $9 on average is way too much for a fast food fried chicken place.

name: Kris
text: Chicken was ok. No white meat. Mashed potatoes were nice and hot. Gravy sauce tasted really good. Popeye's chicken tastes way better.

name: Antonio Rodriguez
text: Good food and their pineapple drink is amazing

name: Gina Garcia
text: Great service , food was amazing! Chicken and spaghetti was off the chain! Loved it

name: Efrain Gonzalez
text: I tried Jollibee for the 1st time and was very disappointed.  The chicken is good, but not as good as Popeyes or Golden Chick.  The spaghetti is flavorless other than being sweet.  The Pabolok is okay.  The peach mango pie was just okay.  There was no excitement in the food.  I will not be going back.  And way too expensive!!!

name: Philippe S
text: I love Jollibee!!! Even if they forgot to put my 5 peach mango pies along with my Bucket D order, I still love Jollibee. It would help a lot of the crew smiles more. 😊

name: Tim Ewest
text: I atebAsian inspired fare in China.  I traveled in China for 10 years.  Jollibee is missing the quality, and it is sad. Normally Asain fast food is cheap, tastey and fresh.

name: Shiela Baltazar
text: Loveeee Jollibee! So glad they opened one near our place. Whenever we crave for the chickenjoy we just drive for a few minutes and where there. Always crispy and juicy! Plus the employees are amazing!

name: Jeff Franklin
text: 7 minutes to make chicken sandwich,  left, pretty sure kid working drive through flipped me off. Like all other restaurants that move here this place will not survive either.

Side note, the chicken sandwich is better than the competition.

name: J D
text: The drive thru menu only showed bone-in chicken meals, but they actually have chicken strips, a chicken sandwich, and other items you have to ask for. That made it very confusing to order considering it was our 1st time visiting & not knowing what all is on the menu. The drive thru attendant was nice, but gave us fries & a pie and told us to park in the drive thru waiting space. The fries were not fresh & hot, which meant they would be cold whenever I got my entree delivered to the car. Instead of waiting we went in to request fresh hot food. There was a language barrier which made it very uncomfortable to communicate...trying to ensure the order request was understood, but not trying to be rude so they won't mistreat my food. We got our food fresh and hot eventually, but this establishment is not worth a second chance.

The fried chicken is definitely comparable to Popeyes and hits the spot.  Pie was my favorite part of the experience!❤️❤️

name: Justine Yates
text:
Where to begin..
My husband had been looking for a new jeep compass and we had found our own financing, so we didn't have to deal with that on arrival.
We get a sales rep (didn't make a prior appt) within 30 seconds of walking in the door. He had been with the company for years but at this particular location training. He helped us find the car that my husband wanted. The process was fairly quick (probably because we were prepared with our own financing), maybe an hour total.
It took half an hour for the car to be brought out to us from being cleaned after we signed the paperwork. So a total of about an hour and a half start to finish with driving off the lot.

Now the "issues"
We were given only two standard keys, although the jeep should have come with a key fob for remote lock/unlock. Well, the manual said that the car security system would not active unless we had the key fob. So, we called the dealership and they told us to speak with the automotive dept.
The receptionist that answers the phones for them told us that she would look into it and call us back (my husband called at 1PM). The lady never called back, so I call back the next day. She informs me that we will have to just buy it from them and she will call the key dealer to estimate a price for me. She eventually calls me back and says $100 and sets up an appt time, over a week away. In the mean time I spoke with the sales manager to inquire about this because why am I paying for something that the car should have come with but didn't? He informs me that yes the fob should have come with it that they guarantee one fob if the car is equipped for it. He says he will inform the lady so there won't be issues when we go get the key.
Appt to get the key arrives and she tries having us pay for the key, saying that no we don't get a free key. We have to tell her that she was informed of this and we had emails from the sales manager to back this up.. we did end up NOT having to pay for the fob though.
Basically sales was great! Automotive receptionist not so much. No call back and uninformed of their policies, not to mention her poor attitude.
